See [tests/retrieve_output_filters.test.ts](tests/retrieve_output_filters.test.ts), [tests/compress_text_token_accounting.test.ts](tests/compress_text_token_accounting.test.ts), [tests/content_store.test.ts](tests/content_store.test.ts), [tests/handoff_resolve_flag_suggestion.test.ts](tests/handoff_resolve_flag_suggestion.test.ts), [tests/install_vscode.test.ts](tests/install_vscode.test.ts).
- **A newly registered CLI command can no longer silently skip the routing gate.** `buildGuidanceBody` in [src/bridges/guidance_block.ts](src/bridges/guidance_block.ts) is the only description of token-goat a model gets unprompted -- it becomes the routing gate written into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and the installed SKILL.md. Three real bugs shipped from the same root cause: a command existed and worked, but nobody updated this prose, so an agent never learned it existed and fell back to a full-file read. A new guard test derives the live command list from the same CLI registry [tests/registry.ts](tests/registry.ts) already used elsewhere and fails if any registered command is neither named in the gate's `Commands:` line nor listed in an explicit, reasoned omission set (operator/lifecycle, session/cache introspection, derived analysis, single-format extractor, write/mutation, or read-adjacent navigation utility). Auditing against it found `brief` and `mcp-output` genuinely missing -- both now named in the gate alongside their existing siblings (`read`, `bash-output`/`web-output`). See [tests/guards/guidance_body_command_coverage.test.ts](tests/guards/guidance_body_command_coverage.test.ts).
- **Relative-spec resolution is now pinned against the machine-wide index.** `global.db` indexes every project ever seen, keyed by absolute path, so two unrelated projects can each hold `src/thing.ts::sharedName`. Nothing asserted that a bare relative spec picks the current project's copy -- the guarantee rested entirely on `resolveIndexPath` turning the relative file into an absolute key *before* the exact-equality lookup, which is the same check-then-use shape that broke repeatedly elsewhere. New tests run the identical spec from two seeded projects and require each to get its own file, and separately pin the deliberate opposite for a bare `symbol <name>`, which is a machine-wide lookup that legitimately answers from every project with each row labelled by absolute path. No behavior changed. See [tests/read_cross_project_relative_spec.test.ts](tests/read_cross_project_relative_spec.test.ts).
- **Tests now sandbox `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` on every platform, not just macOS.** `LOCALAPPDATA`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` were redirected everywhere, but `HOME` only on darwin -- so any code path calling `os.homedir()` directly (waste's transcript fallback to `~/.claude/projects`, bootstrap-audit, the bridge installers, context-stats' CLAUDE.md walk) escaped the sandbox entirely on Windows and Linux. That gap caused a real intermittent failure rather than a theoretical one; sandboxing `HOME` everywhere closes the class. See [tests/setup/isolate-home.ts](tests/setup/isolate-home.ts).

## [2.6.27] - 2026-08-10

### Added
- **`changed` now takes `--exclude-tests` to drop test files from the diff.** The last member of the `refs`/`callers`/`dead`/`call-chain`/`impact`/`semantic`/`symbol` family that lacked it. `--grep` can only ever *select* a path, so there was no reliable way to ask for the non-test half of a diff: the negative-lookahead regex that expresses "not a test" silently degrades to a literal substring match whenever the regex-compile fallback fires. Test files are a large share of a real diff -- measured against this repo, 35-54% of changed files across the last 5, 10 and 20 commits. Filters the file path, so like `--grep` it applies in `--symbol` mode too, and it prunes before the per-file index lookup rather than after, so a test file is never queried at all. Opt-in and byte-identical when omitted, and composes with `--grep` -- a file must satisfy both, with the `--grep` notice taking priority when that filter is what emptied the list. When it hides every changed file there was, the output names how many were hidden and exits 0, rather than a bare "No files changed." that would read as a clean diff. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`symbol` now takes `--exclude-tests` to drop test-file definitions.** The flag already existed on `refs`/`callers`/`dead`/`semantic` but not on `symbol`, the most-used of the set, so the noisiest lookups had no way to suppress it: against this repo's own index `symbol run` returns 18 rows of which 14 are test-file definitions, and `symbol capture` returns 9 of 9. Filters on the DEFINITION site like `dead` (not the call site, as `refs`/`callers` do), is opt-in and byte-identical when omitted, and composes with `--grep` -- a symbol must satisfy both. Applied before the `--limit` slice and over-fetching at the DB level, so a `--limit N` window that would otherwise fill with test-file rows still returns non-test matches rather than falsely reporting none. When it hides every match there was, the output names how many were hidden and exits 0, instead of the exit-1 `No matches` a genuinely unindexed name returns. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **The VS Code extension is now a full chat companion for both support staff and developers.** Non-technical users get clipboard compression (@token-goat /paste), plain-language canned prompts (summarize, draft a reply, action items, explain an error, resolved-ticket-to-KB-article, friendlier/shorter/more-formal rewrites), errors-only extraction from log files, PDF/DOCX attachment extraction into chat, zip-archive peeking without extraction, and folder-level recurring-issue analysis. Developers get selection/cursor-window/symbol-at-cursor/whole-file/git-diff sends, all compressed. Email addresses, phone numbers, ID numbers, and card numbers are scrubbed before any text reaches the chat input (token-goat.scrubPii, default on, with a one-time explanatory dialog offering an opt-out), and a status-bar counter shows a running total of bytes saved. The extension also gained the goat logo as its icon, editor title-bar and context-menu entries, an @token-goat chat participant, and a plain-language README. On Windows it now quotes CLI arguments correctly through the npm .cmd shim. See [vscode-extension/](vscode-extension/).
- **`find` now recovers a mistyped name instead of reporting nothing.** `find` was a case-insensitive substring scan over symbol names, which structurally cannot reach a typo that drops, swaps, or mistypes a character -- `getUserr` is neither a substring of `getUser` nor the reverse -- yet that is the case the docs pointed at it for when an exact `symbol` lookup misses. It now falls back to the same edit-distance ranking `Did you mean:` uses. The fallback runs only when the substring pass found nothing, so an exact match is never reordered or displaced, and a query near nothing still reports a clean miss rather than dredging up unrelated names. A recovered match says which name it actually matched instead of silently answering for a name you did not type; `--json` marks it with `fuzzy: true` and `matchedNames`, both absent on an exact hit. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`semantic` now takes `--exclude-tests` to drop test-file hits.** `--grep` can only ever *select* a path, so there was no reliable way to ask semantic search for non-test hits: the negative-lookahead regex that expresses "not a test" silently degrades to a literal substring match whenever the regex-compile fallback fires. Opt-in and byte-identical when omitted, matching `refs`/`callers`/`dead`/`call-chain`/`impact`. Filters before the `--limit` slice in both the embeddings and full-text-fallback branches (and over-fetches at the DB level in the latter, so a small `--limit` still returns a full page of non-test hits), and composes with `--grep` -- a hit must satisfy both. When it hides every hit there was, the output names how many were hidden (`--json` sets `excludeTestsFilteredToEmpty: true`) and exits 0, rather than the exit-1 "no matches" a genuinely empty search returns; with both filters emptying the view, the `--grep` notice takes priority. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`symbol` now takes `--grep <pattern>` to search project-wide by name pattern.** `symbol` was exact-match only, so "list every `run*` handler" had no answer: `skeleton`/`outline`/`exports --grep` are per-file, `types --grep` covers only type-like kinds, and `dead --grep` only zero-reference symbols. Regex, falling back to a literal substring match when the pattern is not valid regex. The positional name is now optional and mutually exclusive with `--grep` (regex-filtering an already-exact name can only match everything or nothing); giving neither errors clearly rather than dumping the index. Filters before the `--limit` slice, and names the active filter when it matches nothing in a non-empty scope. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`refs`/`callers`/`impact`/`call-chain` now distinguish "symbol not indexed" from "symbol indexed, zero results".** A typo'd or nonexistent name used to print "no references found"/"no callers found", indistinguishable from a real symbol that's genuinely unused -- which invites deleting live code. An unindexed name now reports `Symbol not found: <name>` with a `Did you mean:` suggestion when a near-name candidate is indexed; a real symbol with zero references/callers/impact keeps today's exact message unchanged. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`call-chain` and `impact` now take `--exclude-tests`.** The two commands most polluted by test callers -- both walk the caller relation transitively, so any test touching the path got dragged in. Prunes test-file callers before they're admitted to the traversal (not just from the final output), so nothing walks through a test node either; when every caller was a test, the empty-result message names the hidden count instead of reading as genuinely unreferenced. Opt-in, matching `refs`/`callers`/`dead`. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`semantic` now takes `--grep <pattern>` to narrow by file path.** The only surgical-read query command that had no path filter at all -- every sibling (`refs`, `callers`, `dead`, `skeleton`/`outline`, `exports`) already has one. Matches the pattern against the file path as rendered (an anchored `--grep "^src/"` matches what the output shows, not the stored absolute path), regex falling back to a literal substring match when the pattern is not valid regex. Applies before the `--limit` slice in both the embeddings and full-text-fallback branches, and when it filters everything out the result names the active filter (`--json` sets `grepFilteredToEmpty: true`) instead of reading like the search found nothing. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).

### Fixed
- **`changed --exclude-tests` claimed "No non-test files changed" when `--grep` was the filter that hid them.** `--grep` runs first, so `--grep '^tests/' --exclude-tests` on a diff touching both `src/` and `tests/` left only test files for `--exclude-tests` to remove, and the resulting message was true of the `--grep` slice but false of the diff -- `src/` files had plainly changed. The message now names both filters in that case. Unqualified wording is kept when `--grep` is absent, or when it discarded nothing, so the sentence is never padded with an irrelevant filter. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`changed --symbol` could report "No symbols changed." for a file whose changed symbol sat past a silent 1000-row cap.** Each file's symbol query was capped at a bare 1000, so a symbol beyond the cutoff read as absent rather than truncated -- and under `--json` the envelope said `truncated: false`, asserting nothing had been cut. Both call sites now use the same `FIND_SCAN_LIMIT` the rest of the file uses for whole-set scans. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`changed` and `refs` returned prose instead of JSON under `--json` whenever the result was empty.** Both exit 0 on those paths, so a caller got a success status with a body `JSON.parse` throws on -- the failure surfaces in the consumer, not the command. Four sites were affected in `changed` (nothing changed, nothing changed in `--symbol` mode, `--grep` matched none of the changed files, and the changed files carried no indexed symbols) and one in `refs` (`--grep` matched none of the references). They now emit the same `{items, truncated, totalCount}` envelope the populated branch does, with `totalCount` as the post-filter count; text mode keeps every human notice verbatim. `callers`/`dead`/`deps`/`types` were already correct, so this closes the residual gap in that migration. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`--exclude-tests` and `refs` no longer say "1 in test files" or "1 references".** Seventeen call sites across `refs`/`callers`/`dead`/`call-chain`/`impact`/`semantic` each interpolated the hidden-count parenthetical themselves with a hard-coded plural, and six more interpolated a bare `references` after a count, so hiding or finding exactly one row rendered `1 in test files hidden by --exclude-tests` and `1 references` -- which reads as a bug in the tool rather than a report about the store, and one row is the most common way to reach either message. Both are now shared helpers that agree with the count, and a guard test keeps the literal forms out of the command modules -- it caught two more live sites (`skeleton`/`outline`'s `1 symbols`, `refs --top`'s `1 references across 1 files`) that the first fix pass missed. Nothing caught this because every fixture in the suite exercised the plural branch, and one test pinned `1 references` as the expected output. See [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts).
- **`find`'s documented behavior now matches what it does.** The command reference described it as "unified search: exact/fuzzy symbol match + semantic, merged and ranked by confidence", and the troubleshooting table recommended it for a typo. It did none of those things: no semantic search, no confidence ranking, and no fuzzy matching (now added, above). Both entries now describe the real behavior and point at `semantic` for meaning-based search. See [README.md](README.md).


## [2.6.26] - 2026-08-09

### Added
- **`callers --json` and `dead --json` now also emit `filePath` alongside `file`.** Both fields carry the identical value this release, so existing consumers keep working unchanged while new consumers can switch to `filePath` (the spelling `types --json` already uses). `file` will be removed in a future release. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts).
- **Grep `content`-mode results now fold repeated file paths.** Matches under the same file previously repeated the full `path:lineNo:` prefix on every line; the post-hook now groups them under a single path header with indented `lineNo: text` lines beneath, losslessly (every match line and line number survives verbatim). Only applies to `output_mode: content` with no `-A`/`-B`/`-C`/`context`/`multiline`; `files_with_matches`, `count`, and context-mode results are untouched. See [src/hooks_grep.ts](src/hooks_grep.ts).
- **`hint-stats` now shows what hints cost, not just what they save.** The ledger recorded bytes saved by a hint but never the bytes the hint itself spends by being injected into context, so there was no way to tell whether hints were net-positive at all. Each category now has a `spent` column and there is a `TOTAL saved/spent/net` line. Emissions recorded before this existed show as `n/a` rather than a fake zero. See [src/hint_stats.ts](src/hint_stats.ts), [src/cli_hint_stats.ts](src/cli_hint_stats.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts).
- **`outline` and `skeleton` take `--grep <pattern>` to narrow by symbol name.** `token-goat outline src/cli.ts` lists 502 symbols across 503 lines, and there was no way to look at one area of a large file — the only options were the whole symbol list or the full-file read these commands exist to replace. `--grep` matches the pattern against the symbol name as a regex, falling back to a literal substring match when the pattern is not valid regex, the same convention every other `--grep` flag already uses. It composes with `--min-lines` rather than overriding it, applies to `--json` output as well as text, and when it filters everything out the listing says so and names the filter. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts).
- **MCP result compression now also handles object-shaped payloads.** The existing table pass only compresses a JSON array of homogeneous objects; a config dump, a single-resource response, or a nested settings tree returned `null` no matter how many `null`/`""`/`[]`/`{}` values it carried. A second pass now recursively drops those four empty shapes to a fixed point and renders the remainder as compact JSON with a `dropped N empty value(s) (null, "", [], {})` summary line, so the removal is always visible instead of reading as a server that simply didn't return the field. `0` and `false` are never dropped. Same `MIN_SAVINGS_RATIO` net-benefit gate, `MCP_COMPRESS_MIN_BYTES` size gate, and full-recovery-by-id guarantee as the table pass; the table pass still runs first and is unchanged for every shape it already handled. See [src/mcp_compress.ts](src/mcp_compress.ts).
- **`token-goat index` shows live progress instead of looking hung.** A manual run against a real repo parses and embeds every tracked file inline and can take minutes with nothing printed until the final line. On a real terminal (the same TTY/NO_COLOR/CI gate `token-goat stats` already uses, so Claude Code's own terminal — which reports no `isTTY` at all — counts as rich) it now writes a throttled progress line to stderr: files done/total, current phase (scanning/parsing/embedding), and elapsed time, cleared before the final summary. Piped or CI invocations stay completely silent, and the final `Indexed N files into the symbol index.` line on stdout is unchanged. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts).
- **Intent-based suggestions for command names that don't exist.** Commander's built-in `(Did you mean X?)` is edit distance over the registered names, which works for a typo but misfires on a conceptual miss: `token-goat search foo` suggested `arch`, the import-graph analyser, and `cat` suggested `cost`. Following either wastes a call and teaches the wrong model of the CLI. A short curated list of names you reach for when you know what you want but not what it's called — `search`, `cat`/`show`/`view`, `definition`, `usages`/`references`, `tree`/`ls`, `summarize` — now gets a line naming the commands that actually serve that intent. Commander's own diagnostic is left untouched; the hint is appended after it, and nothing is emitted for a plain typo or an unrecognised name. See [src/command_intent.ts](src/command_intent.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`pdf-meta --json`.** The whole point of `pdf-meta` is to decide, before extracting, whether a PDF is worth running `pdf-extract` on — a decision made programmatically. But the answer was a prose sentence you had to substring-match (`Text layer: no (likely scanned/image-only; ...)`), and an absent title printed as the literal `(none)`, indistinguishable from a PDF actually titled "(none)". A title or author containing a colon or newline broke the `key: value` line shape outright. `--json` emits `{ pageCount, title, author, hasTextLayer }` with `hasTextLayer` as a real boolean and missing values as `null`. Text output is unchanged. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`xlsx-sheets --json`.** Three sibling commands (`xlsx-head`, `xlsx-range`, `xlsx-query`) take a `--sheet` whose help text says "see xlsx-sheets", so this output exists to be fed straight back — but the name had to be recovered from a text line that pads its fields with two spaces. Excel allows consecutive spaces inside a sheet name, so `Q1  Draft  A1:A2  (2 rows x 1 cols)` cannot be split back into fields at all: the text form is lossy, not just awkward. `--json` emits the `{ name, ref, rows, cols }[]` the extractor already produces. Text output is unchanged. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`symbol`, `semantic`, `refs`, `types`, `callers`, `brief`, `dead`, and `call-chain` now flag an unindexed project instead of dead-ending into a plain "not found."** A zero-result query against a project with zero indexed files read exactly like a genuine miss, when the real cause was that nothing had ever been indexed. Doctor's Symbols check already diagnosed this exact condition; these commands now append the same wording (only after their own query already came back empty, so a real result or a genuine miss on an indexed project is unaffected). `semantic --json` gains `indexEmpty`/`hint` fields for this case; the other commands' text-mode messages already aren't real JSON on this path, so nothing there changes shape. See [src/index_health.ts](src/index_health.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts).
- **`logfold` folds more repetition.** It normalized timestamps, UUIDs, IPs, and hex IDs before comparing lines but had no rule for bare integers, so counters, PIDs, ports, line numbers, byte counts, and elapsed-ms values kept otherwise-identical lines from folding (`Retry 1 failed` / `Retry 2 failed` / `Retry 3 failed` stayed three separate lines). It also only folded consecutive duplicates, so the normal interleaved shape of concurrent logs and multi-worker output folded nothing at all. Bare integers now normalize to `[N]` (last in the substitution order so it never overrides the existing timestamp/UUID/IP/hex rules, and skipped when the digits are part of a longer token like `v2`, `utf8`, `x86_64`, or `sha256`). A new `--fold-repeats` flag opts into folding non-consecutive duplicates anywhere in the input, attributing the total count to the first occurrence; the default output is unchanged. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts).
- **Bash hook nudges toward `token-goat failures` right when a test run actually fails.** `failures` extracts just the failing blocks from pytest/jest/vitest/go test/cargo test output, but nothing ever pointed at it at the moment it would pay off, so it went almost unused. A failing test-runner command (including bare `npm test`, which the existing build/monitoring caches deliberately skip as too generic) now caches its output and returns a one-line hint naming the exact `token-goat bash-output <id> | token-goat failures` command to run next. Silent on a passing run, a non-test command, or output too small to be worth reducing. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), [src/hints/lang_patterns.ts](src/hints/lang_patterns.ts).
- **`token-goat recall` with no query now browses instead of erroring.** `recall` exists so you don't have to remember which cache holds a prior result — but it only worked once you already had a search term, and with no argument it was a hard "missing required argument" error. That made it useless in the one case where the index matters most: the ids have scrolled out of context, so you have nothing to search for. It now lists every cached bash-output, web-output, and mcp-output entry newest-first, in the same format and honouring the same `--type`/`--limit`/`--json` flags, instead of making you run `bash-history`, `web-history`, and `mcp-history` in turn. A whitespace-only query browses too, rather than searching for something that can never match. Passing a real query is unchanged. See [src/recall_index.ts](src/recall_index.ts), [src/cli_recall.ts](src/cli_recall.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).

### Changed
- **BREAKING (JSON output): `types`/`callers`/`dead`/`test-for --json` now share the same envelope shape as `symbol`/`refs`/`skeleton`/`outline`.** These four were the half of the migration left on a bare JSON array, so a script consuming `--json` still had to branch on shape depending on which command it called. They now always return `{items, truncated, totalCount}`, whether or not truncation occurred, with `totalCount` meaning the same thing it does everywhere else: items matching the filter, before truncation — so `dead --top 5` reports how many dead symbols there are, not how many it printed. Their rows also route through the overflow guard now, like their four siblings already did, so a whole-project `types --json` is bounded instead of unbounded. `semantic --json` keeps its payload-level `source` field alongside the envelope (`{source, items, truncated, totalCount}`). A user-visible payload change for machine consumers reading a bare array out of any of these four commands. Field names were unchanged at the time — see the dual-key `filePath` addition for `callers`/`dead` below. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-guarded in [tests/json_envelope_shape.test.ts](tests/json_envelope_shape.test.ts).
- **The oversized-skill first-load gate now hands back the compact slice instead of a pointer to it.** The pre-Skill hook already extracted the slice — that extraction is the gate condition — and then threw it away, denying with "run `token-goat skill-body <name> --compact`" to fetch bytes it had just computed. That cost a reasoning turn plus a Bash round-trip every time. The slice now ships inline in the hook reply, under a one-line header naming the skill, its size, and `token-goat skill-body <name>` for the full body, which stays on disk and fully recallable. The old pointer deny is unchanged when there is no `<!-- COMPACT_END -->` marker, when the slice is itself over the 6000-byte oversize threshold, or when the read fails. Inlined loads record a new `skill_compact_inlined` stat with real bytes saved (body minus slice), rather than the zero-byte event the pointer path records. See [src/hooks_skill.ts](src/hooks_skill.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts), regression-tested in [tests/hooks_skill.test.ts](tests/hooks_skill.test.ts).
- **`--help` now points to cheaper lookup options.** A top-level `token-goat --help` emits ~21KB and lists ~140 commands with full descriptions; without guidance most users pay the full cost on every discovery query. A short footer now appears at the end, naming `token-goat help <command>` and `token-goat commands --grep <pattern>` as cheaper alternatives. The tip shows an *anchored* pattern on purpose: `commands --grep '^read$'` costs ~700B against the ~21.9KB full help (97% saved), while a bare `--grep read` also matches every command whose description contains "read" and returns ~7KB. The footer does not leak into subcommand help and costs under 250 bytes, so it pays for itself instantly on the first avoided full-help re-read. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), regression-tested in [tests/help_footer.test.ts](tests/help_footer.test.ts).

### Fixed
- **Copilot CLI never received `rewriteOutput` results (compression, injection fencing, image shrink).** The bridge shim's `postToolUse` branch only ever emitted `additionalContext`, but token-goat's `rewriteOutput` hook results serialize as `hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput`, which matched neither of `extractContext`'s branches -- so the rewritten output was silently discarded and the model received the raw, uncompressed tool result. The WebFetch injection-fencing path is also a `rewriteOutput`, so untrusted-content fencing was not reaching the model under Copilot either. Now maps `updatedToolOutput` to Copilot's `modifiedResult` ({resultType: 'success', textResultForLlm}), which can coexist with `additionalContext` in the same response; `sessionStart` (which shares no code path with `postToolUse` anymore) never emits it, since it has no tool result to modify. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts), regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **`webfetch:compress` stat undercounted savings on non-ASCII pages.** The stat recorded UTF-16 string `.length` instead of UTF-8 byte deltas, so pages with CJK or Cyrillic characters showed 2-3x less compression benefit than they achieved. `String.length` counts UTF-16 code units while every other byte-valued stat in the codebase counts UTF-8 bytes. The delta is now computed from UTF-8 byte lengths, reusing the values already calculated for the net-benefit gate. See [src/hooks_fetch.ts](src/hooks_fetch.ts), regression-tested in [tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts](tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts).
- **`web-output` could never return the raw fetched page.** Large HTML bodies were cleaned before being cached, so the original markup — a script tag, an attribute, an embedded JSON blob — was gone for good and the only way back was re-fetching, which is what the cache exists to avoid. The raw body is now stored alongside the cleaned one and recoverable with `web-output --raw`. Default output is unchanged. See [src/hooks_fetch.ts](src/hooks_fetch.ts), [src/web_cache.ts](src/web_cache.ts).
- **`coverage-gaps`, `note-list --stale-only`, and `stats` read the same whether the store was empty or the filter just matched nothing.** "No coverage gaps found." meant both "your code is clean" and "nothing is indexed"; "No stale notes." meant both "no notes exist" and "notes exist, none stale"; "No stats recorded yet." meant both "nothing was recorded" and "everything falls outside `--window-days`". Each now names which case it is. A new guard checks every command in the CLI registry is classified, so a new one can't ship unaudited. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts).
- **`trace` printed an empty traceback block when every frame was a dependency frame.** Just the header and the exception, nothing between — which reads as "trace found nothing" and sends you back to the raw traceback. It now says all N frames were filtered out as non-project, so a failure entirely inside dependency code is a definitive answer instead of a dead end. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts).
- **`trace --keep N` dropped frames without saying so.** The kept frames are the innermost ones, so the call path that led to the failure vanished silently and the output looked complete. It now notes how many frames were elided and that a higher `--keep` shows more. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts).
- **`dead --kind` silently returned zero rows for a comma-separated or unrecognized kind, printing the same "No dead symbols found." a genuinely clean codebase produces.** `--kind function,method` matched the literal string `"function,method"` against the DB (no stored kind is ever spelled that way) instead of unioning the two kinds, and `--kind bogusnonsense` matched nothing for the same reason — both read as a clean project instead of a filtered-to-nothing or invalid query. `--kind` now splits on `,` like every other multi-spec surface in this CLI (`read`/`refs`/`skeleton`/`outline`/`section`) and returns the union, computed before `--exclude-tests`/`--grep` filtering and `--top` slicing so their counts and notices stay accurate. An unrecognized kind now errors with the same `Did you mean` convention symbol-miss paths use, validated against the union of this project's own indexed kinds and a static list of kinds every language adapter in this repo is known to emit (a kind absent from a small project, like `class` with zero classes, still validates instead of being wrongly rejected). See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/index_reader.ts](src/index_reader.ts), regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **`npm test` and other package-manager run-scripts never reached the specific output filter, only the generic npm one.** Dispatch matches on `argv[0]` (`npm`), but a script alias like `scripts.test` never appears in the command string, so `npm test` backed by `vitest run` always hit the generic package-manager filter instead of the vitest one — a real loss in this repo, where `npm test` output is the dominant Bash volume. `npm test`/`npm run <script>`/`yarn <script>`/`pnpm run <script>`/`bun run <script>` now resolve the script (via the nearest ancestor `package.json`, cached by mtime) and dispatch on the command it actually runs. Falls straight through to the unchanged npm/pnpm/yarn/bun filter — silently, never throwing — when there's no `package.json`, it's unreadable/malformed, the script is missing, or the script body is a compound command (`&&`/`||`/`;`/pipe) that isn't one dispatchable tool; a self-referencing script chain is bounded to 5 hops. Bare `npm install`/`ci`/`ls` and `bun test` (bun's own built-in runner, not a script alias) are unaffected. See [src/tool_filters/helpers.ts](src/tool_filters/helpers.ts), [src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts](src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts).
- **`callers --grep` matching nothing returned a prose notice to a caller that asked for `--json`.** The filtered-to-empty branch exits 0 — the symbol does have callers, the pattern just matched none of them — and printed `(all N callers were filtered out by --grep ...)` regardless of output mode, so a script got a success status and a body no JSON parser accepts. It now emits the same `{items: [], truncated: false, totalCount: 0}` envelope the populated branch does, matching `types --grep`'s own JSON branch. Text output is unchanged. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), regression-guarded in [tests/json_envelope_shape.test.ts](tests/json_envelope_shape.test.ts).
- **A single huge file could claim nearly unbounded bytes-saved on a surgical-read stat.** `sumFileSizes` summed real on-disk file sizes with no ceiling, feeding `recordReadStat`'s counterfactual that the agent would otherwise have read the whole file — false for a large file, and unbounded: measured on a real index, five `sqlite-query` calls against a 940MB `global.db` claimed 1.6GB/410.5Mt of savings, 16.7% of the entire all-time ledger from five events. Each file's contribution is now capped at 100,000 bytes before summing, so a legitimate multi-file read still accumulates across files while no single file inflates the total. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/sum_file_sizes_ceiling.test.ts](tests/sum_file_sizes_ceiling.test.ts).
- **`image_shrink_skipped` was registered as a stat kind but never recorded.** It appeared in `KIND_TO_SOURCE` and the `Images` group of `token-goat stats --full`, so it looked wired, but nothing ever called `recordStat` with it — the row was permanently empty. It now records when a file qualifies for a shrink attempt (over the size or dimension threshold) but the re-encode doesn't beat the original or the image can't be decoded, so `stats` can show how often the threshold is declining a real candidate. Event-only, 0 bytes/tokens, same convention as `skill_oversized_first_load`. See [src/image_shrink.ts](src/image_shrink.ts), regression-tested in [tests/image_shrink.test.ts](tests/image_shrink.test.ts).
- **`token-goat refs` spelled the same file path two different ways depending on how many symbols you asked for.** `refs src/util.ts::foldCase` rendered rows as `src/db.ts:331`, while `refs "src/util.ts::foldCase,src/util.ts::foldPath"` rendered the identical row as `c:/Projects/token-goat/src/db.ts:331`: the single-symbol path resolved a display root and the multi-symbol and cross-file paths passed `undefined`. All three now render root-relative when a project root resolves and absolute when none does, in text rows, `--callers` group headers, `--context` windows, and `--top` summaries. `--json` changes with them (`filePath`, and `--top`'s `fileCounts[].file`), so a payload is reproducible instead of specific to one machine and one drive-letter casing, matching what `outline --json` and `skeleton --json` already do — a user-visible payload change for machine consumers reading absolute paths out of `refs --json`. The render root is now sourced in one place shared by the renderers and the `--grep` filter, so the filter cannot again test a string the rows do not show. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`types`, `callers`, `dead`, `brief`, `test-for`, `symbol`, and `semantic` spelled `--json` paths absolute while their own plain-text output already rendered the same rows root-relative.** Same command, same repo, two spellings decided only by `--json` — the same inconsistency `refs --json` was fixed for one commit ago. `types`' `filePath`, `callers`' `file`, `dead`'s `file`, `brief`'s `symbol.filePath`/`callers[].file`, `test-for`'s `testFile`, `symbol`'s `filePath`, and `semantic`'s `filePath` now all render through the project's `toDisplayPath` — root-relative when a project root resolves, absolute when none does, matching `outline`/`skeleton`/`refs --json` and each command's own text output. A user-visible payload change for machine consumers reading absolute paths out of any of these seven commands' `--json`. `symbol --json`'s test asserting it "stays absolute" pinned this exact inconsistency and has been replaced with a root-relative positive plus an out-of-project negative control, matching every sibling command's coverage. Field names and envelope shapes are unchanged (`file`/`testFile` were not renamed to `filePath`). See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **Merged multi-file `--json` rows could not say which file they came from, and `outline`'s path was machine-specific.** `skeleton --json` projected only name/kind/lineStart/lineEnd, so once a comma-separated spec merged several files into one payload, two rows both reading `lineStart: 3` were indistinguishable while meaning different files. `outline` did carry a path, but an absolute one — different on every machine, and on Windows differing by drive-letter casing — so it could not be compared across runs or fed back verbatim. Both now emit `filePath` through the same `toDisplayPath` helper the rest of the codebase uses, rendering it relative to the project root. It appears when, and only when, the payload can hold more than one file: a single-file caller already named the file, and every per-row field costs rows, because the row guard caps by bytes. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`outline` and `skeleton` with `--json` and a comma-separated file list returned output no JSON parser accepts.** The multi-file path joins per-file blocks with a blank line, which is right for text and produces N complete documents back to back for JSON — so `token-goat outline a,b --json | jq` failed outright, on exactly the input the flag exists to serve. The blocks are now merged into one document: items concatenated in the order the files were named, `truncated` true if any file truncated, `totalCount` summed. Rows carry their own `filePath`, so a flat array stays unambiguous and the payload keeps the shape a single-file call returns — a caller never branches on file count. A file that yields prose instead of JSON (unreadable, or no indexed symbols) is reported in an `errors` array rather than being spliced in as text or dropped, and `errors` is omitted entirely when every file succeeded. Text output is unchanged. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`outline --json` shipped the full source body of every symbol, and the bloat silently truncated the map.** The JSON branch spread the raw indexed row, so `body` came along — for the one command whose purpose is to map a file *without* its bodies. On [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) that was 45 KB of an 87 KB payload, and since the row guard caps by bytes, the bodies crowded out symbols: 164 of 504 survived, so asking for machine-readable output returned under a third of what the text form prints in full. The rows are now projected explicitly to the fields `outline` actually renders, which fits 372 of 504 symbols in the same budget — 2.3x the map for the same cost. The explicit projection also closes the trap that let it in: a spread type-checks against the row type no matter what columns are added later, so the next new column would have leaked in just as quietly. `--stats` columns and text output are unchanged. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`outline` and `skeleton` rendered a filtered-to-empty listing exactly like a file with no symbols at all.** `token-goat outline s.ts --min-lines 9999` printed `# Outline: s.ts  (0 symbols)` and exited 0 — the same shape a genuinely symbol-less file produces, except that case has a dedicated message explaining itself. So the one output that was really a statement about the filter read as a definitive answer about the file, and the caller stops looking instead of widening the filter. Both commands now say when a filter emptied the listing, naming the filter and the pre-filter symbol count. A file that genuinely has no symbols keeps its own message unchanged, and JSON output is untouched: `totalCount` there already means "items matching the filter" consistently across every command, so it stays 0. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`note-add --symbol` and `insert-section --after` dumped every candidate in the file as a "Did you mean" suggestion, and could not resolve a typo.** Both live in [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and build their own miss message, so they never picked up the similarity ranking the read-side miss paths gained earlier — `note-add s.ts --symbol zzzzz` listed every symbol in the file as a suggestion, and `insert-section d.md --after zzzzz` listed every heading. A query resembling nothing produced the same output as a genuine near-miss, which makes the block read as a guess list rather than a suggestion. Both now rank candidates by similarity to the query first, and fall through to `token-goat outline <file>` when ranking leaves nothing, reusing the same helpers and wording as `symbol` and `section`. As a result a misspelled name or heading is now suggested (`epsilo` finds `epsilon`, `Configuraton Options` finds `Configuration Options`) where before it was not. The two existing tests for these paths asserted the unranked dump as correct and have been rewritten. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **A misspelled heading got no "Did you mean" suggestion either, for the same reason.** `token-goat section "d.md::Instalation"` printed the bare `outline` pointer, identical to what a query about nothing gets, even though `Installation and Setup` was right there — `Instalation` is neither a substring of `Installation` nor the reverse, so every containment tier missed it. Heading suggestions now use the same bounded edit-distance fallback as symbol names, matched word-to-word rather than against the whole heading, since a heading is usually several words and no realistic typo budget spans the whole string. It runs only when containment found nothing, so an exact, case-insensitive, prefix, or word-subset match still wins unchanged, and a query near no heading word still gets the `outline` pointer instead of an arbitrary guess. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **A misspelled name got no "Did you mean" suggestion at all, because the suggestion list only did substring matching.** `token-goat symbol parseConfg` filtered out `parseConfig` entirely: the query is neither a substring of the real name nor the reverse, so the caller was sent to a generic fallback for a name one keystroke away. Dropped, swapped, and mistyped characters are the most common way a caller misses a name they already know. A bounded edit-distance pass now runs when — and only when — substring matching found nothing, so it can supply an answer where there was none but can never reorder or displace a substring match. The budget scales with query length (1 edit for short queries, 2 from 8 characters up) and very long queries skip it, so a query far from every candidate still suggests nothing rather than filling the block with noise. Applies to every command that ranks near-name candidates. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`section`'s miss path dumped every heading in the file as a "Did you mean" suggestion regardless of relevance, and could not resolve a distinctive suffix or word-subset query.** A query with no plausible relation to any heading (`zzzz`) printed the exact same candidate list as a genuine near-miss. Suggestions are now filtered and ranked by similarity to the query before being capped at the existing 5-candidate limit; an unrelated query now gets a pointer to `token-goat outline <file>` instead of a full heading dump, so the miss still leads somewhere, and a file with no headings at all says so outright. Separately, a heading resolution now also auto-redirects on a distinctive suffix or word-subset match once exact/case-insensitive/prefix matching all miss (`Setup` → "Installation and Setup", `Config Options` → "Configuration Options"), using the same `(redirected from: ...)` notice as the existing prefix redirect; a query matching 2+ headings under this rule is never guessed and reports a miss listing those candidates instead. See [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`replace` diagnosed a CRLF/LF-only mismatch and then still errored instead of fixing it.** `replace` is the documented fallback edit path when a Read is denied — there is no other way to edit that file. But when the only difference between `--old-from`/`--old-b64` and the file was line endings, it printed "a near-match exists that differs only by line endings" and stopped, forcing a manual re-encode round-trip with no fallback of its own. Transcripts: 462 `replace` calls outside this repo, 41 distinct failures, this CRLF near-match the dominant one, recurring across at least 3 projects on both `.md` and `.ts` files. Now, when the exact match fails but a unique match exists once CRLF/LF are collapsed, `replace` performs it — writing the new text back in the file's line-ending convention at that specific location (not the whole file) and saying so in the success message. An ambiguous normalized match (more than one place) still errors, now naming how many places matched. `--normalize-newlines` is unchanged, for forcing normalization proactively. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **Bash hook denied plain-text background task logs as JSONL transcripts.** Claude Code's `Bash(run_in_background: true)` writes plain-text output logs to `tasks/<id>.output`, the same path shape used for JSONL agent transcripts. The hook unconditionally denied them all as JSONL without reading the file, blocking legitimate task logs and breaking the suggested recovery. Now reads the first byte: only denies if the file starts with `{` (true JSONL); plain-text logs pass through, and missing/unreadable files fall through gracefully. Genuine JSONL transcripts are still denied with the unchanged message. The path is normalized (Git Bash `/c/...` and WSL `/mnt/c/...` both resolve to `C:/...`) before that read, so the deny still fires for a genuine transcript under every path spelling — an earlier pass of this fix read the raw path straight from the command text, which Node cannot resolve on Git Bash, so the read always threw and every transcript silently passed through unread. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts).
- **Bash hook ignored tool-results plain-text cache.** Claude Code offloads oversized tool outputs to `tool-results/<id>.txt`, covered by the Read hook (line 137) but missing entirely from the Bash hook. Commands like `cat`/`tail`/`sed` on these files skirted denial and wasted tokens re-reading cached output. Added matching path pattern and routing to `token-goat bash-output --file`, emitting a contextOutput hint. Transcripts across 13 projects: 1,366 Bash calls touching `tool-results/*.txt` (475 K tokens, 5.5 MB). See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts).
- **`deps` printed absolute paths you could not feed back into another command.** The whole point of `deps` is to list a file's imports so you can then read one, but the imports came out as full machine-specific paths (`C:\Projects\token-goat\src\baseline.ts`) while every sibling command prints paths relative to the project root. Under `--json` the payload contradicted itself: `file` was root-relative while `internal` was absolute. Both are root-relative now, and a dependency outside the project — which cannot be made relative — is spelled the same way in both fields instead of one using backslashes and the other forward slashes. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts).
- **`skill-history` printed a column header and nothing else when nothing was cached.** An empty table with its header still showing reads as a populated result that happened to return no rows, or as a lookup against the wrong cache directory — the same gap `skill-list` and `skill-diff` had already closed. It now says the store is empty. `--json` still emits `[]`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`outline`, `skeleton`, and `types` reported a path that does not exist as a real file with nothing in it.** `token-goat outline src/nope.ts` answered "No indexed symbols found in 'src/nope.ts'", which reads as a definitive statement about a file that exists — so a mistyped or stale path looked like a real answer and the caller stopped looking instead of fixing the path. `exports`, `imports`, `deps`, and `test-for` already said "Could not read: <path>" here; these three were the missed siblings and now use the same wording. A file that does exist but has no indexed symbols keeps its original message. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts).
- **`skill-list --session-id` and `skill-size --session-id` reported a filtered view as an empty cache.** Asking for a session with no cached skills said "No skills cached yet." even when skills were cached under other sessions, so the caller concluded the cache was empty and re-did work that was already there. Both now say how many the filter hid. Output without `--session-id` is unchanged. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **Doctor's empty-index fix suggested a command that fails in its own most common trigger case.** `run 'token-goat index .' here` refuses in a non-git folder ("no tracked files found... Pass --walk or --force-walk") — and an empty index is most often a non-git scratch folder. The suggestion is now git-aware: `token-goat index .` inside a git repo, `token-goat index . --walk` outside one, using the existing cheap fs-only git-detection check rather than shelling out to git. See [src/index_health.ts](src/index_health.ts), [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts), [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts).
- **`map` carried its own copy of that same unrunnable suggestion.** The `## Top symbols: none` line on an unindexed project hardcoded `run 'token-goat index .'`, so it printed a command that refuses outside a git repo just like doctor's did. It now uses the same git-aware helper. See [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts).
- **`symbol` sent you to `semantic` when neither could work.** A miss with no near-name candidates ends in `Try: token-goat semantic "<name>"`, but on a project with zero indexed files `semantic` fails exactly as `symbol` just did — so the caller spent a second command reaching the same dead end before seeing the note that names the real fix. The pointer is now suppressed in that one case; with any index at all it is unchanged. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`read`, `diff`/`log`, `openapi-op`, and `zip-read` did-you-mean lists on a miss dumped every same-file symbol, operation, or archive entry regardless of relevance.** A one-character typo and a totally unrelated query produced byte-identical suggestion lists. Worse, `read`'s and `diff`/`log`'s underlying DB query capped at 5 rows *before* ranking, so on a file with more than a handful of symbols the true near-match could be excluded from consideration entirely — never even shown. All four now filter and rank candidates by similarity to the query first (the same mechanism `symbol` already used, and `section` before it), scanning a larger bounded set and capping only after ranking. An unrelated query now gets no list, plus a pointer to the command that lists the real options (`outline <file>`, `openapi-outline <file>`, or `zip-list <archive>`) instead of a wrong or dead-ending suggestion. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).

## [2.6.25] - 2026-08-06

### Fixed
- **`map` printed whole absolute paths instead of locations you can reuse, on some machines.** Symbol locations are shown relative to the project root, but the comparison was textual, so a root spelled differently from the indexed path shared no prefix and the full absolute path was printed instead. Two spellings do this in practice: a Windows 8.3 short directory name (`RUNNER~1`) against its long form, and macOS reporting the same directory as both `/var` and `/private/var`. Both are collapsed now. See [src/paths.ts](src/paths.ts).
- **Piping any command into `head` crashed.** `token-goat grep ... | head -2` died with an unhandled `EPIPE` error and a stack trace, because nothing anywhere handled a consumer closing the pipe early. Piping to `head`, `grep -q`, or a pager you quit is one of the most common ways these commands get called, and the crash read as the command failing rather than the pipe closing. Only `EPIPE` is absorbed; every other stream error still surfaces. See [src/main.ts](src/main.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts).
- **`token-goat changed HEAD~1` ignored the ref you gave it.** The README documented `changed [<ref>]` but the command took no positional argument, so the ref was silently dropped and the `HEAD~5` default ran instead — an agent that followed the docs got a wrong answer with nothing to indicate its argument had been thrown away. An explicit `--since` still wins over the positional. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`token-goat changed` on a shallow repo printed a raw git error naming no working flag.** The `HEAD~5` default fails on any repo with fewer than six commits, which includes CI checkouts (`actions/checkout` defaults to depth 1), fresh worktrees, and new projects. Git's own message is unchanged; a hint now names the repo's real commit count and a `--since` ref that actually resolves, falling back to the empty-tree hash on a single-commit repo. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`context-for` and `ask` emitted `read` commands that did not work.** Their whole output is a list of follow-up commands, but the commands left off the line anchor. When one symbol name had two definitions in a file, both suggestions came out byte-identical and running either failed with "Ambiguous symbol". Every suggestion now ends in `@LINE`, so it runs as printed. `--json` entries gained a matching `line` field. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts).
- **`outline src/a.ts src/b.ts` silently dropped the second file.** It printed the first file's outline and said nothing about the rest, so an agent believed it had seen files it never got. Extra file arguments are now reported in a note that names the comma-separated form. Same for `skeleton`, `exports`, and `imports`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).

### Added
- **`--exclude-tests` on `refs`, `callers`, and `dead`.** Test references drown out production ones: on this repo `refs "src/paths.ts::normalizePath"` returns 428 references across 46 files, 393 of them from tests, and the default view surfaces about one of the 13 production files. `callers` emits 19,968 bytes where 1,363 are production. `dead` reports 20 symbols, 16 in test files and fixtures. The flag is opt-in — output without it is unchanged — and filtering runs before any `--limit`/`--top` cut, so it never quietly returns fewer results than you asked for. `dead` filters on where a symbol is defined; `refs` and `callers` filter on where it is used. When the filter removes everything, the output says how many were hidden instead of reporting the symbol as unreferenced. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **Comma-separated file lists on `outline`, `skeleton`, `exports`, and `imports`.** `token-goat outline "src/a.ts,src/b.ts"` reads both files in one call and prints one clearly-headed block per file. The rest of the family (`read`, `section`, `refs`, `brief`) already took this form; these four rejected it. Single-file behaviour and all flags are unchanged. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`-C, --context <n>` on `refs`, `callers`, and `brief`.** These commands told you where a symbol was used but never showed the call site. `-C 1` prints one line of real source either side of each hit, in the same form `grep -C` already uses. Under `--json` each item gains a `contextLines` array; the existing `context` field (the enclosing symbol name) is untouched. Default is 0, and output with the flag omitted is unchanged. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts).
- **`symbol --project [path]`.** Scopes a bare-name symbol search to one project's index instead of the default cross-project global index — pass no value to use the current directory's project root, or a path to scope to a different one. The runtime already accepted a `projectRoot` option (used by the MCP server) but the CLI never exposed a flag for it, so every `token-goat symbol` call searched every indexed project on the machine. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`grep --symbol`.** Annotates each hit with its enclosing indexed symbol — ` [name (kind)]` in text mode, a `symbol: {name, kind, lineStart, lineEnd} | null` field per item under `--json` — so a match's containing function is visible without a follow-up `scope` call. `null`/no tag for a hit outside any indexed symbol (module-level code). See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`exports` reports line ranges.** Text output appends `(lineStart-lineEnd)` per exported symbol; `--json` adds `lineStart`/`lineEnd` fields. Names caught only by the source-text scan (no corresponding index row, e.g. certain re-export forms) report no location rather than a fabricated one. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`semantic` now names the enclosing symbol.** Each hit's `name`/`kind` (previously always `null`) resolve to the innermost indexed symbol containing the hit's start line, with `null`/`null` kept for a hit outside any symbol (e.g. a top-of-file imports chunk). Text output gets a matching `— inside <name> (<kind>)` suffix. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **Cross-file "did you mean" for a wrong-file `file::symbol` spec.** Guessing the right symbol name against the wrong file (`token-goat read "src/util.ts::walkProject"` when `walkProject` actually lives in `src/baseline.ts`) now leads with the correct file and a ready-to-run spec, ahead of the existing same-file candidate list. Covers `read` and the shared `diff`/`log` resolver. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`--json` on `map` and `doctor`.** `token-goat map --json` emits the project map (file count, languages, top symbols, recent files) as JSON. `token-goat doctor --json` emits the check results as a JSON array, one entry per check with its `ok`/`warn`/`fail` status. Text output is unchanged when the flag is omitted. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`map` now says when the index is empty** instead of silently dropping the "Top symbols" section. A project with no indexed files gets an explicit marker line telling you to run `token-goat index .`, instead of the heading just vanishing. See [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts).
- **Path-priority scoring for `semantic`.** Results are re-ranked with a multiplier so live source wins ties/near-ties against stale or archival prose that otherwise outranks it on raw vector similarity: `archive/`, `archived/`, `old/`, `deprecated/`, `plans/`, `drafts/`, `CHANGELOG*`, `*.bak`, `*.orig` get a stronger penalty, and general docs (`docs/**`, `*.md`) get a milder one. It's a nudge, not a hard filter — a genuinely much better archival match still surfaces. Configurable via `semantic.archive_weight` / `semantic.docs_weight`; set either to `1` to disable that penalty. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts), [src/config.ts](src/config.ts).

## [2.6.24] - 2026-08-05

### Fixed
- **`install --copilot` now honours `COPILOT_HOME`.** Copilot CLI documents that variable as replacing `~/.copilot` for both hooks and instructions. token-goat ignored it and always wrote to the home-relative path, which fails in the worst way available: install reports success, the config it writes is perfectly valid, and Copilot reads a different directory — so every hook silently never fires and nothing points at the mismatch. An exported-but-empty value is treated as unset rather than resolved against the working directory. Project scope (`--local`) is unaffected. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts).
- **Copilot CLI now gets the token-goat routing reminder at session start, so it stops forgetting the commands exist.** Copilot was the only supported harness where `sessionStart` was hard-wired to do nothing. The reason given in the code was that token-goat had no session-start handler — untrue for a long time, and the reason Copilot sessions alone were never told token-goat was available. `install --copilot` now registers `sessionStart` and the shim returns the reminder as `additionalContext`. Verified against Copilot CLI 1.0.77 with a canary that appears only in the reminder: wired, a session answers with it; with the hook removed and nothing else changed, the same question in the same directory answers that it has no such note. The upstream bug that would have made this pointless ([github/copilot-cli#2142](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/2142), `additionalContext` discarded) was fixed months ago, and its companion multi-extension bug never applied to this config-file hook path. If you installed the Copilot bridge before this release, re-run `token-goat install --copilot` and restart Copilot CLI — it caches hook config at session start. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts), [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts).

## [2.6.23] - 2026-08-05

### Changed
- **Claude Code hooks now run through a generated shim instead of a bare `token-goat hook <event>` command.** `token-goat install` writes `~/.claude/hooks/token-goat-shim.js` and wires each hook to `"<node>" "<shim>" <event> "<entry>"`. The shim imports the hook library in-process rather than spawning a second process, and naming the node binary directly skips the npm bin wrapper — on Windows that wrapper is a `cmd.exe` layer every hook was paying for. Measured 480 ms → 324 ms per hook call, about a third, on every tool call in a session. The shim itself was written and fully unit-tested months ago but no install path ever wrote it to disk, so it had never run for anyone. Re-running `install` upgrades an existing bare-command entry in place, and hook groups you have added your own commands to are left alone. See [src/install.ts](src/install.ts), [src/bridges/claudecode.ts](src/bridges/claudecode.ts).
- **Oversized subagent reports are compacted before the parent agent sees them.** A report over 8 KB keeps 6 lines at each end of any long fenced code block and loses the middle to a marker, with the full text still recallable. Prose is never touched — the caveats and "I did not verify X" admissions that catch a subagent shipping something it never checked all live in prose, while what collapses is gate transcripts and diff tables that can be regenerated from the repo. Measured 32% smaller on a realistic report. Thanks to Gerard for the envelopes idea. See [src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts](src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts).
- **`token-goat install` now says when hooks were already up to date** instead of reporting a fresh install every time. Every other harness already reported this; the base Claude Code path was the one that discarded it. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).

### Added
- **Cross-file `read`.** `token-goat read "a.ts::alpha,b.ts::beta"` pulls symbols from several files in one call. A bare name after a `file::symbol` segment keeps the previous file, so `"a.ts::alpha,beta"` still means two symbols from `a.ts`. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **Multi-symbol `brief`.** `token-goat brief "file.ts::alpha,beta"` returns a merged view, matching the comma syntax `read` and `refs` already had. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`--full` on `bash-output`, `web-output`, and `mcp-output`.** These commands elide the middle of a long entry by default (head 30 / tail 80), so a cached entry could not actually be recalled in full — the store was lossless but no reader was. `--full` prints the stored entry verbatim. Explicit narrowing you asked for (`--section`, `--grep`, `--max-matches`) still applies. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`agent_report` config section** with `min_bytes`, `fence_collapse_min_lines`, and `fence_collapse_keep_lines`, plus matching environment overrides. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts).

### Fixed
- Envelope compaction recorded no savings of its own, so the largest new saver reported as worth nothing on the stats dashboard. It now records real bytes under `agent_report_compact`. See [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts).
- The fenced-block scanner used a plain backtick toggle, so a nested ` ``` ` inside a `~~~` or four-backtick block ended it early and corrupted the collapse. It now tracks the opening marker's character and length. See [src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts](src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts).

### Internal
- New guard walks every scalar key in the config and checks it survives a save/load round trip. This repo has shipped a missing `saveConfig` line at least four times, each caught in production and closed with its own single-key test; this one grows with the schema instead. See [tests/guards/config_roundtrip_completeness.test.ts](tests/guards/config_roundtrip_completeness.test.ts).

## [2.6.22] - 2026-08-02

### Added
- **Doc comments are now indexed for every supported language, not just Python.** A `/** ... */`, `///`, `//`, or `#` comment sitting directly above a declaration is now stored as that symbol's docstring, so `skeleton --stats`, `outline --stats`, and `read --stats` report real doc coverage instead of calling everything undocumented. Previously only Python's in-body docstrings were captured, which meant token-goat misreported coverage on its own TypeScript source. Covers the tree-sitter languages plus 12 regex-based ones (Kotlin, PHP, Swift, Scala, C#, Dart, Zig, Apex, R, Elixir, PowerShell, Bash). Lua, INI and Vue SFC are deliberately left out rather than guessed at. See [src/doc_comment.ts](src/doc_comment.ts), [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts).
- **Multi-symbol `read`.** `token-goat read "file.ts::alpha,beta"` returns several symbol bodies from one file in a single call, matching the comma syntax `refs` already had. The existing line-range form (`file.ts::120,140`) still means a line range and is unaffected. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`read --stats`.** Adds each symbol's reference count and whether it has a doc comment, matching the flag `skeleton` and `outline` already had. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`indexing.skip_files` config key.** The list of generated files skipped during indexing is now configurable by basename, the same way `skip_dirs` already was. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts).

### Changed
- **Installed hook matchers now list only the tools token-goat handles.** `token-goat install` wrote a catch-all matcher for `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse`, so Claude Code started a hook process for every tool call — including ones token-goat has no handler for. Most of a hook's cost is process startup rather than the hook's own work (measured 308 ms to load the bundle versus 333 ms to also do the work), so those calls were paying full price for nothing. The matcher is generated from the live hook registry instead of a fixed list, so it stays correct as handlers change, and re-running `install` upgrades an existing catch-all entry in place. Hook groups you have added your own commands to are left alone. Measured against a real 2,316-call session: 906 of 4,632 hook process spawns (19.6%) no longer happen. See [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts), [src/install.ts](src/install.ts).

### Fixed
- Symbols in regex-parsed languages reported their parent class name as if it were a doc comment, so an undocumented method inside a class showed up as documented. The parent name now has its own database column. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts).
- Generated coverage reports (`coverage.json`, `coverage-final.json`) are no longer indexed. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts).

### Internal
- `tests/` is now type-checked with no exclusions via a dedicated `tsconfig.tests.json`, closing a gap where lint covered test files but `typecheck` did not. See [tsconfig.tests.json](tsconfig.tests.json).

## [2.6.21] - 2026-07-31

### Added
- **`semantic --json`.** Machine-readable output for `semantic`, the last surgical-read command that lacked one. Emits `{source, items, truncated, totalCount}`, with every item carrying the same keys across both the embeddings and full-text paths (`null` for the ones that don't apply to that source), so a caller never has to branch on `source` to know which keys exist. Goes to stdout on every exit code, including a no-match, so piping to `jq` works. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`doctor` now checks stored symbol body size.** The existing check only warned once `global.db` passed 1 GB, which a damaged index can sit well under: a real 478 MB index reported healthy while holding a 1.3 million-character symbol body left behind by the since-fixed extractor bug. The new check compares against the parser's own `MAX_SYMBOL_BODY_CHARS` cap — any stored body above it can only predate the fix — and names the file responsible. See [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts).
- **The SessionStart hook surfaces that warning once per session**, so a damaged index is noticed instead of waiting for someone to run `doctor` by hand. Silent on a healthy index. See [src/hooks_session_start.ts](src/hooks_session_start.ts).

## [2.6.20] - 2026-07-31

### Changed
- **The routing guidance written into agent instruction files is now a pre-call *gate*, not an advisory list.** An advisory "prefer token-goat" line loses to a harness's own imperative tool-preference rules (Claude Code's Read/Grep, Codex's `shell`/`apply_patch`, Copilot CLI's `view`/`grep`/`glob`) that fire at the moment a read happens — verified empirically, the old block was present in context and still repeatedly violated. The rewritten block phrases one gate question to answer before any read, names and subordinates each harness's own read-tool rules to the *fallback* choice once token-goat is ruled out, lists exemptions exhaustively (file <~200 lines and fully needed; never-indexed; binary/image; no symbol handle) so the gate is decidable, enumerates concrete failure shapes → the command that replaces each, and instructs that sub-agent briefs must carry the gate. The three per-harness copies (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`) plus the base-install skill body (`~/.claude/skills/token-goat/SKILL.md`) now all render from one shared builder ([src/bridges/guidance_block.ts](src/bridges/guidance_block.ts)): the three instruction files wrap `buildGuidanceBlock` (body + begin/end markers) and the skill file embeds `buildGuidanceBody` (the same gate body, marker-free, under its own frontmatter), so the gate has a single source across all four surfaces and the wording can no longer drift across call sites. The skill's YAML frontmatter `description` is deliberately kept as the plain, keyword-dense relevance trigger the harness reads to decide whether to load the skill — it is intentionally exempt from the gate wording. See [src/install.ts](src/install.ts), [src/bridges/codex_install.ts](src/bridges/codex_install.ts), regression-tested in [tests/install_claude_md_skill.test.ts](tests/install_claude_md_skill.test.ts).
- **The subagent-spawn briefing reminder is now an imperative gate-in-miniature, not an advisory preference.** The spawn hook ([src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts](src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts)) is a runtime nudge under a ~300-token briefing budget, so it can't carry the full ~481-token gate — but its old wording ("Prefer surgical reads over full-file dumps…") was the softer register the gate itself warns against, and a freshly spawned subagent starts with no other context pulling it toward token-goat. The line now directs the subagent, in the imperative, to check for a token-goat command before its first read and run it instead of a full-file read or wide grep, with the same "skipping the check is a violation, not an oversight" framing and a short exemption list. Measured cost 72 → 136 tokens (`estimateTokens`, chars/3), well within the 300-token budget; the reminder sits in the survive-first `tail`. Regression-tested in [tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts](tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts).

### Added
- **Copilot CLI install now writes the token-goat routing block into `copilot-instructions.md`.** Previously `install --copilot` registered hooks but wrote no instructions file, so a fresh Copilot CLI user got zero routing guidance. The Copilot bridge now upserts a delimited block into `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` (user scope) or `<repo>/.github/copilot-instructions.md` (`--local`), mirroring the Codex AGENTS.md writer exactly — same `upsertDelimitedBlock` merge, same byte-for-byte preservation of content outside the markers, wired into install/uninstall/`isCopilotCliInstalled` and surfaced as `CopilotCliInstallResult.instructionsPath`. Regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts). See [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts).

## [2.6.19] - 2026-07-30

### Added
- **`insert-section` command.** Inserts new content immediately after a matched section, resolved the same way `section`/`replace` resolve headings (exact, normalized, or an unambiguous prefix) instead of requiring a byte-exact anchor of the previous section's current trailing text — removes the staleness window that bites any append-to-a-running-log edit (e.g. adding the next entry to a lessons-learned doc) the moment an earlier edit in the same session already changed what used to be the last line. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts) and [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`replace --normalize-newlines` flag.** Converts the `--old-from`/`--new-from`/`--old-b64`/`--new-b64` text's line endings to match the target file's dominant line ending before matching, instead of requiring a byte-exact CRLF/LF match. Opt-in — the previous byte-exact-only behavior remains the default. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).
- **`replace`'s "old string not found" now falls back to a closest-matching-line hint** when the CRLF/trailing-newline near-match diagnostic doesn't explain it either, instead of a bare "not found" — mirrors the "Did you mean" pattern `section` already has for unresolvable headings. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).
- **`section`'s existing unambiguous-heading-prefix matching is now documented** in its CLI description and in the large-markdown-file hint, instead of being discoverable only by reading the source — a short prefix like `"Lesson 16"` resolves a much longer unique heading, which is both shorter to type and avoids shell-quoting issues with punctuation in long headings. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts).
- **The large-markdown-file deny hint now promotes `--old-b64`/`--new-b64`** as the no-temp-file path for editing anyway, alongside the existing `--old-from`/`--new-from` example. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts).
- **Architecture notes: `note-add`/`note-get`/`note-list` commands.** Attach a free-text rationale note to a file or a specific symbol (`token-goat note-add <file> [--symbol NAME] --content-from <path>|--content-b64 <b64>`), and read it back with `note-get` or list all notes with `note-list --stale-only`. Each note is fingerprinted against the symbol's body (or the file's symbol manifest) at write time, so `note-list --stale-only` surfaces notes whose underlying code has since changed — advisory only, nothing is auto-rewritten or deleted. See [src/notes.ts](src/notes.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).

### Fixed
- `dep-docs`'s `@types/<pkg>` fallback could point at the wrong file when a package's `main` was a `.js` file — it now correctly swaps the extension to `.d.ts` instead of appending it. See [src/dep_docs.ts](src/dep_docs.ts).
- The Zig language adapter could misattribute a struct declared inside a method as a member of the method's enclosing type, instead of the method-local struct it actually is. See [src/languages/zig.ts](src/languages/zig.ts).
- An aliased `eza --tree` invocation was silently compressed as plain `ls` output instead of using the dedicated eza compressor, because the `ls` binary-claim check ran first and always matched. See [src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts](src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts).
- PHP class/interface/trait/enum detection had no brace-depth check, so a function-local `class Helper {}` (a common lazy-class-definition idiom) was misattributed as a nested member of the enclosing method's class. See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts).
- Bash-output compression could shift real command arguments by one position when a flag's value was a separate token, causing several CLI-aware compressors to silently miss their subcommand and fall back to plain generic compression:
  - `aws --profile prod s3 cp ...` (and other global value-taking AWS flags before the subcommand). See [src/tool_filters/cloud.ts](src/tool_filters/cloud.ts).
  - `gh -R owner/repo pr list` / `gh --hostname ...`. See [src/tool_filters/ci.ts](src/tool_filters/ci.ts).
  - `git --git-dir ... fetch` / `git --work-tree ...`. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts).
