  - `kubectl -n myns get pods` (and `--context`/`--kubeconfig`/`--cluster`/`--user`/`--server`/etc.). See [src/tool_filters/containers.ts](src/tool_filters/containers.ts).
- **The `TOKEN_GOAT_NO_WORKER_SPAWN` test-isolation env var was silently ignored.** The auto-heal path that restarts the background worker daemon after an edit never checked it, so any test exercising the post-edit hook could spawn a real detached worker process during the test run, relying only on the daemon's own self-check to eventually notice and exit. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts).

## [2.6.18] - 2026-07-27

### Fixed
- C# delegates nested in a class now correctly remember which class they belong to, fixing lookups when two classes have a delegate with the same name.
- `csv-query`/`csv-profile` no longer wrongly reject a real column name when the CSV file has a header but no data rows.
- Scala: top-level `val`/`var` declarations (outside any class or object) are now indexed.
- C# delegates marked with an attribute (like `[Serializable]`) are now indexed.
- C++ `using X = Y;` alias declarations are now indexed.
- `token-goat resume` now includes a Skills section with checklists from recently used skills.
- The compact-hint manifest now includes a short "Session goal" summary line.
- `token-goat types` now shows GraphQL scalar declarations.
- `token-goat types` now shows Kotlin and Scala `object` declarations.
- `token-goat types` now shows GraphQL types, interfaces, inputs, enums, and unions.
- `token-goat types` now shows Apex classes, interfaces, and enums.
- Fixed a Lua parsing bug where anonymous functions used as callbacks could corrupt which function a later symbol belonged to.
- 15 more commands — PDF, Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and transcript extraction — now show up in usage stats.
- `csv-profile` now shows up in usage stats.
- **`checkSymbolCount`'s rootDir-scoping test failed deterministically on Windows/macOS CI (never locally).** The regression test built its `files.path` fixture with a raw backslash-to-forward-slash replace instead of `normalizePath()`, diverging from the invariant every real writer relies on: on macOS, `os.tmpdir()`'s `/var/...` public alias gets rewritten to `/private/var/...` by `normalizePath()`'s query-side `normalizeDarwinSystemAlias()` step but not by the raw fixture path; on Windows, a `%TEMP%` pinned to 8.3 short form hits the same divergence via `expandShortPath()`. Fixed by normalizing the fixture path. This is the 4th occurrence of this anti-pattern, so `tests/guards/windows_path_fixture_normalization.test.ts` was hardened with a second check that flags any test hand-flipping backslashes while inserting fixture rows into a path-keyed table, independent of whether a `.toLowerCase()` call happens to co-occur. See [tests/cli_doctor.test.ts](tests/cli_doctor.test.ts), [tests/guards/windows_path_fixture_normalization.test.ts](tests/guards/windows_path_fixture_normalization.test.ts).
- **`extractImports` missed parenthesized PHP `require_once`/`include_once` calls.** The bare-keyword form (`require_once 'x.php'`) matched but the equally common function-call form (`require_once('x.php')`) did not, because the regex required whitespace directly before the quote. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`cleanupStaleDownloads` could delete an in-flight WebFetch download.** It swept every `.tmp` file in the download cache unconditionally, with no age check, so a concurrent download's temp file could be deleted mid-write. Added a 10-minute mtime-based staleness threshold. See [src/webfetch.ts](src/webfetch.ts), regression-tested in [tests/webfetch.test.ts](tests/webfetch.test.ts).
- **`doctor`'s disk-space check could misparse `df` output on a long filesystem name.** `df -k` doesn't guarantee single-line rows; a wrapped name line shifted the column parse. Switched to `df -Pk`, which guarantees POSIX-portable single-line output. See [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts), regression-tested in [tests/cli_doctor.test.ts](tests/cli_doctor.test.ts).
- **Session transcript streaming leaked a file descriptor on early exit.** `streamTurns` called `rl.close()` on an early break but never destroyed the underlying `fs.ReadStream`, which `readline` does not do automatically. See [src/session_read.ts](src/session_read.ts), regression-tested in [tests/session_read.test.ts](tests/session_read.test.ts).
- **`hooks_compact` spawned git unconditionally even when the manifest already fit.** `capManifestChars` ran `adaptiveCharBonus`'s two git spawns before checking whether the manifest was already under the base cap. See [src/hooks_compact.ts](src/hooks_compact.ts), regression-tested in [tests/hooks_compact_adaptive_budget.test.ts](tests/hooks_compact_adaptive_budget.test.ts).
- **Legacy `pnpm-lock.yaml` (`lockfileVersion` < 6) failed to parse.** Legacy lockfiles use slash-separated package keys with no top-level `@` version separator (`/lodash/4.17.21`) and bare-string dependency-section values; the parser required an `@`-delimited key and an object-valued `.version`. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).
- **`runGit` did not defend against a repo-local `diff.external` or `.gitattributes` textconv driver.** A configured external-diff or textconv command would run arbitrary code on every `git diff` call. Hardened by inserting `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` for `diff` subcommands. See [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), regression-tested in [tests/util.test.ts](tests/util.test.ts).
- **Rust/C/C++ symbol extraction gaps**: Rust `mod_item`, `function_signature_item` (unbodied fn / trait required methods / extern FFI declarations), `foreign_mod_item` (`extern "C" { ... }`), `macro_definition` (`macro_rules!`), `static_item`, and `union_item` were all unindexed — none had a `RUST_KIND_BY_TYPE` entry, so `token-goat symbol`/`skeleton` returned nothing for them; `static_item` also required a `RUST_LOCAL_KINDS` exclusion so function-local statics stay out of the global index, matching `const_item`. C/C++ `union_specifier` was likewise unindexed. C/C++ `typedef struct/union/enum { ... } Alias;` indexed zero symbols because the extractor read the node's own (empty) name instead of resolving the aliased name through the `declarator` field chain; a new `cTypedefAliasName` helper now descends plain/pointer/array/function-pointer declarator forms to the terminal identifier. `token-goat types`' `TYPE_KINDS` list also omitted `union`, so the newly-indexed union symbols were findable via `symbol`/`skeleton` but invisible to `types`. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts), [tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts](tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts), [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts). Two related C/C++ typedef gaps remain open: multi-alias typedefs (`typedef struct {...} A, B;`) only index the first name, and C++ `using X = Y;` alias declarations are untouched.
- **Further symbol-kind-map gaps across the tree-sitter-backed language adapters**: C++ `namespace_definition` (including the C++17 nested `namespace A::B { ... }` shorthand) had no entry, so every namespace declaration was invisible even though its members still indexed. C/C++ bodiless function prototypes (`int add(int a, int b);`, the dominant content of any header file) parse as a plain `declaration` node, not `function_definition`, and had no entry either; a new `cFunctionPrototypeName` helper resolves the declarator chain for real prototypes while correctly skipping plain variables, `extern` declarations, and function-pointer variables. Go's `method_elem` (interface method requirements), TypeScript's `method_signature`/`property_signature`/`abstract_method_signature` (interface members and abstract class members), Java's `annotation_type_element_declaration` (`@interface` members), Python's `type_alias_statement` (PEP 695 `type X = ...`), and Rust's `associated_type` (`trait { type Item; }`, the mechanism behind `Iterator::Item`/`Deref::Target`) were each likewise missing from their respective `*_KIND_BY_TYPE` maps, so every declaration of that shape in every affected language was silently invisible to `symbol`/`read`/`outline`/`skeleton`. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts), [tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts](tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts) (each entry has its own built-bundle e2e assertion, since a kind-map addition proven only at the source level can still be tree-shaken out of the shipped bundle).
- **Extensionless Ruby-DSL filenames indexed zero symbols.** `Gemfile`, `Rakefile`, `Vagrantfile`, `Guardfile`, `Podfile`, `Capfile`, `Fastfile`, and `Brewfile` are all plain Ruby syntax already handled correctly by the ruby extractor, but none had a `FILENAME_LANGUAGE` dispatch entry, so `detectLanguage` fell through to `'unknown'` and every method/task defined in these near-universal manifest/task-runner files was invisible to the index. See [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser_types.test.ts](tests/parser_types.test.ts), [tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts](tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts).
- **`extractMarkdownHeadings` dropped every H4-H6 heading even when called with `limit: Infinity`.** The embedding-boundary path (`buildEmbeddingBoundaries`) passes `Infinity` specifically to capture every heading level for chunk-boundary snapping, but a hardcoded `level > 3` filter applied regardless of the requested limit, silently degrading semantic search precision on any markdown doc using H4+ subheadings (API references, changelogs). The display-hint path keeps its existing H1-H3-only behavior; only the indexing/embedding path now captures all six ATX levels. See [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts); regression-tested in [tests/markdown_hints.test.ts](tests/markdown_hints.test.ts), [tests/markdown_embedding_boundaries_fix.test.ts](tests/markdown_embedding_boundaries_fix.test.ts).
- **`--top 0`/`--limit 0` silently produced a false-clean empty result instead of an error, across a wide swath of commands.** `token-goat dead --top 0` (and the same for `impact`/`similar`/`context-for`/`coverage-gaps`/`arch`/`ask` in [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), plus `bash-history`/`web-history`/`mcp-history`/`history`/`hot`/`recent` in [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts)) sliced its results with an unvalidated limit, so `0` always produced zero rows before the "nothing found" branch ran — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty result (e.g. `dead` claiming no dead code exists when it does). Each command now explicitly rejects a non-positive `--top`/`--limit`, matching the convention already used by `find`/`refs`. A pre-existing `runDead` test that asserted `--top 0` returns zero entries as correct behavior was itself a wrong-oracle test locking in the bug; rewritten to assert rejection. Regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts](tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts), [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts), [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).
- **`token-goat csv-query` and `token-goat brief` never recorded stats**, leaving their `token-goat stats --full` buckets permanently absent regardless of real usage — the same registry/producer desync (a command exists but never calls `recordStat`, or `stats.ts`'s `KIND_TO_SOURCE`/`COMMAND_KINDS` never got an entry for it) already fixed for `map_lookup`/`changed_lookup`/`imports` in prior releases. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_csv_query_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_csv_query_stats.test.ts), [tests/cli_brief_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_brief_stats.test.ts).
- **`commandMentionsCorrelator` only checked the string boundary after a substring match, not before.** A hint's correlator (a file path or cache id) could be wrongly credited as "acted on" when it merely appeared as the suffix of a longer, unrelated token in a later Bash command — inflating a hint category's measured effectiveness, which feeds directly into the auto-suppression threshold for ineffective hint categories. See [src/hint_stats.ts](src/hint_stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hint_stats.test.ts](tests/hint_stats.test.ts).
- **`extractChangelogVersionHint` returned nothing for any `CHANGELOG.md` without an `## [Unreleased]` header.** It fell back to `''` instead of the first version heading actually present, so a fully-released changelog (no pending Unreleased section) surfaced no version hint at all. See [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts), regression-tested in [tests/markdown_hints.test.ts](tests/markdown_hints.test.ts).
- **`token-goat ignores` made two false claims about which exclusion mechanisms apply to which commands.** It implied gitignore/`.env` exclusions and `blocked_roots` config both apply broadly across the CLI, but both are only enforced by `token-goat index`/`index --walk` (and the worker's drain loop, for `blocked_roots`) — `map`/`todo`/`conflicts`/`hot --project` use `baseline.ts`'s `walkProject` and never consult either. `SKIP_DIRS` is the one exclusion genuinely shared across all of them. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).
- **`token-goat session-outline`/`session-slice` never recorded stats**, leaving their dashboard buckets permanently absent regardless of real usage — same registry/producer desync as the `csv-query`/`brief` fix above. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_session_read_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_session_read_stats.test.ts).
- **`.rake` files (Rake tasks) were unindexed and reported zero imports.** No `EXTENSION_LANGUAGE` entry existed for `.rake`, and `extractImports` had no matching branch, so `require_relative` calls in any `.rake` file were silently dropped. See [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/parser_types.test.ts](tests/parser_types.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`extractImports` had per-language regex gaps for Scala, Kotlin, Swift, Haskell, and C#**: Scala/`.sc` grouped imports (`foo.bar.{A, B, C}`) returned one truncated blob instead of the real targets — the same brace-truncation class already fixed for Rust `use foo::{A,B}`. Kotlin/Swift's generic fallback swallowed an `as`-alias or submodule keyword into the import target instead of stripping it. Haskell's qualified/`safe` import modifiers were likewise swallowed into the target. Worst of all, C# using-alias directives (`using X = Y.Z;`) matched **nothing at all** — a total silent drop, not just truncation — because the regex's `\s*;` anchor sat right after the alias name instead of after the full `= target;` clause; this bug existed in both `extractImports`' `.cs` branch and `src/languages/csharp.ts`'s own `USING_RE`, and was fixed in both. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts), regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`extractRgSymbolSearch` and `extractDirectoryListing` matched their trigger flags without a token boundary.** The `-r`/`--recursive` detection regex could match starting at the second dash of an unrelated long flag (`--color=never` contains `r`), silently suppressing the symbol-search hint; `ls -R` detection matched inside plain filenames containing `-R` (e.g. `docs/API-Reference.md`), producing a bogus directory-listing hint. Both anchored to a real token boundary. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **11 more read/query commands never recorded stats**: `json-query`, `json-outline`, `yaml-query`, `yaml-outline`, `openapi-op`, `openapi-outline`, `zip-list`, `zip-read`, `sqlite-query`, `sqlite-schema`, and `conflicts` all left their dashboard buckets permanently zero — same registry/producer desync fixed in one combined pass after auditing every `COMMAND_KINDS` entry against its implementation and confirming no further instances remain. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_structured_read_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_structured_read_stats.test.ts). `runCoverageReportGaps` had the identical gap, fixed separately; regression-tested in [tests/cli_coverage_report_gaps_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_coverage_report_gaps_stats.test.ts).
- **`makeDedupHintHandlers`' Grep/Glob dedup-recall hint recorded the wrong match count.** Claude Code's real `Grep` `files_with_matches` response prefixes the file list with a `"Found N file(s)"` summary line, or the literal string `"No files found"` for an empty result — confirmed against real session transcripts. The handler fed that whole string into a plain non-empty-line counter, which counted the header line itself as an extra match: every non-empty result was recorded one match too high, and a genuinely empty result was recorded as "1 match" instead of 0. No existing test caught this because every fixture omitted the header line — the same injected-seam trap CLAUDE.md's Critical Path section warns about. Added `estimateResultCount()`, which reads the authoritative `"Found N"`/`"No ... found"` summary line when present and falls back to the plain counter otherwise (Grep `content`/`count` mode, Glob's header-less path list). See [src/hooks_common.ts](src/hooks_common.ts), regression-tested in [tests/hooks_common.test.ts](tests/hooks_common.test.ts), [tests/hooks_grep.test.ts](tests/hooks_grep.test.ts).
- **`TYPE_KINDS` (the `token-goat types` allowlist) was missing two language-specific type-declaration kinds.** Swift's `protocol` declarations and Zig's `opaque` container declarations (indexed through the same shared code path as `struct`/`enum`/`union`) were both correctly parsed and stored in the symbol index but silently excluded from `types` output — the same allowlist-omission class already fixed once for Rust's `union`. A full audit of every `languages/*.ts` kind literal against `TYPE_KINDS` found no further gaps. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **The Gmail compression pack's quoted-reply/forwarded-history trim silently no-op'd on CRLF-formatted bodies.** `findQuotedReplyOffset`'s `"On ... wrote:"`/`"-----Original Message-----"` markers and `FORWARD_HEADER_CLUSTER_RE`'s sibling-header lines are all `$`-anchored; JS regex `$` without the `m` flag matches only the true end of string with no exception for a trailing character, so a CRLF-formatted body (routine for real email) left a trailing `\r` on every `split('\n')` line and those branches never matched — the whole trim was a no-op for any CRLF thread. Same CR-handling gap class as the earlier `stripProgress` fix. See [src/mcp_compress_packs.ts](src/mcp_compress_packs.ts), regression-tested in [tests/mcp_compress_packs.test.ts](tests/mcp_compress_packs.test.ts).
- **`tryWrapCompoundSegments`' per-segment path lacked the bare-background-operator guard its sibling `detectFromCommand` has.** Wrapping a segment ending in a bare `&` (e.g. `cd /app && npm run dev &`) reproduces the exact hang the guard exists to prevent: `spawnSync`'s piped stdio blocks on the backgrounded grandchild's inherited stdout until it exits or the wrapper's timeout kills the process tree the user wanted kept running. Currently latent (the function is exported but not yet wired into a live hook path), but the asymmetry with the identical-purpose guard on `detectFromCommand` was clearly unintentional. See [src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts](src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts), regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).

## [2.6.17] - 2026-07-22

### Added

- **`token-goat yaml-outline`/`token-goat yaml-query` for surgical YAML reads**, mirroring the existing `json-outline`/`json-query` commands. `yaml-outline <file>` shows the document's shape (type/count per node) without dumping values; `yaml-query <file> <path>` extracts one value by dotted path, including array-filter syntax (`items[status=active].name`). Multi-document YAML streams (`---`-separated) unwrap into an array before querying, reusing `json_query.ts`'s value-agnostic traversal logic rather than a second implementation. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **Shell/Bash symbol extraction (`.sh`/`.bash`).** `.sh`/`.bash` files previously fell through to a totally generic regex fallback and silently indexed to zero symbols, the same failure shape this repo's own `.tf` regression test already documented. A dedicated extractor now finds top-level functions (`function name`, `function name()`, bare POSIX `name()`, one-lined bodies) and top-level `NAME=value`/`export`/`readonly` variable assignments, correctly excluding `local` in-function assignments. Handles bash's non-C-style `#` comment rule (`${VAR#pattern}` parameter expansion is not a comment) and masks heredoc bodies so their contents are never parsed as real code. See [src/languages/bash_idx.ts](src/languages/bash_idx.ts), [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts), [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`token-goat refs --top <n>` for high-fanout symbols.** A symbol referenced in hundreds of places (e.g. a widely-extended base class) produced an unusable per-line dump under the normal `refs` output. `--top <n>` instead groups references by file (count only), ranks by fanout descending, and shows only the top N files with an explicit elision note (`...(N more files, M more references elided; use a higher --top to see more)`) rather than truncating silently. Takes precedence over `--callers` when both are set; `--json` output uses a distinct `{fileCounts, totalFiles, totalRefs, shown}` envelope reflecting the opt-in grouped shape. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **MCP compression pack for Google Workspace (Gmail/Drive)**, joining the existing GitHub and browser-automation packs. Gmail `get_thread`-style results carry an HTML-duplicated rendering of each plaintext message body, a raw MIME payload, a full quoted-reply chain repeated in every message, and inline attachment bytes — all stripped or summarized (attachments collapse to id/filename/mime type/size) before the smaller JSON is handed to the same generic table-ifying pass the other packs use. The full original result remains recoverable in full via `token-goat mcp-output <id>` exactly as with the unpacked generic path. Scoped defensively: body-trimming and attachment-summarizing only fire on specific known key names, never a bare `content` key, so a Drive `read_file_content` result is never touched. See [src/mcp_compress_packs.ts](src/mcp_compress_packs.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_compress_packs.test.ts](tests/mcp_compress_packs.test.ts).
- **`token-goat install --qwen` — Qwen Code harness bridge.** Qwen Code (QwenLM/qwen-code) is a Gemini CLI fork, but its hooks system diverged from its ancestor and now mirrors Claude Code's own natively — `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`PreCompact`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SubagentStop` event names and snake_case stdin JSON, confirmed against QwenLM/qwen-code's published docs, not Gemini's custom `BeforeTool`/`AfterTool`/`PreCompress` scheme `gemini_install.ts` uses. Writes hook entries into `~/.qwen/settings.json` with a catch-all matcher per event (Qwen's own tool-name taxonomy is only partially documented, so no per-tool matcher list is guessed at). This bridge has not been validated against a live Qwen Code install. See [src/bridges/qwen_install.ts](src/bridges/qwen_install.ts), [src/bridges/registry.ts](src/bridges/registry.ts), [src/bridges/types.ts](src/bridges/types.ts), [src/bridges_status.ts](src/bridges_status.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_qwen.test.ts](tests/install_qwen.test.ts), [tests/bridges_status.test.ts](tests/bridges_status.test.ts), [tests/bridges/registry.test.ts](tests/bridges/registry.test.ts), [tests/hook_event_harness_matrix.test.ts](tests/hook_event_harness_matrix.test.ts).
- **`token-goat commands` — machine-readable manifest of every registered CLI command.** Introspects the built Commander program into a plain-object shape (name, description, options, arguments, subcommands) instead of leaving that introspection as a test-only capability (`tests/registry.ts`). Default output is a text listing; `--json` emits the manifest for external tooling (shell completion, doc generators, scripts). `tests/registry.ts::allCommandNames` now derives from this same manifest instead of a second hand-rolled tree-walk. See [src/cli_commands.ts](src/cli_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [tests/registry.ts](tests/registry.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_commands.test.ts](tests/cli_commands.test.ts), [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`token-goat semantic`/`token-goat index` now cover PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX file content, not just source code.** These formats had no `Language` entry, so `detectLanguage()` reported `'unknown'` and both `cmdIndex`'s bulk-walk gate and the non-git `--walk` fallback (`walkProject`) silently excluded them entirely, even when git-tracked. `indexFileEmbeddings` now dispatches through the already-working pdf/docx/pptx/xlsx extraction modules (the same ones behind the read-only `pdf-read`/`docx-*`/`pptx-*`/`xlsx-*` commands) before falling through to the generic content read, so their extracted text flows into the same chunking/embedding pipeline as source files. A query like `token-goat semantic "rollout plan"` can now surface a spec PDF, design doc, deck, or spreadsheet sitting in the repo. See [src/doc_embed_extract.ts](src/doc_embed_extract.ts), [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts), [src/walk_index.ts](src/walk_index.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_embed_extract.test.ts](tests/doc_embed_extract.test.ts), [tests/embeddings_index_wiring.test.ts](tests/embeddings_index_wiring.test.ts), [tests/cmdindex_unchanged_skip.test.ts](tests/cmdindex_unchanged_skip.test.ts).
- **TaskOutput poll-delta caching hook**, mirroring the existing BashOutput redundant-resend fix — repeated polls of a running Task's output no longer resend content the model has already seen.
- **ExitPlanMode plan-body deduplication hook** — repeated echoes of the same plan body are collapsed instead of resent in full; the marker echo is verified against `tool_input.plan` before truncating, so an unrelated echo is never mistaken for the plan.
- **`WmicFilter`** collapses `wmic`'s fixed-width column padding, the same class of compression the other structured-CLI-output filters already apply.
- **Accessibility-tree snapshot compression for browser MCP results** — a11y-tree text is compressed the same way other MCP result bodies are, decoupled from read-only cache eligibility so compression fires independent of whether a result is cacheable.

### Fixed

- **`token-goat statusline` showed the full `current_dir` instead of just the project name when the payload's path used backslash separators on a non-Windows CI runner.** `buildStatuslineData` derived `project` via `path.basename(cwd)`, which uses the host platform's separator convention -- so a Windows-style `C:\Projects\token-goat` path rendered unchanged on Linux instead of extracting `token-goat`. Surfaced as a `test` (ubuntu-latest) CI failure on the v2.6.16 release; `lint` and `test-windows` had already passed. Now splits on both `/` and `\` explicitly, independent of the host platform. See [src/cli_statusline.ts](src/cli_statusline.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_statusline.test.ts](tests/cli_statusline.test.ts).
- **Symbol/parser extraction accuracy**: Kotlin extension functions/methods were never indexed (or misattributed to their receiver type); Kotlin `interface`/`object` declarations indexed as kind `class` instead of their real kind; `VAR_RE`'s `readonly`/`export` branches did not allow `getopts` flags like `declare`'s did (bash); multi-line Apex annotation argument lists now fold into the annotated member's span, counting paren depth on stripped code rather than raw source; LWC HTML templates dropped all base HTML symbols (headings, ids) behind `lwc:ref`/`c-*` extraction; `.h` files with C++ syntax now route to the cpp grammar instead of c; `extractRustSymbols` now folds leading `#[attribute]` lines into the symbol range; `extractTsJsSymbols` now folds leading `@decorator` lines on TS/JS class methods into the symbol range; `extractApex` now folds a standalone annotation line above class/interface/enum/trigger declarations into the symbol span; `parseRustBlock` no longer aborts a Rust backtrace on the first location-less frame; `isProjectFrame` no longer matches sibling directories with similar names, and no longer wrongly kept JVM `Native Method`/`Unknown Source` and .NET no-location frames; `extractGo` no longer drops Go test failure detail lines or panic/assertion detail (`extractCargo`); `extractGo`/`extractJest` now populate `statsLine`; `extractOperations` no longer duplicates a path-level parameter an operation overrides; `extractImports` gained a `.cs` branch (was returning zero results for every C# file); `pruneDeletedFiles` could wipe a file resurrected mid-scan; `token-goat deps` now resolves barrel/directory imports to `index.ts`; `tarjanSCCs` is now iterative and no longer stack-overflows on deep import chains; `coverage-report-gaps` no longer crashes on an fnMap/branchMap entry with a `loc` but no `start`; `chunkFile` no longer drops a boundary that partially overlapped a prior one.
- **Stats/dashboard tracking gaps**: `runImports` never called `recordReadStat`, so `token-goat imports` was invisible to stats/waste; the `imports` kind was missing from `stats.ts`'s `KIND_TO_SOURCE`/`COMMAND_KINDS` maps; three hint-lifecycle stat kinds were missing from `KIND_TO_SOURCE`; `runChanged` never recorded a `changed_lookup` stat; `cmdMap` (`token-goat map`) never called `recordStat`, leaving the `map_lookup` dashboard bucket permanently zero; `token-goat hot` undercounted `readCount` across sessions when a file's casing varied, and `--project` didn't fold case correctly on a case-sensitive filesystem.
- **`--json`/`totalCount` accuracy**: `token-goat symbol --json` and `token-goat refs --json` both lied about matches beyond `--limit` (SQL `LIMIT` applied before the count); `csv-query`/`sqlite-query --json --head` lied about `totalCount` the same way; `token-goat refs --top` undercounted high-fanout symbols by inheriting the 100-row per-line refs cap; `sqlite-query` silently corrupted 64-bit integers beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; `grep --json` silently dropped truncated hits with no signal.
- **Compression/filter accuracy across CLI-output filters**: `BanditFilter` leaked/duplicated the closing separator line around collapsed issue blocks; `GitDiffFilter` never honored `[bash_diff].max_hunks_per_file` for `git diff`/`show`; `CargoFilter._compressBench` dropped the running-N-tests header; `makeLanguageFilter`'s dedup key truncated to 40 chars by default, colliding distinct warnings; `TerraformFilter._compressInit` dropped its `[token-goat: ...]` wrapper when head/tail compression also fired; `LsFilter` by-type extension breakdown counted shown entries too; `stripProgress` wiped lines whose only `\r` was a trailing CRLF remnant, not a real progress overwrite; `AwsCliFilter` never truncated `aws --output table` results; `compressNpmAuditHuman` never collapsed npm audit blocks on modern npm output; `Sqlite3Filter`'s row-threshold slice ate the `.mode` column header/separator as data rows; `compressGhList` undercounted `gh pr/run/issue list` totals by mistaking the first data row for a header; `MUTATING_VERBS_RE`'s mid/trailing "run" token misclassified real read-only GitHub Actions MCP tools as mutating; `_compressEslintStanza` deferred the file header push until after body processing, reordering stylelint/rome output; `MSBuildFilter` warning dedup key omitted column, collapsing distinct diagnostics; `preReadImageHandler`'s byte-only gate missed small-file/large-dimension images.
- **Config/wiring gaps**: `config.ts`'s `ENV_KEYS` list omitted `TOKEN_GOAT_GLOB_DEDUP_MIN_MATCHES` and `TOKEN_GOAT_OCR_ENABLED`; `repomap.compact_file_threshold`, `compact_assist.max_manifest_chars`, and `compact_assist.enabled` were all dead config never wired into their consumers; `doctor`'s Worker check always inspected the real default data dir, ignoring a caller-supplied `dataDir`; `doctor --context` pregen-gap check listed a skill once per cached version instead of once; `listSkills` picked an arbitrary cached version of a skill instead of the newest, and its session filter could leak cross-session skills via unbounded prefix match.
- **Secret redaction / security**: the `curl`/`gh api` `Authorization` guard missed the `--header` long-flag spelling and the `--header=value`/`-X=`/`--method=` equals-sign spellings; `storeMcpOutput` sized cached entries off the raw pre-redaction text instead of the redacted output; `mcp_compress_packs.ts`'s quoted-reply detector only matched a bare `>` line, never real quoted content; `QUOTED_REPLY_RE`'s bare `From:` alternative silently truncated real Gmail body content.
- **Token/budget accuracy**: `pack.ts`'s local `estimateTokens` used chars/4 with no ANSI stripping (drifted from `overflow_guard.ts`'s chars/3 ratio, undercounting `token-goat pack --budget N` by 25%); `compact.ts`'s local `estimateTokens` had the same ANSI-stripping drift; `estimateBudget` under-reported token counts for files over 100KB; `token-goat tokens`/`budget` silently dropped results or crashed on large glob matches; `waste` now attributes `MultiEdit` calls to their file and no longer inflates token cost on ANSI-colorized output.
- **Surgical-read hint accuracy**: cd-prefixed `tail`/`head`/`Get-Content -Tail`/`Select-Object -First`/`cat|jq`/markdown-heading-grep/rg-structural hints suggested a path relative to the wrong directory, as did cd-prefixed `sed -n` line-range reads; quoted paths silently defeated `Get-Content -Tail`/`-First` surgical-read hints; PowerShell-wrapped `Get-Content` of a `.sql` file was denied instead of advised; `head`/`tail`/`Get-Content -Tail`/node-read hints on `.sql` files said `SectionHeading` instead of `table_name`; `classifyBashHint` no longer captures the literal `--file` flag as a bash-output correlator; `pr-slice diff:<path>` never matched a Windows-style backslash path.
- **Misc CLI correctness**: `parseClockSpec` rejects time specs with more than three colon segments; `buildTranscriptOutline` no longer crashes on very large transcripts; `hint-stats isActedOn` credited unrelated files/ids sharing a correlator prefix; `skill-diff` no longer conflates a mid-diff cache eviction with only-one-version; `dep-docs --json` now shares one overflow-guard budget across README and declarations instead of two independent ones; `test-for`/`coverage-gaps` no longer lose test refs past the 500-ref query cap; `lockdeps` mislabeled every `Pipfile.lock` dependency as `"direct"`; `Qwen Code` bridge never self-identified its harness to `detectHarness()`; `preWriteRewriteHandler` now guards an unbounded `readFileSync` before diffing the old file; `BashOutput`/`TaskOutput` poll-delta diffing desynced permanently once a secret-shaped token appeared; `token-goat trace --bodies` frame resolution and `token-goat symbol`/`refs` scoping got stronger regression assertions closing several mutation-testing coverage gaps.

### Changed

- Several DRY/dedup refactors consolidated near-duplicate logic with no behavior change: shared lazy optional-module-loader pattern (6 files), hook-relay JS block between opencode/OpenClaw bridges, `writeIfDifferent` helper, `runJsonOutline`/`runYamlOutline` and `runJsonQuery`/`runYamlQuery`, `findBlockEndLine` (proto/terraform), Grep/Glob session dedup-hint handlers, `stripJsComments` (sfc/salesforce), `packageNameDistance`/`suggestPackageNames`, stale-hook-group filtering across codex/gemini/qwen install, `stripCstyleComments`/`stripBlockCommentSpan`, `enqueueDirtyPathSafe`, `isDoc`/`isConfig` extension classification, `valueRefIdentifiers`'s default-parameter-value gap.
- Added regression/mutation-testing coverage in several previously mutation-silent areas: `chunkFile` boundary flattening, `parser.ts` yaml quote-escape and skip-dir/skip-size boundaries, `index_reader` limit enforcement, `worker.ts` `pidAlive` EPERM/ESRCH branch, `hooks_read.ts` boundary conditions, `resolvePendingHintsForEvent`'s `ACTED_ON_WINDOW` boundary, `config_commands` numeric field bounds, `overflow_guard.ts` threshold comparisons, cycle-90 targets (parser decorator walk-back, `tarjanSCCs` `onStack` guard, `runGrep` truncation boundary).

## [2.6.16] - 2026-07-18

### Added

- **`token-goat hint-stats` tracks whether discretionary hint hooks are actually followed.** Each `context`-output hint from the Bash/Read/Edit hooks (`bash_redirect`, `bash_recall`, `read_reread_dedup`, `read_structural_nav`, `edit_reread_suggest`) is mined for the specific file path or cached-output id it pointed at; a `post_tool_use` advisory handler then checks up to 5 subsequent tool calls in the same session for a Bash command that both invokes `token-goat` and references that exact correlator, crediting real follow-through rather than any unrelated token-goat call. Hints with no extractable correlator are honestly counted as emitted with no automatic "acted on" credit rather than guessed. A category is auto-suppressed per `(category, harness)` once it has at least `hint_stats.min_sample_size` emissions (default 5) and its efficacy falls below `hint_stats.suppress_threshold_pct` (default 15%), until `token-goat hint-stats --reset` clears tracked data. `--mark-effective <category>`/`--mark-ineffective <category>` record a separate manual vote that supplements but never blends into the automatic signal. Schema-version bumped 4 -> 5 (purely additive: new `hint_emissions`/`hint_manual_marks` tables). See [src/hint_stats.ts](src/hint_stats.ts), [src/cli_hint_stats.ts](src/cli_hint_stats.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts), [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts), [src/hooks_edit.ts](src/hooks_edit.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hint_stats.test.ts](tests/hint_stats.test.ts), [tests/cli_hint_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_hint_stats.test.ts).
- **Per-server MCP compression packs for GitHub and browser-automation tool results.** Layered on top of the existing generic MCP-output table-ifying pass (`src/mcp_compress.ts`, untouched): the GitHub pack (`mcp__*github*__*` tools) strips `_links`, `node_id`, `gravatar_id`, `site_admin`, and every `*_url` field except `download_url`/`git_url`/`clone_url`/`ssh_url`; the browser-automation pack (claude-in-chrome/chrome-devtools-mcp/`@playwright/mcp` console- and network-list tools) strips console `stackTrace` frames and network `requestHeaders`/`responseHeaders`/`timing`/`initiator`/`securityDetails`/cookie fields. Both hand the stripped JSON back to the generic pass for the actual table-ification, fail closed to the unmodified generic pass on any tool/shape mismatch, and reuse the existing `TOKEN_GOAT_MCP_COMPRESS=0` opt-out and full-recovery-by-id guarantee. See [src/mcp_compress_packs.ts](src/mcp_compress_packs.ts), [src/hooks_mcp.ts](src/hooks_mcp.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_compress_packs.test.ts](tests/mcp_compress_packs.test.ts).
- **`token-goat recall` — unified full-text search across every cached bash-output, web-output, and mcp-output entry.** A single `token-goat recall "<query>"` now searches all three cache types at once instead of requiring the caller to know which one holds the result. Backed by a new SQLite FTS5 index (`cache_recall`/`cache_recall_fts`, mirroring the existing `symbols_fts` pattern) that hooks into the three existing write paths (`storeBashOutput`, `storeWebOutput`, `storeMcpOutput`) so it stays current with no separate rebuild step, falling back to a substring scan if FTS5 is unavailable. `--type`/`--limit`/`--json` mirror the existing `bash-history`/`mcp-audit` conventions. See [src/recall_index.ts](src/recall_index.ts), [src/cli_recall.ts](src/cli_recall.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts); regression-tested in [tests/recall_index.test.ts](tests/recall_index.test.ts), [tests/cli_recall.test.ts](tests/cli_recall.test.ts).
- **`token-goat mcp-audit` — MCP server token-cost report.** Scans `.mcp.json` for installed MCP servers, estimates per-server token cost from cached tool calls, and correlates schema complexity against real call frequency; outputs a markdown table or `--json`. See [src/cli_mcp_audit.ts](src/cli_mcp_audit.ts); tested in [tests/cli_mcp_audit.test.ts](tests/cli_mcp_audit.test.ts).
- **`injection.enabled` is now a real scan+fence+log check, not a dead config field.** The config key was already typed, defaulted, and settable via `config get`/`config set`, and the README already documented the intended contract (every fetched page scanned for attack patterns, matches wrapped in an untrusted-content fence, one config line to disable) -- but nothing on the read side ever consumed it. `postFetchHandler` now scans every fetched body against a case-insensitive pattern set (imperative override language: "ignore previous instructions," "new instructions," "you are now," "reveal system prompt," etc.) ahead of the caching-size gate, logs matched pattern names via `recordStat('injection_detected', ...)`, and returns a fence-wrapped rewrite when patterns match; a non-match leaves the response unchanged. See [src/injection_scan.ts](src/injection_scan.ts), [src/hooks_fetch.ts](src/hooks_fetch.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts](tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts).
- **A batch of seven `hints.*` config fields were fully wired on the write side (typed, defaulted, validated, echoed by `config get`/`config set`) but had zero read-side consumer, so setting them silently did nothing.** All seven now actually govern hook behavior: `hints.git_hint_max_ms` bounds the two synchronous git calls behind `hooks_session.ts`'s branch-name and uncommitted-changes advisories; `hints.grep_dedup_min_matches` powers a new Grep dedup-hint pair (`src/hooks_grep.ts`) that advises on an identical repeat once the prior match count clears the threshold; `hints.context_threshold_advisory` appends a tier-aware "Context pressure: hot/critical" note to the large-file structural-nav hint; `hints.pre_skill_advisory` gates both `preSkillHandler` denies in `hooks_skill.ts`; `hints.protect_recent_reads` exempts the N most-recently-read files from the re-read-deny hints in `hooks_read.ts`; `hints.min_file_lines_for_hint` and `hints.truncated_read_min_lines` gate the surgical-read suggestion and the truncated-read deny below a configured line count; `hints.quiet_hours` (`"HH:MM-HH:MM"`, wraps past midnight) degrades every advisory hint to a pass-through during the configured window while leaving correctness-relevant denies untouched; and `hints.diff_hint_min_tokens_saved` replaces a hardcoded 0.6 length-ratio diff-savings guard (source files only) with a configured token-savings floor applied uniformly to both doc and source files. See [src/hooks_session.ts](src/hooks_session.ts), [src/hooks_grep.ts](src/hooks_grep.ts), [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts), [src/hooks_skill.ts](src/hooks_skill.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested across [tests/hooks_session.test.ts](tests/hooks_session.test.ts), [tests/hooks_grep.test.ts](tests/hooks_grep.test.ts), [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts), [tests/hooks_skill.test.ts](tests/hooks_skill.test.ts), [tests/util.test.ts](tests/util.test.ts).
- **`token-goat memory`'s duplicate-cluster detection now has a real embedding path instead of always falling back to Jaccard.** The Python-to-TS port dropped the embedding/cosine-similarity branch of `findContentDuplicates` entirely ("not implemented in this port; skip gracefully"), leaving `DupCluster.method: 'embedding'` a type that could never occur in practice. Recovered the pre-port Python source to confirm the Jaccard fallback's own 0.60 threshold was always correct and unaffected; the embedding path now runs through the existing `embeddings.ts` module (already used for semantic search/indexing), gated on `indexing.embeddings_enabled` the same way the rest of the codebase gates it. See [src/memory_prune.ts](src/memory_prune.ts); regression-tested in [tests/memory_prune.test.ts](tests/memory_prune.test.ts).
- **`cache-audit` now flags a suspiciously small `indexing.large_file_skip_kb`.** The existing `constants.ts` guard for this only fires inside a Vitest worker, so it could not catch a config already corrupted by a stray manual `config set` or an external agent outside a test run -- which is how this repo's own `config.toml` actually ended up at `large_file_skip_kb=1`, silently skipping indexing on nearly every real source file with no error anywhere. `cache-audit` now surfaces it directly with a fix command. See [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts](tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts).
- **Inline browser-automation screenshots are now compressed, and repeated `Tab Context` boilerplate is deduplicated.** `mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer` and `browser_batch` return raw, full-resolution base64 screenshots in-band with no destination-file option, bypassing both the screenshot-redirect guard (name doesn't match `*screenshot*`) and the MCP read-only cache/compress pipeline (they're mutating tools). A new `post_tool_use` hook shrinks each inline image block via the existing `image_shrink.ts` pipeline and collapses a repeated `Tab Context:` listing (appended to nearly every call, often unchanged) to a placeholder once it has been seen unchanged this session. Also fixes a latent bug where the new session-state field tracking the last-seen `Tab Context` never survived a save/load round-trip across separate hook processes (the same "session-state field needs touch points beyond its own definition" bug class as the earlier `bashReruns` fix), which made the dedup inert in practice even though it worked correctly in-process. See [src/hooks_browser_image.ts](src/hooks_browser_image.ts), [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_browser_image.test.ts](tests/hooks_browser_image.test.ts), [tests/session_store.test.ts](tests/session_store.test.ts).
- **Oversized Agent (subagent) reports are now cached for later recall.** A mining pass over real session transcripts found Agent tool results were the third-largest uncovered `tool_result` category with no `post_tool_use` hook at all. Since a subagent report is already-distilled prose with no safe lossless way to shrink it, the new handler only appends a recall pointer (via `contextOutput`) for reports at or above 8000 characters -- the original result always reaches the parent untouched; typical reports (~2,220 chars average) are unaffected. See [src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts](src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts), [src/hooks_common.ts](src/hooks_common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts](tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts).
- **Agent (subagent-spawn) tool calls now get a compact briefing pack appended to their prompt.** A new `PreToolUse` handler scoped to the Agent tool appends a one-line project-map summary, 2-3 recent cached-output IDs as reuse hints, and a one-line surgical-read reminder, budgeted to roughly 300 tokens. Fails open (passes the prompt through unchanged) if briefing construction fails for any reason. See [src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts](src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts](tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts).
- **`token-goat safeSlice` truncation is now shared and covers `resume.ts`.** `bash_compress.ts` and `overflow_guard.ts` each defined a byte-identical private `safeSlice` (UTF-16 surrogate-pair-safe truncation, see the 2.6.2 entry below); extracted to `util.ts` and reused by both. `resume.ts`'s `buildResumePacket` truncated its final output with a plain `text.slice()`, which can split a surrogate pair at the cut boundary and produce a malformed string -- switched it to the shared `safeSlice` too. See [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), [src/resume.ts](src/resume.ts); regression-tested in [tests/util.test.ts](tests/util.test.ts).
- **`context-stats --fix` is now confirm-gated, matching `memory --fix`.** Previously wrote to `MEMORY.md` unconditionally with no diff preview and no escape hatch. `context-stats --fix` now routes its prune through the same `confirmAndApply` gate `memory --fix` already used, showing a diff and requiring `--yes`/`-y` (new flag) or an interactive y/n before writing; `pruneIndex` gained a `dryRun` pass so the diff can be built before anything is written. See [src/cli_context_stats.ts](src/cli_context_stats.ts), [src/memory_prune.ts](src/memory_prune.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_context_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_context_stats.test.ts).
- **`doctor --context` no longer silently swallows an error as an unhandled promise rejection.** Its `--context` path called the now-`async` `runContextStats` (made async by the `context-stats --fix` confirm-gating fix above) without awaiting it, so a throw during `runContextStats`'s synchronous prefix became a silently unhandled rejection instead of `doctor`'s normal clean error path. `runDoctorAndExit` and its `cmdDoctor` caller are now properly `async`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_doctor.test.ts](tests/cli_doctor.test.ts).
- **`getWebOutputByUrlFromDisk` now accepts an optional `dedupKey`, matching `storeWebOutput`'s own signature.** It previously always recomputed `cacheIdForUrl(url)`, only correct when an entry was stored under `storeWebOutput`'s default `dedupKey = url` (see the 2.6.0 entry below). A caller storing under a composite dedup key (e.g. `hooks_fetch.ts`'s `${url}\x00${prompt}`) would derive the wrong id and silently miss an entry that exists on disk -- currently unreachable in production since `gdrive.ts`, the only real caller, always uses the default, but latent for the next caller. See [src/web_cache.ts](src/web_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/content_cache_disk.test.ts](tests/content_cache_disk.test.ts).
- **`token-goat pr-slice <pr>` -- surgical GitHub PR reads.** Extracts one slice of a PR (diff for one file, a single review-comment thread, the description, or CI check statuses) via `gh` instead of pulling the whole PR payload into context. See [src/pr_slice.ts](src/pr_slice.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pr_slice.test.ts](tests/pr_slice.test.ts).
- **Per-project `.token-goat.toml` config overrides.** A project-root `.token-goat.toml` now layers on top of the global `~/.token-goat/config.toml`, so a repo can override hint thresholds, indexing settings, etc. without touching global config; `config get`/`config set` report which layer a value actually resolved from. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/constants.ts](src/constants.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config.test.ts](tests/config.test.ts).
- **`token-goat bridges-status` -- parity matrix across every supported harness/bridge.** Reports which hooks/commands are wired for Claude Code, Codex, opencode, openclaw, Grok, etc. side by side, and the Codex install path now wires hooks it was previously missing. See [src/bridges_status.ts](src/bridges_status.ts), [src/bridges/codex_install.ts](src/bridges/codex_install.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/bridges_status.test.ts](tests/bridges_status.test.ts), [tests/install_codex.test.ts](tests/install_codex.test.ts).
- **`token-goat statusline` -- a Claude Code statusline command surfacing session stats (bytes saved, hint efficacy, cache hit rate) inline in the terminal.** See [src/cli_statusline.ts](src/cli_statusline.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_statusline.test.ts](tests/cli_statusline.test.ts).
- **Secrets are now redacted at the `storeBlob` choke point.** Every cached bash/web/mcp output passes through a pattern-based secret scan (API keys, tokens, private key blocks, etc.) before being written to disk, so a cached command output can't leak a credential into a later `bash-output`/`recall` read. See [src/secret_redact.ts](src/secret_redact.ts), [src/disk_cache.ts](src/disk_cache.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/secret_redact.test.ts](tests/secret_redact.test.ts), [tests/disk_cache.test.ts](tests/disk_cache.test.ts).
- **Terraform/HCL language adapter.** A regex/brace-counting extractor (mirroring the existing `proto_idx.ts` pattern, since no maintained tree-sitter grammar package exists for HCL) indexes `resource`/`data`/`variable`/`output`/`module`/`provider`/`locals` blocks, so `symbol`/`read`/`outline`/`skeleton` work on `.tf` files. See [src/languages/terraform_idx.ts](src/languages/terraform_idx.ts), [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts), [src/languages/index.ts](src/languages/index.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts), [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`token-goat coverage-report-gaps <file>` -- extracts uncovered lines/branches/functions from an LCOV or Istanbul coverage report.** Auto-detects format (LCOV `TN:`/`SF:` signature vs. Istanbul `statementMap`+`s` "final" vs. aggregate-only "summary" shape), collapses consecutive uncovered lines into ranges, drops fully-covered files, and supports `--file`/`--json`. See [src/coverage_query.ts](src/coverage_query.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/coverage_query.test.ts](tests/coverage_query.test.ts).
- **Duplicate-subagent-spawn detection on the `Agent` tool's pre-hook.** Tracks outstanding subagent-spawn prompts for the session and, when a new spawn's prompt is a near-duplicate (word-set Jaccard similarity >= 0.75) of one still outstanding, appends an advisory noting the likely-duplicate work rather than silently letting two agents redo the same task. See [src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts](src/hooks_agent_spawn.ts), [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts](tests/hooks_agent_spawn.test.ts).
- **Whitespace/EOL-only diff hunks are now collapsed in the git-diff tool filter.** A hunk collapses to a one-line marker only when every removed/added line pairs up and is byte-identical once all whitespace is stripped (which also naturally catches a CRLF-vs-LF flip, since `\r` is whitespace); any non-whitespace-only pair or count mismatch leaves the whole hunk untouched. Directly fixes the "an external tool flips a file's line endings, inflating its diff 15x with pure noise" failure mode. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`token-goat trace --bodies` resolves each stack-trace frame to its enclosing symbol's code body.** Reuses the exact same symbol-resolution (`querySymbols` + `enclosingSymbol`) and body-rendering (`resolveBody`) machinery `token-goat scope`/`read`/`symbol` already use, so a traceback becomes directly readable without a separate lookup per frame. An unresolvable frame gets the same graceful miss message `scope` already uses; a repeated frame (recursion) shows its body once with `(same as above)` on repeats. Purely additive -- the default (non-`--bodies`) output is byte-for-byte unchanged. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/trace_bodies_e2e.test.ts](tests/trace_bodies_e2e.test.ts).
- **`token-goat conflicts [path]` -- surgical read for unresolved git merge-conflict markers.** Parses two-way (`<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>`) and diff3 three-way (`<<<<<<< / ||||||| / ======= / >>>>>>>`) conflict regions out of a file, or scans the whole project (via the existing `walkProject` walker) when no path is given, and surfaces only the conflicted files/regions -- line range, side labels, and ours/base/theirs content -- instead of a full `Read` of a possibly-huge file. `--summary` narrows each region to its line range and labels; malformed/unbalanced markers are surfaced as per-file warnings rather than thrown errors. See [src/conflict_query.ts](src/conflict_query.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/conflict_query.test.ts](tests/conflict_query.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **`curlDownloads` session-state merge could resurrect a download record a process had explicitly cleared.** The shared `mergePairs` helper is a blind union of disk and in-memory entries with no way to represent "this process deleted this key" -- so a stale in-memory view from a process that loaded before another process called `clearCurlDownload` could resurrect the cleared entry on save. Added a load-time snapshot + tombstone merge (`mergeCurlDownloads`), mirroring the existing `pendingLargeFileHints`/`outstandingAgentSpawns` pattern; fields with no real removal path (`bashOutputs`, `webFetches`, `grepQueries`, `globQueries`) are unaffected. See [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts); regression-tested in [tests/session_store.test.ts](tests/session_store.test.ts).
- **A `curl -o` download recall resolved the saved file's relative path against the wrong working directory.** The recorded path was stored as written on the command line (often relative) and re-resolved against whatever cwd the *next* matching command happened to run from, rather than the cwd it was actually downloaded from -- a same-named file in a different directory could shadow the real download. Now stores the already-resolved absolute path at record time. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **`openapi-outline`/`openapi-op` and `coverage-report-gaps` failed to parse a UTF-8 BOM-prefixed `.json` file.** Common from Windows editors; the BOM byte is valid content but broke a strict `JSON.parse`. Added a shared `stripBom` helper. See [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), [src/openapi_query.ts](src/openapi_query.ts), [src/coverage_query.ts](src/coverage_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/openapi_query.test.ts](tests/openapi_query.test.ts), [tests/coverage_query.test.ts](tests/coverage_query.test.ts).
- **`coverage-report-gaps --file` was case-sensitive on case-insensitive filesystems.** `filterCoverageGapsByFile` only ran paths through `normalizePath` (which case-folds the drive letter only), so a case-differing query missed a real match on Windows/macOS. Now reuses the existing platform-gated `foldPath` helper already used for the same problem elsewhere in the codebase. See [src/coverage_query.ts](src/coverage_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/coverage_query.test.ts](tests/coverage_query.test.ts).

## [2.6.15] - 2026-07-12

### Added

- **The background worker daemon now restarts itself if it dies.** `startDetachedWorker()` was previously only ever invoked from `token-goat worker start` -- a crash, manual kill, or sleep/wake race left the daemon dead indefinitely, so the dirty queue kept growing and `read`/`symbol`/`section`/`skeleton`/`outline` served stale index content with no recovery until someone noticed and restarted it by hand. `ensureWorkerAlive()` now checks liveness and respawns the daemon from the hot edit-hook path (`postEditHandler`), rate-limited via a marker-file mtime so a burst of edits doesn't retrigger the check on every call. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/hooks_edit.ts](src/hooks_edit.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`read`/`outline`/`skeleton`/`symbol` now warn when the index is stale relative to the on-disk file.** Indexed content may lag behind edited files while the background worker drains the dirty-queue. These commands now hash the on-disk file before serving content and prepend a one-line warning if the hash differs from the stored sha256, pointing to retry or read-directly options. Served content is unchanged -- only the new warning is added. Reuses existing `files.sha` and `fingerprintFile` from the worker. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **Added `stats --short` to force the rich KPI view over a pipe, overriding TTY/CI detection.** Bare `token-goat stats` picks between rich KPI rendering and flat plain-text totals based on `process.stdout.isTTY`. Agents invoking via pipe had no TTY and always got the flat view. `--short` bypasses the TTY/CI check (NO_COLOR still wins) and forces the rich KPI view regardless of stdout connection, available on both bare and `--full` invocations. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_stats.test.ts), [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts).
- **`gdrive-sections` now accepts a `--fresh` flag to bypass on-disk cache.** `fetchDoc` previously always served the cached document first with no way to refresh, making edits to live Google Docs invisible for up to 24 hours. `--fresh` forces a live fetch while still writing the result back to cache afterward for the default cache-miss behavior. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **`project prune --dry-run` now reports blocked roots without touching config.** Adds `--dry-run` to the CLI's project command and threads it through `cmdProject`'s prune branch, reporting which blocked roots would be removed without modifying config.toml. Also corrects two flags the README claimed but the CLI never implemented: `install --dry-run`/`install --verify` (install has real side effects, left as a doc fix) and `uninstall --purge` (uninstall never deletes the data directory). See [README.md](README.md), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **`token-goat memory --analyze` and `--fix` now surface CLAUDE.md duplicates and overlaps.** Wires previously-uncalled memory_prune.ts analysis functions (`auditClaudeMd`, `findContentDuplicates`) and `findClaudeMdFiles` into a new `token-goat memory` command that reports exact-duplicate lines, duplicate headings, and cross-file content overlaps across project CLAUDE.md files and auto-memory siblings; `--fix` applies only mechanical exact-duplicate-line removal and gates all changes via a new `confirmAndApply()` helper supporting `--yes` (non-interactive), TTY y/n prompts, or dry-run refusal. See [src/cli_memory.ts](src/cli_memory.ts), [src/confirm_apply.ts](src/confirm_apply.ts); tested in [tests/cli_memory.test.ts](tests/cli_memory.test.ts), [tests/confirm_apply.test.ts](tests/confirm_apply.test.ts).
- **`token-goat waste` command reports per-tool token cost from Claude Code transcripts.** Parses the most-recent session transcript (JSONL), attributes token cost per tool call via `estimateTokens`, and flags two waste signals: files Read once and never referenced, and Bash commands run repeatedly without hitting the bash-output cache. Supports `--transcript`, `--top`, and `--json` flags. See [src/cli_waste.ts](src/cli_waste.ts), [src/waste.ts](src/waste.ts); tested in [tests/waste.test.ts](tests/waste.test.ts), [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`bash-output` cache now folds repeat-command deltas to avoid re-absorbing full outputs unchanged.** When an exact repeat command's fresh output differs from what's cached under the same key, a short `[token-goat: delta]` hint summarizes the change instead of the full output, while the new output remains stored and fully recallable via `bash-output <id>`. See [src/bash_output_cache.ts](src/bash_output_cache.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); tested in [tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts](tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts).
- **`compact` manifest now includes a `SAFE_TO_DISCARD` section naming recoverable prior context.** Tracks three conservative classes of prior context that can be safely dropped because they're already recoverable: superseded identical-command bash reruns, file reads followed by edits/rewrites of the same file, and all other cached bash output (each recallable via `bash-output <id>`). Each entry names its item count and recall command -- the section never claims data is gone, only that the inline transcript copy duplicates something accessible. See [src/hooks_compact.ts](src/hooks_compact.ts), [src/session.ts](src/session.ts); tested in [tests/hooks_compact.test.ts](tests/hooks_compact.test.ts).
- **`baseline --suggest-mem` flag identifies preference-shaped bullets eligible for memory import.** Scans the project's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files for preference/decision bullets outside structural headings and outside must-enforce directive headings (MANDATORY/REQUIRED/CRITICAL/NEVER/ALWAYS), then advises `mem import --from-md <path>` for each file with eligible content. Advisory only -- never invokes `mem` or writes anything. See [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts), [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts); tested in [tests/baseline.test.ts](tests/baseline.test.ts).
- **`compact` manifest folds mem epoch into the manifest on supported systems.** When the `mem` binary is on PATH, shells out to `mem epoch` with an 800ms timeout and folds the result into a new `### mem epoch` section, so a resumed session can detect whether mem's fact store advanced since the transcript was captured. Fails open on every failure mode (absent, timeout, unparsable); never throws or blocks the manifest. See [src/hooks_compact.ts](src/hooks_compact.ts); tested in [tests/hooks_compact.test.ts](tests/hooks_compact.test.ts).
- **`HookOutput` now supports a `rewriteOutput` variant for Claude Code's `updatedToolOutput` mechanism.** Adds a `rewriteOutput` field to `HookOutput` (types.ts) and its `serializeOutput` case in hook_registry.ts, emitting the MCP-spec `hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput` format. Includes a trivial pass-through spike handler in hooks_mcp.ts (gated behind `TOKEN_GOAT_MCP_REWRITE_SPIKE=1`), live-confirmed against Claude Code v2.1.201. See [src/types.ts](src/types.ts), [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts), [src/hooks_mcp.ts](src/hooks_mcp.ts); tested in [tests/hook_registry.test.ts](tests/hook_registry.test.ts), [tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts](tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **The shared `global.db` index had no automatic recovery for dead file rows.** `pruneDeletedFiles` only ever ran via the manual `token-goat index` CLI command, so a machine that never ran it could accumulate stale symbol/ref/chunk rows for deleted files indefinitely. Every edit hook now records its project root into a new `known_roots` table (throttled to once an hour), and the worker sweeps known roots once a day, pruning dead rows for roots that still resolve on disk. A root that goes unreachable -- drive unmounted, project deleted -- gets a 7-day grace period before it's fully pruned and forgotten, rather than being pruned immediately or skipped forever; a root where more than half its rows (and at least 20) would be deleted in one pass is flagged and skipped instead, in case a mount point inside it is only temporarily offline. Both mechanisms are purely additive to the schema and run automatically from the existing worker loop, so anyone upgrading gets them with no migration step. See [src/index_prune.ts](src/index_prune.ts), [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/hooks_edit.ts](src/hooks_edit.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts); regression-tested in [tests/index_prune.test.ts](tests/index_prune.test.ts) and [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`hints.reread_deny` and `reread_deny_min_bytes` were configurable but never enforced.** Both keys were defined, validated, persisted, and displayed by `config.ts`, but the real re-read deny logic in `hooks_read.ts`'s `preReadHandler` (truncated-file deny, markdown second-read deny, count-based deny, size-based deny) fired unconditionally, gated only by a hardcoded 50KB constant that ignored both settings. All four deny branches are now gated on `hints.reread_deny`, and the size-based deny uses the configured `reread_deny_min_bytes` in place of the removed constant; its default is bumped from 2048 to 51200 bytes to match the old hardcoded value, so wiring it up as the real gate doesn't silently change default behavior for existing users. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts).
- **`context-for`/`ask` no longer silently miss on multi-word natural-language queries.** `searchSymbolsFts` joined every query word with implicit FTS5 AND, so realistic phrases failed unless one symbol contained every word verbatim. Now retries with an OR-joined query when the AND-joined search returns zero rows, widening recall only when the strict match is empty (chosen over unconditional OR to keep ranking precise). `runContextFor` now emits "No matches found" and exits 1 on zero hits instead of printing nothing and exiting 0; `runAsk` degrades to pointers instead of invoking an LLM backend with an empty snippet block (which risked hallucinated answers). `runContextFor`'s `--budget` loop now skips oversized hits with `continue` instead of `break`, so one large hit no longer blanks the rest of the result set. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/index_reader.ts](src/index_reader.ts); tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/embeddings_index_wiring.test.ts](tests/embeddings_index_wiring.test.ts), [tests/semantic_embeddings_e2e.test.ts](tests/semantic_embeddings_e2e.test.ts).
- **Corrupt config.toml now warns instead of silently reverting to defaults.** `loadConfig()` treated TOML parse failures the same as missing files, falling back silently. Both loaders now record parse errors via `getLastConfigParseError()`; the CLI's per-command guard emits a stderr warning pointing at `config validate`. `config set` against corrupt config.toml used to overwrite it outright, destroying the original; it now backs up to config.toml.bak first. `config validate` always exited 0 regardless of findings, making it useless as a script/CI gate -- now sets `process.exitCode = 1` whenever findings exist, in both human-readable and `--json` modes. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts), [tests/config.test.ts](tests/config.test.ts), [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **Concurrent embedding pipelines are now capped at `worker.max_pool_workers` (default 4).** `processDirtyBatch` fired `indexFileEmbeddings` for every changed file without awaiting, so a batch of N changed files could spawn N concurrent transformer-inference pipelines at once with no cap, spiking CPU/memory. `embedFileSerialized` now claims a slot from a global counter before dispatching, queueing callers beyond the cap for FIFO dispatch as running embeds finish. Also exports `pendingEmbeddings()` so callers needing work to have actually settled (not just started) can await it instead of guessing timing. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts), [tests/salesforce_worker_e2e.test.ts](tests/salesforce_worker_e2e.test.ts).
- **Stats output now signals when hints fired but no commands were run.** When `by_command` is empty but `by_source` has hint events, the plain-text and TTY renderers now emit an explicit note stating the exact count of hints fired with zero direct command invocations, surfacing the gap between passive hook savings and active surgical-read savings. See [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts), [src/render/stats_renderer.ts](src/render/stats_renderer.ts); regression-tested in [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts), [tests/render.test.ts](tests/render.test.ts).
- **JSON output now capped by `guardJsonRows`, ANSI codes stripped on non-TTY pipes, and bare `token-goat map` recognized in dedup.** Uncapped `--json` paths (csv-query, imports, list-sections, changed) are now wrapped in the same `{ items, truncated, totalCount }` envelope as other guarded commands; stdout writers strip ANSI codes when output is piped or redirected; and the surgical-read session dedup now recognizes bare/flag-only `token-goat map` invocations. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts).
- **`config set` now uses a 15s lock wait budget instead of 2s, closing a corruption risk under concurrent hook writes.** `applySet` in config_commands.ts used the default 2s `LOCK_WAIT_MS` timeout, and on timeout fell through to an unprotected read-modify-write -- the exact race this lock exists to prevent. Extracted the 15s `LOCK_WAIT_MS_HARDENED` constant already applied to session_store.ts into a shared util.ts constant and applied it to both call sites. See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **`csv-query --json` test updated for the `guardJsonRows` envelope.** See [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`appendDirtyPath` no longer opens the full index DB on every edit hook.** `appendDirtyPath` called `resetTransientRetryCount`, which opens a database connection (WAL pragma, FTS triggers, sqlite-vec extension load) just to run a no-op retry-counter reset on every single edit hook. `processDirtyBatch` already clears the counter on every successful read during a drain, so the append-time reset is redundant. See [src/hooks_index.ts](src/hooks_index.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_index.test.ts](tests/hooks_index.test.ts).
- **Worker batch processing now memoizes project lookups and serializes embedding runs per file.** `processDirtyBatch` re-ran a full `findProject` ancestor-marker walk for every dirty path instead of memoizing it per distinct dirname; and `indexFileEmbeddings` calls could run concurrently for the same path, allowing older stale chunks to overwrite fresher ones. Fixed via per-batch project memoization and per-file embedding serialization. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`removeFileFromIndex` now wraps both deletes in a transaction, preventing orphaned index rows.** `deleteFileRows` and `deleteFileEmbeddings` ran without a transaction, leaving orphaned chunks/chunk_vectors rows if a crash occurred between them -- `pruneDeletedFiles` cannot clean these since it only iterates paths still in the files table. See [src/index_prune.ts](src/index_prune.ts); regression-tested in [tests/index_prune.test.ts](tests/index_prune.test.ts).
- **Worker daemon lifecycle hardened: `stopWorker` re-guards pid-file delete, and transient retries no longer double-bump within a cycle.** `stopWorker` deleted the pid file unconditionally, risking orphaning a new daemon's pid if a concurrent worker start reclaimed it between the kill and delete -- now re-reads the pid file immediately before delete and only removes it if it still names the killed pid. Additionally, `drainOnce`'s stage (a) requeued transient failures to the live dirty.txt which stage (b) then immediately reclaimed and reprocessed, double-bumping the retry counter and halving the effective retry budget; retry append is now deferred until after both stages complete. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **Graph commands now scope correctly to project root, hoist the file-symbol cache, and surface module-scope impact references.** `resolveCallers`, `runCallChain`, and `runImpact` queried the shared global.db without a `rootDir` parameter, allowing same-named symbols from unrelated projects to leak into results; both `runCallChain` and `runImpact` rebuilt the file-symbol cache on every BFS node instead of once before the loop; and `runImpact` silently dropped module-scope references instead of surfacing them as file-level entries like `resolveCallers` does. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **Project scoping now resolves to the actual project root, FTS search is project-scoped, and MCP `projectRoot` is validated.** `graph_commands.ts` and `read_commands.ts` fed raw `process.cwd()` into `projectScopeClause`, so running a command from a subdirectory silently narrowed the scope to that subtree instead of the whole project; `searchSymbolsFts` took no `rootDir` parameter at all, allowing full-text searches to leak across every project in the machine-wide global.db (the default fallback path on installs without sqlite-vec); and the MCP `semantic` tool accepted invalid `projectRoot` values and returned empty results with `isError: false`. Now uses `resolveProjectRoot` on all cwd-based scopes, threads `rootDir` through FTS search call sites, and validates MCP `projectRoot` as absolute and existing. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/index_reader.ts](src/index_reader.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/mcp_server_semantic_projectroot_validation.test.ts](tests/mcp_server_semantic_projectroot_validation.test.ts), [tests/semantic_fts_fallback_project_scope.test.ts](tests/semantic_fts_fallback_project_scope.test.ts).
