- **`symbol` and `semantic` now reject `limit: 0` with an explicit error instead of returning a false "no matches".** SQL `LIMIT 0` always returns zero rows, so passing `limit: 0` falsely reported a symbol didn't exist even when it genuinely did. CLI handlers and MCP schemas now require a positive limit and reject non-positive values. See [src/mcp_server.ts](src/mcp_server.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_server.test.ts](tests/mcp_server.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/semantic_limit_zero_rejected.test.ts](tests/semantic_limit_zero_rejected.test.ts).
- **Kotlin companion objects, PHP `final const`, and PowerShell scoped function names were dropped from the index.** Kotlin's `companion object` headers never matched `CLASS_HEADER_RE` because the `companion` keyword wasn't in its modifier list; PHP's `CONST_RE` allowed only one modifier and didn't include `final`, silently skipping PHP 8.1+ constants; PowerShell's function-name regex excluded `:`, so `function global:prompt { }` indexed the scope qualifier as the function name instead. Fixed by adding a companion-object regex for Kotlin (using "Companion" when unnamed), allowing multiple modifiers including `final` in PHP, and including `:` in PowerShell function names. See [src/languages/kotlin.ts](src/languages/kotlin.ts), [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts).
- **Files were permanently re-embedded on every index run, or false-stamped as embedded when they weren't.** Three related bugs on the embedding path: policy-skipped files (over 512KB or metadata-excluded) called `deleteFileEmbeddings` but never stamped `files.embed_sha`, so the freshness gate never held and the multi-megabyte content was re-read forever; when optional embedding deps were absent, `embedIndexFile` skipped embedding but still stamped `embed_sha = sha`, so users who indexed first then installed the model later found the semantic index permanently empty; `chunkVectorsTableExists` probed only sqlite_master, not whether the vec0 module was actually loaded, so reinstalling without sqlite-vec would crash `searchSemantic` and leak deleted files' rows from the transaction. Fixed by stamping the real sha in all three branches, returning an `EmbedOutcome` with an `unavailable` marker for deps-absent cases (refreshing once deps become usable), and probing actual vec0 usability instead of just the table name. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts).
- **Markdown headings with a bare trailing # (like `## C#`) were truncated in the index and section hints.** `parser.ts`'s heading regex stripped a trailing `#` even with no whitespace before it, violating CommonMark and indexing "C#" as "C"; `markdown_hints.ts` never stripped closing hashes at all, so "## Setup ##" produced hint text "Setup ##" that then failed to resolve. Both now require whitespace before closing hashes, matching `section_reader.ts`'s already-correct rule. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser_markdown_closing_hash.test.ts](tests/parser_markdown_closing_hash.test.ts), [tests/markdown_hints.test.ts](tests/markdown_hints.test.ts).
- **`token-goat semantic` from project subdirectories silently scoped searches to that subtree instead of the project root.** `runSemantic` defaulted its scope to `opts.projectRoot ?? process.cwd()`, whereas earlier commits fixed the same raw-cwd-vs-project-root pattern for `runFind` and `queryRefCounts` via `resolveProjectRoot`. Now resolves `runSemantic` the same way, matching those call sites. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/semantic_fts_fallback_project_scope.test.ts](tests/semantic_fts_fallback_project_scope.test.ts).
- **`token-goat brief` on HTML/Liquid heading symbols showed blank bodies and ~0 token estimates.** Symbols with empty stored bodies are created by design (by `sectionsToHeadingSymbols`), and both `runRead` and `runSymbol` already re-read from disk when `body` is empty, but `runBrief` had no fallback. Extracted the duplicated fallback logic into a shared `resolveBody` helper and call it from all three read surfaces. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **The `-j` short flag was not recognized for `stats` and `context-stats`.** Both commands registered `.option('--json', ...)` instead of the `-j, --json` form used by ~55 other commands. Fixed by adding the `-j` short form to match the standard CLI convention. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **PowerShell and Apex files were never pointed at skeleton/outline in re-read denies.** `SOURCE_EXT_RE` and `DIFFABLE_SOURCE_RE` are hand-maintained duplicates of `EXTENSION_LANGUAGE` and had drifted after the PowerShell and Apex adapters were added, so the count-based re-read deny never recognized `.ps1`, `.psm1`, `.cls`, or `.trigger` extensions. `DIFFABLE_SOURCE_RE` also still listed Swift, which has no adapter. Fixed by syncing both regexes and dropping the stale Swift entry. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **Project memory was stored in an orphaned path on Windows, outside every tool's reach.** `memoryPath()` hand-rolled its own `XDG_DATA_HOME`/homedir resolution instead of using the shared platform-aware `dataDir()` resolver, landing project memory in `~/.local/share/token-goat/projects` on Windows (a path that `dataDir()`-based tools never checked) and skipping `safeEnvDir`'s validation against crafted env vars. Fixed by using `dataDir()` directly; constants.ts is a dependency-free leaf module, so the old circular-dependency concern was stale. See [src/project_memory.ts](src/project_memory.ts); regression-tested in [tests/project_memory.test.ts](tests/project_memory.test.ts).
- **HTTP request headers (API keys, auth) could be leaked across redirects to different hosts.** The redirect recursion in `performHttpFetch` forwarded `{...opts}` verbatim, including `requestHeaders`, to whatever host the `Location` header pointed at. No current caller sets `requestHeaders`, but the first one adding an `Authorization` or API-key header would silently leak it cross-origin. Fixed to only forward `requestHeaders` when the redirect target's host matches the original request's host. See [src/webfetch.ts](src/webfetch.ts); regression-tested in [tests/webfetch.test.ts](tests/webfetch.test.ts).
- **Path normalization was inconsistent in retry count functions, and its doc comment was stale.** The doc comment in `sql_path.ts` claimed `files.path` stored the raw path exactly as written, but every actual writer normalizes before queuing. `bumpRetryCount` and `clearRetryCount` only worked because every current caller happened to pre-normalize; a future caller passing a native backslash path would silently miss the existing row and always insert. Fixed by normalizing defensively inside both functions and correcting the comment to state the actual invariant. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **Multiple `/*` comments on one line were ignored if the first one contained an odd quote.** `stripCstyleComments` and `stripBlockCommentSpan` called `isInsideStringLiteral` without a starting offset, rescanning the whole line from column 0 each time. A stripped comment earlier on the same line (e.g., `"it's fine"`) could leave an odd quote count that made a later real `/*` look like it was inside a string, preventing recognition as a comment opener. Fixed by adding an optional `from` offset to `isInsideStringLiteral` (default 0, unaffecting other callers) and passing the current scan position from both call sites. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages_common.test.ts](tests/languages_common.test.ts).
- **HTML `id=` and `class=` attributes were matched inside longer attribute names, and duplicate symbols were never deduplicated.** `ID_RE` and `CLASS_RE` had no left boundary, falsely matching `data-id=`, `data-testid=`, `gid=`, and `data-class=`; the same unboundaried pattern was inlined in heading-anchor extraction, so `<h2 data-id="x">` registered a false anchor. Minified HTML could emit thousands of duplicate rows per file. Fixed by requiring proper left boundaries via negative lookbehind on all three sites, deduping symbols by (name, line), and capping at 500 per file (matching `MAX_SYMBOLS` used elsewhere). See [src/languages/html.ts](src/languages/html.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **PHP symbol kind misclassified when the declared name is a substring of the keyword.** `CLASS_RE` extracted kind from the text after splitting by name, which could corrupt the keyword when the name itself appeared within it (e.g., "interface face" split by "face" mangled the keyword). `CLASS_RE` now captures keyword and name as separate regex groups. See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **C# method definitions misclassified due to generic return types, missing readonly modifier, and hardcoded class kind.** `METHOD_RE`'s name-suffix pattern allowed a generic return type to anchor a phantom capture, readonly fields were missing from modifier patterns so `readonly Dictionary<...> Handlers` got captured as a phantom method, and `CLASS_HEADER_RE` always hardcoded the symbol kind to "class" regardless of actual struct/interface/enum construct. The name-suffix now requires a bare or generic-qualified opening paren, readonly is recognized, double-processing is skipped when the property regex already matched, and the keyword is captured directly and mapped to distinct kinds. See [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **CSV header matching and column lookups failed on Excel-exported UTF-8 files due to a BOM prefix.** Excel/PowerShell "Save As UTF-8" prefixes CSVs with a UTF-8 BOM, which stuck to the first header cell and silently broke `--columns`/`--where` lookups on that column. Both `parseRecords` csv-parse calls now pass `bom: true` to strip it. See [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts).
- **Markdown fence tracking in doc-compact diverged from the canonical implementation, allowing mismatched fences and heading misidentification.** `buildExtractiveCompact` used a naive toggle that accepted mismatched fence chars and allowed shorter runs to close longer ones, diverging from `eachUnfencedLine` in markdown_lines.ts. `extractDocCompact`'s heading mode had no fence tracking, so content inside a fenced block could be misidentified as section boundaries. Both now use the same CommonMark-correct fence-state logic as `eachUnfencedLine`. See [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_compact.test.ts](tests/doc_compact.test.ts).
- **Excel Date cells rendered as verbose JavaScript locale strings instead of clean ISO dates.** `cellText` fell through to `String(cell.value)` for Date-typed values, emitting full `toString()` output instead of a clean date. `cellText` now special-cases `instanceof Date` and formats directly as ISO date/datetime. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts).
- **Image format conversions by shrinkImage silently mislabeled output files with the wrong extension.** `takeScreenshot` and `cmdFetchImage` wrote shrink-converted bytes (e.g. re-encoded to WebP) under the original extension, so a `.png` request could contain actual JPEG bytes. A new `withExtension` helper in util.ts renames the destination when shrinkImage reports a format change. `fetch-image`'s default extension also came from a hardcoded `.bin` regardless of response content-type; it now derives from the actual response. See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/screenshot.ts](src/screenshot.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts), [tests/screenshot.test.ts](tests/screenshot.test.ts).
- **`csv-query --head` accepted invalid input (non-numeric, negative) that silently corrupted results.** `runCsvQuery` parsed `--head` with raw `parseInt` instead of the `requireNonNegativeInt` validation already used by the parallel `xlsx-query --head` path. Non-numeric values produced `NaN`, turning `.slice(0, NaN)` into 0 rows with a misleading "N more rows elided" message; negative values silently used negative-index semantics. Added mirrored `requireNonNegativeInt` validation. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **Gemini hook re-installs skipped upgrading legacy hook commands instead of replacing them.** `installGemini`'s idempotency gate matched both current exec-path-hardened and legacy bare `"token-goat hook <event>"` forms, so pre-hardening installs reported already-installed and never picked up the safer command. The gate now checks for the current form specifically and strips any stale entries before writing the replacement. See [src/bridges/gemini_install.ts](src/bridges/gemini_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_gemini.test.ts](tests/install_gemini.test.ts).
- **Codex hook re-installs failed to correct stale baked `process.execPath` values.** `installCodex`'s idempotency check only tested for presence of a marker, never byte-compared the actual command text. Stale paths (from deleted dev checkouts or node version switches) were never refreshed on re-install. The check now requires an exact match against the current command and replaces any divergence. See [src/bridges/codex_install.ts](src/bridges/codex_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_codex.test.ts](tests/install_codex.test.ts).
- **`lockdeps` ignored explicit lockfile arguments and re-picked based on priority.** `findLockfile` reduced an explicit file path down to its directory and re-selected by `LOCK_PRIORITY`, discarding the caller's choice. Running "lockdeps ./yarn.lock" in a directory with both yarn.lock and package-lock.json would parse the npm lockfile. Explicit file arguments are now returned directly without re-picking. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).
- **Legacy hook entries were not removed when a current-format entry already coexisted.** `installHooks` skipped the legacy-strip pass once a current entry was found, leaving outdated entries alongside working ones. Legacy strip now always runs first, regardless of whether a current entry is present. See [src/install.ts](src/install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install.test.ts](tests/install.test.ts).
- **`map --compact` now returns output on real projects instead of empty results.** The command was routed to the legacy `buildCompactMap` in `repomap.ts`, which tied every file's `symbolCount` at the limit (8) and stopped token estimation after ~10 entries. `--compact` now uses the same `buildProjectMap` as plain `map`. Also corrected multiple fictional README.md claims about `symbol --strict`, `src/read_replacement.ts`, `context-stats --fix`, `impact`, and the repomap example section. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/repomap.ts](src/repomap.ts), [README.md](README.md); regression-tested in [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`config-get` no longer corrupts TOML/INI values containing inline comments or mismatched quotes.** Value parsing stripped a trailing quote independently of a leading quote, so `dogs'` got truncated and `"foo'` lost its opening quote. Inline comments were never stripped from values (unlike section headers), so `key = "val" # comment` emitted the corrupted string `val" # comment`. Added `stripInlineComment` (quote-aware, splits only on unquoted `#` or `;`) and `stripPairedQuotes` (strips only when both ends are present and match) to the TOML/INI path, and applied the same paired-quote fix to `lookupYaml`, which had the identical independent-single-end bug. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/test_configget_bug.test.ts](tests/test_configget_bug.test.ts).
- **`gdrive-sections` no longer caches and displays private/unshared Google Docs' sign-in pages.** A private document's export URL 302-redirects to Google's sign-in page, which `fetch()` follows transparently and resolves as plain 200 text/html. `fetchDoc` accepted any 2xx response with no content-type check, so the sign-in HTML got cached and parsed as real content, showing misleading "No sections found." even after the doc was later shared. `fetchDocFromApi` now rejects and does not cache any response whose `content-type` includes `text/html`, with a clear error message. See [src/gdrive.ts](src/gdrive.ts); regression-tested in [tests/gdrive.test.ts](tests/gdrive.test.ts).
- **`runTestFor` now lists only tests that actually reference the target file, and `runBrief` now reports the uncapped total number of callers.** `testFileMap` was created but never populated, so `testFunctions` listed every test-prefixed symbol in candidate files regardless of whether they referenced the target. Each reference into a test file now records its enclosing symbol, and `testFunctions` is filtered against it. `runBrief`'s `totalCallers` was capped at 500 by `queryRefs`'s internal limit and the length was reported as the true count; it now queries `queryRefCounts` (a separate uncapped COUNT(*)) instead. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`csv-query --where` now recognizes `>=` and `<=` operators.** `WHERE_SPEC_RE`'s alternation had no `>=`/`<=` entries, so `col>=5` matched the bare `>` alternative and left `=5` as the value, silently comparing the string `"=5"` instead of performing a `>=` comparison or rejecting the malformed spec. See [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts).
- **XLSX extraction no longer silently drops trailing rows after interior blank rows.** `actualRowCount` counts only populated rows, so a sheet with an interior blank row undercounted the loop bound and lost trailing rows in `xlsx-sheets`, `xlsx-head`, and `xlsx-query` output. Now uses `ws.rowCount`, which reflects the index of the last populated row and the true extent. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts).
- **SQL indexer no longer drops symbols after a multi-line string containing `--`.** `stripSqlLineComments` ran line-by-line before string scanning with no awareness that a line could start mid-way through an already-open multi-line string. A `--` inside such a string got treated as a comment, blanking the closing quote and flipping string-parity tracking for the rest of the file, dropping every symbol after that point. `--` handling is now folded into `stripSqlStringLiterals`'s stateful character scan, which already tracks whether a string is open across line boundaries. See [src/languages/sql_idx.ts](src/languages/sql_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Kotlin adapter no longer indexes function-local classes as class members.** The class/companion-object detection branch lacked a `depthInClass` gate, unlike the method/const branch below it. A class or companion object declared inside a method body (legal in Kotlin) got indexed as a real nested member instead of being skipped as function-local, polluting `symbol`, `outline`, and `semantic` results. See [src/languages/kotlin.ts](src/languages/kotlin.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`extractDocCompact` now matches closed-ATX heading style (`## Title ##`).** The greedy capture in the `--heading` regex swallowed closing hash runs, so `## Setup ##` captured "Setup ##" instead of "Setup", failing exact-equality and returning empty string for any doc using closed-ATX style. Now uses lazy capture with space-preceded-hash stripping, matching `section_reader.ts`'s already-correct form. See [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_compact.test.ts](tests/doc_compact.test.ts).
- **`.mdx` files are now indexed as markdown instead of skipped as unknown.** `EXTENSION_LANGUAGE` had no `.mdx` entry, so `detectLanguage` returned `'unknown'` and every `.mdx` file was skipped entirely -- no headings made it into the symbol index. MDX heading syntax is plain ATX and works with the existing markdown extractor as-is. See [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts), [tests/parser_types.test.ts](tests/parser_types.test.ts).
- **Language adapters no longer misidentify string delimiters as context-blind false positives.** C#'s verbatim-string opener check lacked an `isInsideStringLiteral` guard, so an ordinary string ending in `@` was misread as opening a verbatim string that swallowed every line until a stray quote. PowerShell's here-string opener had the same gap. Apex's `stripStringLiterals` ran before comment-stripping and blanked characters (including newlines) without state awareness, dropping content mid-file. Each check now guards against surrounding context. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts), [tests/salesforce_languages.test.ts](tests/salesforce_languages.test.ts).
- **`install_gemini.test.ts` is now independent of checkout directory name.** The suite identified hook commands by checking whether `process.argv[1]` contained a "token-goat" path segment, which worked in real npm installs but under vitest's fork pool, `argv[1]` is tinypool's worker script unrelated to token-goat. Test pass/fail depended on whether the repo's directory name happened to contain "token-goat". Now stubs `argv[1]` to a realistic token-goat entry path in `beforeEach` so install/uninstall behavior is exercised deterministically. See [tests/install_gemini.test.ts](tests/install_gemini.test.ts).
- **Package manifest hints now appear once per session instead of repeating on every read.** `buildPackageManifestHint` was called unconditionally on every whole-file read of package.json without checking if the hint had already been shown. Fixed with the real `wasFileReadThisSession`/`markHintShown` primitives from session.ts. Also removed the unwired `hints.ts` hint-dedup/priority subsystem (`dedupHints`/`applyHintPriorityLimit`/`SessionCache`), which had zero production call sites and a shape mismatched to session.ts's actual dedup primitives. See [src/hints.ts](src/hints.ts), [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **MCP surgical-read tools now scope results to the client's workspace and use client-friendly error text.** Section miss-path errors previously listed all available sections unbounded (46+ lines for a single typo), and only the `semantic` MCP tool accepted `projectRoot` to scope searches -- the other five (`read`, `symbol`, `skeleton`, `outline`, `section`) resolved relative paths against the server's working directory and could match same-named symbols anywhere on disk. All five MCP tools now accept optional `projectRoot` to scope searches to the client's workspace, and both section and read miss-paths reuse the same `didYouMean()` helper to cap suggestions at 5 lines. See [src/mcp_server.ts](src/mcp_server.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_server_cli_affordance_rewrite.test.ts](tests/mcp_server_cli_affordance_rewrite.test.ts), [tests/mcp_server_projectroot_scope.test.ts](tests/mcp_server_projectroot_scope.test.ts).
- **`--force-refresh` reads now re-embed content so semantic search returns fresh results.** `symbol`/`skeleton`/`outline --force-refresh` called `indexFileSync` directly, which wiped `files.embed_sha` but never enqueued the file for re-embedding, leaving semantic search serving stale content indefinitely. Fixed by mirroring `cmdReplace`'s `enqueueDirtyPathSafe` pattern at all 3 call sites. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **Cross-process embedding races no longer overwrite fresh embeddings with stale stamps.** `inFlightEmbeddings` serializes concurrent embed calls only within a single process, so a slow foreground call could commit its `embed_sha` after a second process had already re-embedded the file, silently overwriting the fresher stamp with a stale one. `stampEmbedSha`'s UPDATE now requires `files.sha` to match the original value at the start of the embed run, so a stale writer becomes a no-op once fresher content has moved the row forward. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/embeddings_stale_writer_race.test.ts](tests/embeddings_stale_writer_race.test.ts).
- **Worker dirty-queue drain now handles concurrent writes, logs embedding errors, and rotates state files.** The rename-to-claim atomicity in `drainOnce` is unsafe on Windows and POSIX, so concurrent writes during the claim window were silently discarded -- it now re-reads `.draining` before deleting it and forwards raced-in paths back into the live queue. Embedding failures were previously fully swallowed with zero trace (the background daemon runs with `stdio: 'ignore'`) and now route through the same `appendWorkerErrorLog` path as parse failures. Neither `worker-errors.log` nor `.draining.corrupt-*` quarantine files had size/age rotation; added periodic cleanup via `cleanupWorkerStateFiles` wired into the existing periodic sweep. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker_drain_rename_race.test.ts](tests/worker_drain_rename_race.test.ts), [tests/worker_embed_error_log.test.ts](tests/worker_embed_error_log.test.ts), [tests/worker_state_file_rotation.test.ts](tests/worker_state_file_rotation.test.ts).
- **XLSX formula results and CSV output now handle dates and errors correctly.** `cellText` stringified formula cell cached results directly, so Date results printed as locale strings instead of ISO format, and error results printed as "[object Object]". `sheetToCsv` emitted each row only up to that row's own last non-empty column, producing ragged CSV that strict parsers rejected -- now pads every row to the sheet's actual used-column-count, matching the pattern `headSheet` already uses. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts).
- **`stats --home-dir` now resolves the correct data directory on Windows.** `computeDataDir(homeDir)` had drifted from `defaultDataDir` logic and was missing the `\AppData\Local` segment on Windows, so `--home-dir <home>` silently pointed at an empty/wrong database and reported "No stats recorded yet" with no error. Extracted home-relative platform branching into a new exported `dataDirForHome(homeDir)` in constants.ts, structurally derived from the given home, so it can't drift from `defaultDataDir` again. See [src/constants.ts](src/constants.ts), [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/constants.test.ts](tests/constants.test.ts), [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts).
- **`stats --json` now includes the by_source breakdown in the summary envelope.** `summarize()` already computed `by_source` and the human-readable output rendered a "By Source" section, but the JSON envelope was missing it alongside `by_kind`, `by_day`, `by_project`, and `by_command`. See [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_stats.test.ts).
- **PowerShell Windows path literals in strings no longer corrupt symbol parsing.** PowerShell strings never use backslash as an escape -- a trailing backslash in a path like `"C:\Temp\"` is just a literal character. The brace-depth scanner reused C-like `stripStringLiterals`, which treats backslash as an escape, so it misread the trailing backslash as escaping the closing quote, leaving the string "open" and swallowing braces on the rest of the line, desyncing brace-depth tracking for every subsequent line and silently dropping top-level symbols. Added `stripPowershellStringLiterals`, which only recognizes PowerShell's real escaping rules. See [src/languages/powershell_idx.ts](src/languages/powershell_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **SQL block comments inside multi-line strings no longer corrupt SQL extraction.** `extractSql` ran `stripCstyleComments` (a per-line, non-string-aware pass) before the SQL string-literal scanner, so a `/*` sequence inside an open multi-line string was misread as a comment opener; with no matching `*/` after it, the "comment" never closed and everything after it -- including real DDL statements -- was silently dropped to EOF. Folded `/* */` handling directly into the existing single-pass, string-aware scanner. See [src/languages/sql_idx.ts](src/languages/sql_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Multi-line string literals in doc/context packing now preserve their content when comments are stripped.** pack.ts's `stripComments` determined whether comment-like sequences sat inside a string by counting quotes from the start of the current line only, so multi-line strings (JS template literals, Python triple-quoted strings) that opened on earlier lines always looked "not open" on later lines, and `//` or `#` inside them were misread as real comments and stripped, corrupting the string. Added `computeLineStartQuoteStates` to run a single pass recording which quote kinds are open at the start of each line. See [src/pack.ts](src/pack.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pack.test.ts](tests/pack.test.ts).
- **GraphQL block descriptions containing `#` comments no longer corrupt symbol parsing.** `extractGraphql` ran `stripHashComments` before the multi-line-aware `"""..."""` masker, so a `#` inside an open block description looked "not inside a string" and was treated as a real comment; if it sat before the description's closing `"""` on the same line, the closer got deleted too, so masking never found an end for the rest of the file and silently dropped every symbol after it. Reordered passes so descriptions are masked first, and taught `stripGraphqlDescriptions` to resolve precedence between an unquoted `#` and a preceding `"""`. See [src/languages/graphql_idx.ts](src/languages/graphql_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Salesforce LWC JavaScript files no longer lose all symbols after a `/*` inside a template literal.** `extractLwcJavaScript` stripped comments via helpers whose quote-awareness only recognized `"` and `'` (not backticks) and reset per line. A `/*` sequence inside a multi-line backtick template literal was misread as opening a block comment; with no matching `*/` later in the file, the "comment" never closed and everything after it -- including real `@api` declarations -- was silently dropped from the index. Replaced both calls with a new local `stripJsComments`, a single linear scan that copies quoted-string and backtick template-literal spans through verbatim. See [src/languages/salesforce_frontend.ts](src/languages/salesforce_frontend.ts); regression-tested in [tests/salesforce_frontend.test.ts](tests/salesforce_frontend.test.ts).
- **`stripPrefixes` no longer skipped env assignments with a path value.** The leading-assignment loop tested `!out[0].includes('/')` against the whole token (name and value), so any assignment whose value contained a slash (e.g., `PATH=/usr/local/bin`) broke the loop before the real binary was resolved. The check now only examines the assignment name. See [src/tool_filters/helpers.ts](src/tool_filters/helpers.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).
- **Env assignments after wrapper tokens are now stripped.** `stripPrefixes` only stripped leading env assignments once, before the passthrough-prefix loop, so assignments appearing after a wrapper token (e.g., `env FOO=bar git log`) were never stripped and got misresolved as the binary. Both passes now alternate to a fixpoint. See [src/tool_filters/helpers.ts](src/tool_filters/helpers.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).
- **The `-i` flag no longer consumes the binary token for `sudo`/`env` wrappers.** `sudo -i` and `env -i` are valueless flags, but `-i` was listed as taking a value, so the real binary token following it got consumed as the flag's value, causing the wrapper to misresolve. The flag is now removed from the value-taking list. See [src/tool_filters/helpers.ts](src/tool_filters/helpers.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).
- **`GrepFilter`'s context-aware summarizer is now reachable instead of always losing to `RgFilter`.** `RgFilter` is registered before `GrepFilter` and both claim `rg`/`grep`, but `RgFilter.matches()` had no flag gate, so it won plain `grep`/`rg` with no context flags too. `RgFilter` now only claims commands carrying an actual `-A`/`-B`/`-C`/`--context` flag. See [src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts](src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_shell_file.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_shell_file.test.ts).
- **`git grep` now routes to `GrepFilter` instead of being caught by `GitFilter`.** `GitFilter` has no subcommand gate and was registered before shell-file filters, so it claimed every git subcommand including `grep`, leaving `GrepFilter`'s dedicated git-grep compression unreachable. `GitFilter.matches()` now explicitly excludes the `grep` subcommand from dispatch. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`envInt` now trims whitespace before parsing, matching `envStr`/`envBool`.** `envInt`'s docstring promised strip-whitespace-then-parse, but it ran its integer regex against the raw untrimmed value, so a whitespace-padded value silently fell back to the default instead of parsing. See [src/env.ts](src/env.ts); regression-tested in [tests/env.test.ts](tests/env.test.ts).
- **`bash-output`/`web-output --head`/`--tail` now reject non-numeric input and honor 0.** Parsing used bare `Number.parseInt` plus a truthy check that only accepted strictly-positive results, so a non-numeric value and an explicit `--head 0` both silently fell back to the default instead of erroring or honoring the 0. Both flags now route through `requireNonNegativeInt`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts](tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts).
- **Git subcommand detection no longer hijacked by commit message text in `-m` flags.** `positionalArgs()` only drops dash-prefixed tokens -- it doesn't know `-m`/`--message` takes a value, so that value's text stayed in the positional stream. A commit message equaling another filter's subcommand (e.g., `git commit -m log`) hijacked dispatch to the wrong filter. A git-specific positional-args scanner now skips the value token of `-m`/`--message` and other known value-taking git flags. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`refs`/`callers` with `limit: 0` now correctly reject instead of falsely reporting "no references found".** Both passed `opts.limit` straight through to `queryRefs`, which translates limit 0 into SQL `LIMIT 0` -- always zero rows regardless of whether the symbol has references. Both now reject `limit <= 0` explicitly up front. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`find`/`types`/`brief` with `limit: 0` now correctly reject instead of falsely reporting "no matches".** All three sliced or SQL-limited by `opts.limit`, silently producing zero rows for limit 0 even when matches existed, then reporting a false "no matches" message. All three now reject `limit <= 0` explicitly up front. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`csv-query` no longer treats blank cells as zero in numeric `--where` comparisons.** `matchesWhere` ran `Number(cell)` directly for `>`/`<`/`>=`/`<=` comparisons -- `Number('')` is 0, not NaN, so blank cells were silently coerced to 0, wrongly matching filters like `col<10` for rows with no value in that column. Blank cells now short-circuit to non-match for numeric comparisons; literal string "0" is unaffected. See [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts).
- **ESLint warnings are no longer dropped on clean exit.** `ESLintFilter.compress`'s fast path treated `exitCode === 0` as "nothing to report", but ESLint exits 0 whenever there are no errors, even with warnings emitted. Output with no stylish summary footer (e.g., `--format unix`) had no summary to find, so real warning text was silently replaced. The fast path now only elides output when no line looks like an issue. See [src/tool_filters/linters.ts](src/tool_filters/linters.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_linters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_linters.test.ts).
- **Multi-line quoted dotenv values no longer create phantom environment keys.** `extractEnv` scanned every line independently for column-0 `KEY=value` assignments with no open-quote state carried from the previous line, so a multi-line quoted value containing text that looked like an assignment was misread as a real key. `extractEnv` now tracks whether the previous line opened a quote it didn't close, and skips key-scanning until that quote closes. See [src/languages/ini_idx.ts](src/languages/ini_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Markdown fence detection no longer miscloses on marker lines with trailing info strings.** A line like a fenced-open with a trailing info string while an unlabeled fence was open was treated as a valid closer because the fence-close check compared only marker character and run length, ignoring trailing content. Per CommonMark, a closing fence must have no info string. This desynced open/closed state and silently dropped every real heading after it. The check now rejects closers with trailing content. See [src/markdown_lines.ts](src/markdown_lines.ts); regression-tested in [tests/section_reader.test.ts](tests/section_reader.test.ts).
- **`git log --graph --oneline` no longer miscounts connector-only ASCII-art lines as commits.** The regex for identifying commit lines counted every non-empty line, including connector-only lines like `|/` and `|\` that appear around merges but carry no commit hash, inflating both the truncation cap and the "+N more" elided-count message. Added a graph-tolerant oneline regex to filter for lines that actually carry a commit hash before counting. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`PsqlFilter` now recognizes the header row when preceded by a top border (style 2).** The SELECT-table state machine identified the header line only on the first border it encountered; `\pset border 2` output has a top border before the header text, so the header line fell through into dataRows and got counted and truncated as if it were data. Peek at the line following a leading top border; if it is not itself a border, consume it as the header. See [src/tool_filters/misc.ts](src/tool_filters/misc.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts).
- **Combined diffs (merge-commit conflict resolutions) now get per-file compression.** Git uses `diff --cc <path>` instead of `diff --git a/<path> b/<path>` for combined diffs, but the file-boundary regex only recognized the `--git` form, so a combined diff never split into per-file blocks and fell through unprocessed. Extended the file-boundary regex to recognize the `--cc` form. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`compress --context` (and `cmdBudget --context`) now validate input and reject invalid values.** `cmdBudget` used a bare `Number.parseInt` instead of the shared `requirePositiveInt` validator, so negative or malformed values silently produced nonsensical output, since `--context` is used as a divisor in a percentage calculation. Routed through `requirePositiveInt` to reject both malformed and zero values. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pack_cli.test.ts](tests/pack_cli.test.ts).
- **Large hunks in combined diffs (`git show --cc`, `git diff --cc`) now get truncated instead of passing through.** Combined-diff hunk headers use one extra `@` per merged parent, and the hunk-boundary regex only matched the plain form, so large-hunk truncation never engaged on `--cc` hunks. Updated the regex to recognize the triple-`@` format. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **Liquid extractor now indexes includes/sections/renders/schema blocks with whitespace-control tags.** The regex patterns required a plain {% raw %}`{%`{% endraw %} opener, so Shopify's dominant whitespace-control form {% raw %}`{%- ... -%}`{% endraw %} never matched and those blocks were silently dropped from the index. Now allows optional whitespace-control dashes around the delimiters. See [src/languages/liquid.ts](src/languages/liquid.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Makefile multi-target rules now emit separate symbols for each target.** `TARGET_RE` captured everything up to the colon as a single name, so a rule like `all clean:` emitted one fused "all clean" symbol instead of two, and exact-match symbol lookup returned nothing for a visibly present target. Split the captured target group on whitespace and emit each token as its own symbol. See [src/languages/makefile_idx.ts](src/languages/makefile_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Makefile adapter now correctly masks nested `define...endef` blocks regardless of depth.** `DEFINE_BLOCK_RE` was non-greedy, so with GNU make's legal nested define/endef structure the mask stopped at the first (innermost) `endef`, leaving the rest of the outer block unmasked and scanned as real rule text. Any colon-bearing line in that tail was wrongly emitted as a real target symbol. Replaced the regex with a depth-tracking line scanner that masks the entire outer block regardless of nesting depth. See [src/languages/makefile_idx.ts](src/languages/makefile_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`compress --max-tokens` now caps unfiltered commands and validates its input.** When no tool filter matched, `run()` passed through to raw stdio without checking `opts.maxTokens` -- the cap logic only lived inside `wrapAndCompress`, a silent no-op for unfiltered commands, exactly where the cap is most needed. Also validated `--max-tokens` through `requireNonNegativeInt` instead of bare `parseInt`. See [src/bash_runner.ts](src/bash_runner.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/bash_runner.test.ts](tests/bash_runner.test.ts), [tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts](tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts).
- **`bash-output`/`web-output --max-matches` now validates input and enforces the cap.** Bare-parsing allowed non-numeric, zero, and negative values to silently print every matching line with exit code 0 instead of erroring. Routed through `requireNonNegativeInt` so invalid input errors clearly and an explicit 0 means "match zero lines" rather than unlimited. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).
- **HTML extractor no longer indexes markup inside HTML comments.** Comments were never stripped before the heading/id/class/link/script regexes ran, so dead markup inside `<!-- ... -->` blocks got indexed identically to live markup and corrupted the following section's line-range bookkeeping. Reuses the existing offset-preserving `stripXmlComments` helper before extraction runs. See [src/languages/html.ts](src/languages/html.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Proto extractor now matches `rpc` and `oneof` declared at column 0.** Both patterns required at least one leading space/tab, so an unindented service or message body with column-0 declarations had those lines silently dropped from the index. Now allows optional leading whitespace. See [src/languages/proto_idx.ts](src/languages/proto_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`config set` now validates JSON-array values on number-list keys.** The JSON-array branch of `coerce()` returned `JSON.parse(raw)` unchecked, so setting a number-list key to a JSON array of non-numeric strings reported success but the load-time int-list validator silently filtered it to an empty array on the next load. Now applies the same type validation the comma-separated branch already does. See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **`screenshot --width` and `--height` now validate input before launching a browser.** `parseInt` on garbage input produced `NaN`, which isn't nullish so it passed the fallback check and reached Chrome DevTools Protocol, causing an opaque error after a full browser launch. Both flags now route through `requirePositiveInt` for fast-fail validation with a clean CLI error. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`stats --window-days` rejects trailing garbage instead of truncating.** `opts.windowDays` was parsed with bare `parseInt`, silently accepting values like `'30abc'` as `30`, inconsistent with strict numeric validation on other flags. Now routes through `requireNonNegativeInt`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts](tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts).
- **`git diff/show` binary collapse now matches combined-diff (`--cc`) format.** The binary-message regex only matched plain two-filename messages, not the combined-diff form that omits filenames entirely, so binary collapse never triggered for `--cc` conflicts. The regex now makes the filename segment optional. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`fetch-image` now writes output atomically instead of truncating in place.** `cmdFetchImage` wrote fetched/shrunk bytes via bare `fs.writeFileSync`, unlike other disk-cache paths which use `atomicWriteBytes` (temp file + rename), so concurrent readers of the same `--out` path could observe partial or truncated content. Now routes through `atomicWriteBytes`. See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **`callers` and `dead` now scope ref-matching to the symbol's defining file when names collide.** `resolveCallers` and `runDead` matched refs by bare name project-wide, so when two files each define a function with identical names, a call to one file's definition was attributed to the other file's unrelated same-named symbol too, making genuinely dead symbols look alive. Added `filterRefsForSymbol`, which keeps refs in the symbol's own file or in files with no local shadowing definition. The unscoped `token-goat callers <name>` CLI path remains intentionally global. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **`dead` and `refs` now capture non-invoked identifier usages like callbacks and assignments.** `extractRefs` only walked call-site node types, missing symbols passed as callbacks, assigned to bindings, or stored as object values -- producing false-positive dead reports and under-reported ref counts. Added `valueRefIdentifiers`, which recognizes bare identifiers in call/constructor arguments, assignment RHS, and object-literal values, scoped to TypeScript/JavaScript/Python. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts).
- **`.env` parser now correctly handles backslash-escape sequences in quoted values.** The open-quote detection in `ini_idx.ts` checked only whether the single character before a quote was a backslash, mishandling escaped backslashes (only odd runs escape) and single-quoted values (which have no backslash-escape semantics in dotenv/POSIX). A value like `DIR='C:\Users\me\'` was misread as an escaped still-open quote, silently swallowing every subsequent `.env` key as phantom continuation. Now counts the run of consecutive backslashes and treats as escaped only on odd count; skips escape handling for single quotes entirely. See [src/languages/ini_idx.ts](src/languages/ini_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`hot`, `recent`, `trace`, and `logfold` now validate limit flags instead of silently ignoring bad input.** Each used bare `Number.parseInt` unvalidated, then checked `> 0` to gate output, so a value of `0`, a non-numeric string, or a negative value all bypassed the guard the same way as absent input, silently printing unbounded results. All four now route through `requireNonNegativeInt`; `0` is accepted since it carries real meaning for each command. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).
- **`tryWrapCompoundSegments` now splits `&&` with quote awareness.** The function split on a naive regex with no notion of quoting, so a `&&` inside quoted arguments was treated as a segment boundary, corrupting quoted content on rejoin. The current live hooks_bash.ts entry point bails before this runs, so the bug is unreachable in shipping today, but the function reads as deliberately-built documented code. Replaced the regex split with `splitTopLevelAnd`, a char-by-char scan that tracks quote state and only treats `&&` as a boundary outside quoted spans. See [src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts](src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).
- **`xlsx-range` now normalizes reversed ranges instead of returning empty.** `decodeRange` decoded ranges like `B5:A1` to a start row/col greater than end row/col, so `rangeSheet`'s iteration loop never executed and the command returned an empty result indistinguishable from a range covering no data. Both axes now normalize via min/max, matching Excel's own behavior. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts).
- **`cellText` now renders a plain error cell's error text explicitly.** Non-formula error cells (e.g. `#N/A` entered directly) have shape `{ error: '#N/A' }` with no `richText`/`result`/`text` key, and `cellText` depended on ExcelJS's implicit `cell.text` getter to format them -- now checks `obj.error` directly. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts).
- **`section` now resolves the exact-text sibling heading instead of an earlier normalized-tier match.** Header resolution OR'd exact/normalized/stripped equality checks into one flat array and returned the first document-order match, so two sibling headings differing only by a parenthetical or subtitle normalize to the same text and an exact-text query for the later one silently returned the earlier one's content. Now tiers matching so exact equality is preferred, falling back to normalized then stripped equality only when the higher tier found nothing. See [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts); regression-tested in [tests/section_reader.test.ts](tests/section_reader.test.ts).
- **Five more numeric CLI flags now reject invalid input instead of silently truncating.** `history --limit`, `bash-history --limit`, `web-history --limit`, `prune-cache --maxCount`, and `compact-doc --sentences` used bare `Number.parseInt`, so trailing garbage and exponential notation were silently accepted, and negative `--maxCount` was coerced to 0 instead of erroring; also tightened `graph_commands.ts`'s `scope` command, which parsed "file:12abc" as line 12. Added a strict-integer validation trio (`requireInt`, `requireNonNegativeInt`, `requirePositiveInt`) to util.ts. See [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts](tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts), [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts), [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **Transcript reader no longer strips dialogue starting with "Word:" when the speaker came from a `<v>` tag.** `parseTranscript` correctly extracted the speaker from a cue's `<v Name>` tag, but then ran the same leading-"Name:" prefix heuristic a second time on the tag-stripped text without knowing the speaker was already resolved, so dialogue like "Bob said: hello there everyone" was mistaken for a redundant speaker label and deleted. The prefix heuristic now only runs when the cue had no `<v>` tag to begin with. See [src/transcript_extract.ts](src/transcript_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/transcript_extract.test.ts](tests/transcript_extract.test.ts).
- **`config set` now rejects unrecognized enum-string values instead of silently persisting them.** `compression.profile` and `compact_assist.harness` accepted any string with no revalidation, so a typo was written to disk and silently fell back to a default at runtime with no signal to the user. Now validates enum values symmetrically with existing numeric-bounds revalidation and rejects out-of-set strings with a clear error before disk write. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/bridges/registry.ts](src/bridges/registry.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **`image_shrink` stat recording is now restored (dropped during the Python->TS port).** The Read-hook image shrink was verified against retired Python source to have recorded a stat on every successful shrink, but that call was never carried over to the TS port's `preReadImageHandler`, making the image-shrink kind silently unreachable in production since the port. See [src/image_shrink.ts](src/image_shrink.ts); regression-tested in [tests/image_shrink.test.ts](tests/image_shrink.test.ts).
- **`gdrive-sections` now parses Google Docs' actual markdown export, not the txt export's headingless output.** The `format=txt` export renders styled headings as bare plain-text lines with no `#` characters, so the #-based heading regex could never match real doc headings. Switched to `format=markdown`, which renders headings with bold markers and an anchor slug, and strips those when extracting heading text. See [src/gdrive.ts](src/gdrive.ts); test fixtures updated in [tests/gdrive.test.ts](tests/gdrive.test.ts).
- **`test-for` ref lookup now scopes to the current project root.** `runTestFor` called `queryRefs` with no `rootDir`, unlike every sibling graph command; since `global.db` is a single machine-wide index shared across every project ever indexed, a test file in a completely unrelated project referencing a same-named symbol could leak into test-for's results. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **`csv-query`/`xlsx-query --where` now resolves the correct column when a header name contains operator characters.** The column capture in `WHERE_SPEC_RE` excludes operator-class characters outright, so it always split at the first one -- a header containing `<` queried with a where-spec intended for that whole header name silently parsed as a shorter column name plus a bogus operator/value. `queryCsv` now re-checks each parsed `where` against real headers by reconstructing the raw spec text and finding the longest header that is a valid prefix of it. `xlsx-query` shares the fix since `querySheet` delegates to `queryCsv`. See [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts).
- **Stat recording is now restored for all surgical-read commands (symbol/read/section/skeleton/outline/exports/refs/semantic).** The Python->TS port dropped `recordStat` calls for the entire surgical-read command family, the same class of bug fixed for `image_shrink` in a prior commit -- `stats.ts`'s mappings still defined entries for all of them, but nothing ever wrote a row. Adds `recordStat` calls on each command's success path, computing `bytesSaved` as full on-disk source size (deduplicated across multi-file/multi-hit results) minus the emitted slice, with `tokensSaved` approximated as `bytesSaved/4`. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands_stats.test.ts](tests/read_commands_stats.test.ts).
- **`bash-compress` gate now rejects backgrounded and newline-separated commands.** The compressibility gates rejected `&&`, `||`, `|`, `;`, `$()`, and backticks, but a bare `&` (background operator) and embedded newlines slipped through -- commands like `vite dev &` were rewritten into a compress-wrapped form, causing bash_runner's spawnSync to block on piped stdio until the backgrounded grandchild exited, turning fire-and-forget into a 600s timeout hang. Added a helper that masks quoted spans before checking for a bare `&` or newline, wired into both gates. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), [src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts](src/tool_filters/dispatch.ts), [src/tool_filters/helpers.ts](src/tool_filters/helpers.ts); tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts), [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).
- **`pruneIndex` no longer misclassifies URL and absolute-path MEMORY.md targets as dead.** `pruneIndex` checked existence by joining the entry's target onto memoryDir, which mangled full URLs and absolute filesystem paths into bogus paths, silently deleting genuinely-valid entries -- at the time, `context-stats --fix` called `pruneIndex` with no confirmation or backup, so a misclassification like this wrote straight to disk with no chance to catch it first (`context-stats --fix` gained confirm-gating in a later [Unreleased] entry above). URL-scheme targets are now always treated as valid, and absolute-path targets are checked directly. See [src/memory_prune.ts](src/memory_prune.ts); tested in [tests/memory_prune.test.ts](tests/memory_prune.test.ts).
- **`normalizePath` now handles `\\?\` extended-length-path prefixes correctly.** The backslash-to-forward-slash conversion turned a leading `\\?\` prefix into `//?/`, which incorrectly matched the UNC host/share pattern, so the extended-length form and the plain form of the same path normalized to different keys and broke cache lookups. `normalizePath` now strips a leading `\\?\` prefix (rewriting `\\?\UNC\` appropriately) before other transformations. See [src/paths.ts](src/paths.ts); tested in [tests/paths.test.ts](tests/paths.test.ts).
- **`--worker-daemon` interception now matches only the exact spawn form.** The pre-commander interception matched the literal string `--worker-daemon` anywhere in argv, not just the specific form `startDetachedWorker` spawns. Any user command carrying that string as an argument was silently hijacked into daemon mode. Changed the check to require it at the exact spawn position. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); tested in [tests/cli_worker_daemon_flag.test.ts](tests/cli_worker_daemon_flag.test.ts).

### Changed

- **Config set validation now uses a targeted single-field validator instead of a full-tree rebuild.** Replaced the full-tree config rebuild on numeric `config set` paths with a validator that checks only the specific field's bounds and cross-field constraints, eliminating wasted validation work when only one field is being set. All bounds checking and cross-field constraint logic is preserved. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts).
- **Language adapters now use O(log n) line lookups instead of O(n·matches) rescans.** `sql_idx.ts`, `graphql_idx.ts`, `proto_idx.ts`, and `makefile_idx.ts` computed each match's line number via slice+split on preceding content; switched to the shared `buildLineIndex`/`offsetToLine` helpers (already used by `html.ts`) for binary search. Also stopped copying `lineIndex` on every `offsetToLine` call in `apex.ts` and `salesforce_metadata.ts`. See [src/languages/apex.ts](src/languages/apex.ts), [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts), [src/languages/graphql_idx.ts](src/languages/graphql_idx.ts), [src/languages/makefile_idx.ts](src/languages/makefile_idx.ts), [src/languages/proto_idx.ts](src/languages/proto_idx.ts), [src/languages/salesforce_metadata.ts](src/languages/salesforce_metadata.ts).
- **README now correctly describes the worker as a manually-started detached process, not OS-level autostart.** Removed false claims of a Windows registry Run key, systemd user unit, XDG `.desktop` entry, launchd plist, and auto-update mechanism, none of which exist in the codebase. Also corrected an example autostart command that named the wrong bundle file and flag. See [README.md](README.md).
- **`baseline` command description corrected and a dead `baseline_budget_tokens` config removed.** `token-goat baseline` emits only a project map, but the README described unbuilt features. Also removed `[hints] baseline_budget_tokens`, which was validated and round-tripped through config get/set but had zero actual consumers. See [README.md](README.md), [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/constants.ts](src/constants.ts); updated test expectations in [tests/config.test.ts](tests/config.test.ts).
- **README corrected on `ask` command flags, backend, retrieval, and caching.** The README described flags, env vars, a default synthesis model, cross-session answer caching, and semantic search that don't exist in `runAsk()`. The real flags are `--top` and `-j`, the real env var is `TOKEN_GOAT_ASK_BACKEND` (claude|codex), retrieval is BM25 full-text search, and caching is explicitly not implemented. See [README.md](README.md).

### Removed

- **Dead in-process `Worker` variant removed.** The in-process Worker pattern had no callers in source or tests; production only uses the detached-daemon path. If it were called, it would bypass worker pid tracking entirely, risking silent double-drain of the queue. Dropped the unused code and its `node:worker_threads` imports. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts).

## [2.6.14] - 2026-07-11


### Added

- **Layered Salesforce DX indexing for metadata and frontend bundles.** Every `*-meta.xml` file now receives a stable top-level symbol, while Apex, Flow, object-member metadata, Custom Labels, LWC, Aura, and Visualforce receive detailed symbols and selected cross-file references. LWC indexing understands public `@api` members, Salesforce imports, template handlers/child components, bundle targets, and target properties; Aura/Visualforce markup now has a dedicated `salesforce_markup` adapter. The real default worker path and built bundle are covered by a Salesforce DX fixture so these adapters cannot silently disappear from the shipped artifact.

### Fixed

- **macOS `/var` and `/private/var` aliases could produce different cache and index keys for the same file.** Path canonicalization now normalizes the Darwin system alias consistently, restoring relative `skeleton`/`outline`, trace frame detection, project discovery, settings paths, and doc-compact reuse for temporary paths.
- **The test harness could touch the live macOS data directory or fail to start TypeScript race helpers in restricted sandboxes.** Darwin tests now isolate `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, and subprocess fixtures load `tsx` without its IPC-based CLI.
- **The declared Node.js floor (`>=18.0.0`) was untested.** CI, publish, and the tarball smoke test have only ever exercised Node 22; the esbuild target was also still `node18`. Both now declare Node 22 as the floor, matching what is actually built and tested.
- **`token-goat stats` rendered the colorized rich box-table in CI instead of plain text.** The TTY heuristic treated any non-`false` `isTTY` as an interactive terminal (needed so Claude Code's own terminal, which reports `isTTY: undefined`, still gets rich output) but that same `undefined` value is also true of any non-interactive process, including CI runners. Now only `isTTY: true`, or `isTTY: undefined` with `CI` unset, uses the rich renderer.
- **`saveSessionState` could silently drop a concurrent hook process's update under real machine load.** The read-merge-write critical section is lock-protected, but on a lock-wait timeout it fell back to an unprotected write, recreating the exact clobber the lock exists to prevent -- precisely when contention (the trigger for needing the lock at all) is highest. The lock-wait budget for this hot, frequently-contended call site is now generous enough that only a genuinely wedged holder (which still gets its lock stolen via the existing stale-lock check) or a hard failure reaches the unprotected fallback.

## [2.6.13] - 2026-07-10

### Security

- **`xlsx` (SheetJS) has unpatched HIGH-severity CVEs (prototype pollution / ReDoS).** Replaced with `exceljs` for the `xlsx-sheets`/`xlsx-head`/`xlsx-range`/`xlsx-query` commands. Output format (CSV-formatted sheet/range/query text) is unchanged. The module doc comment's claim of `.xls`/`.ods` support was dropped — ExcelJS, like the SheetJS build actually in use, only reads `.xlsx`. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts) and [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`global.db` is a single machine-wide index shared across every project ever indexed, and five read paths queried it with no project scope — leaking or misattributing data across unrelated projects sharing the same machine.** `token-goat map` (`fetchTopSymbols` in `baseline.ts`), `token-goat semantic` (`searchSemantic`'s sqlite-vec KNN scan), `token-goat find` (`querySymbols`), `token-goat dead`/`types`/`coverage-gaps` (`runDead`/`runTypes`/`runCoverageGaps` in `graph_commands.ts`), and `outline --stats`/`skeleton --stats` (`queryRefCounts`) all ran unscoped: `token-goat semantic`/`map`/`find` run from project A could surface chunks, symbols, or files from unrelated project B; `dead` could misreport a function as ALIVE off a same-named symbol's reference in a different project; and `--stats` reference counts could be inflated by cross-project name collisions. All five now scope to the invoking project root via a new shared `projectScopeClause` helper — a LIKE-based path-prefix predicate with escaped wildcards and boundary correctness (`/proj` no longer matches `/proj-other/file.ts`). sqlite-vec's `chunk_vectors` vec0 table has no partition column to scope the ANN query itself against, so `searchSemantic` over-fetches KNN candidates, post-filters each candidate by project root, and retries once with a larger `k` if too few survive (`fetchScopedHits`, `BACKFILL_MULTIPLIER`) — a deliberate latency/correctness tradeoff: at most one extra query round-trip, in exchange for never leaking a chunk across projects. See [src/sql_path.ts](src/sql_path.ts), [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts), [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/index_reader.ts](src/index_reader.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/sql_path.test.ts](tests/sql_path.test.ts), [tests/baseline.test.ts](tests/baseline.test.ts), [tests/semantic_project_scope.test.ts](tests/semantic_project_scope.test.ts), [tests/find_project_scope.test.ts](tests/find_project_scope.test.ts), [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), [tests/index_reader.test.ts](tests/index_reader.test.ts), [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), and [tests/semantic_overflow_guard.test.ts](tests/semantic_overflow_guard.test.ts).

### Changed

- **Removed the unused `USE_COLOR` export from `src/render/ansi.ts`.** Computed once at module load and never read anywhere in the codebase; live callers already check `colorStdout()`/`colorStderr()` directly for the stream in question. See [src/render/ansi.ts](src/render/ansi.ts), [src/render/index.ts](src/render/index.ts).
- **BREAKING (JSON output): `symbol`/`refs`/`skeleton`/`outline --json` now share one envelope shape.** All four commands previously emitted inconsistent JSON — a bare array in some cases, an object wrapped under differently-named keys (`symbols`, `references`) in others, depending on whether overflow_guard truncated the result. They now always return `{items, truncated, totalCount}`, whether or not truncation occurred, so scripts consuming `--json` output no longer need to branch on shape. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); updated in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`sharp` and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` moved to `optionalDependencies`.** Both were already lazy-imported with a try/catch degrade path (image shrinking silently passes through when `sharp` is unavailable; `mcp-serve` now reports a clear "install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk" error and exits instead of crashing the whole CLI when the SDK is missing), but sat in `dependencies`, forcing every install to pull `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`'s ~17 transitive packages even for users who never touch `mcp-serve`. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is now lazy-`import()`ed only inside the `mcp-serve` command handler via type-only imports, so no other CLI command's startup path loads it. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [package.json](package.json); regression-tested in [tests/cli_mcp_server_lazy_load.test.ts](tests/cli_mcp_server_lazy_load.test.ts) and [tests/image_shrink_sharp_unavailable.test.ts](tests/image_shrink_sharp_unavailable.test.ts).

### Added

- **`token-goat doctor` now warns when the index has indexed files but zero symbols.** Guards against the worker-draining-to-a-stub-callback failure mode documented in this repo's own CLAUDE.md ("Critical path" section): files can be marked indexed in the `files` table while the parser never actually ran, silently leaving `symbol`/`read`/`skeleton`/`outline`/`semantic` permanently empty with no other signal. See [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_doctor.test.ts](tests/cli_doctor.test.ts).
- **`semantic`'s query embedding now carries BGE's retrieval instruction prefix.** The `bge-small-en-v1.5` model this project embeds with is asymmetric: query text is meant to carry a `"Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: "` prefix that document/chunk text never gets. `searchSemantic` now applies it to the query side only, leaving chunk/document embedding unprefixed. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/semantic_project_scope.test.ts](tests/semantic_project_scope.test.ts).
- **`image_shrink.enabled` config toggle.** Defaults to `true`; setting it to `false` (`token-goat config set image_shrink.enabled false`) skips the shrink-on-Read intercept entirely and passes large images through unshrunk, for users who want the raw image regardless of size. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/image_shrink.ts](src/image_shrink.ts); regression-tested in [tests/image_shrink.test.ts](tests/image_shrink.test.ts).
- **Diagnostic for languages with no symbol extractor at all.** Swift, Scala, Lua, Elixir, Dart, and Zig/R files previously indexed to zero symbols indistinguishably from a genuinely empty file. `outline`/`skeleton` now report e.g. "Swift has no symbol extractor yet, so this file always indexes to 0 symbols regardless of its contents" instead of the generic "no symbols found" message for these languages. See [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **`write-file`/`replace` dropped the destination file's mode on every rewrite.** `atomicWriteBuffer` (cli.ts) and `atomicWriteCore` (util.ts) both created their temp file at `0o600` and renamed it over the destination, so the new inode always carried `0o600` regardless of the file's actual mode -- on POSIX, rewriting a committed executable (a `chmod +x` hook script, a binary) via `write-file` or `replace` silently dropped the exec bit, and git would record it as a `100755->100644` mode change. Both now `stat` the existing destination and `chmod` the temp file to match before the rename, falling back to the `0o600` default only when the destination doesn't exist yet. No effect on Windows, which has no POSIX mode bits. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested (platform-gated) in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).
- **`replace` could silently clobber a concurrent write to the rest of the file.** `cmdReplace` read the whole target file, computed the snippet replacement in memory, then rewrote the WHOLE file via `atomicWriteBuffer`. The snippet match only protected the matched region -- a concurrent write to any OTHER part of the file between the initial read and the final rename was silently lost (last-writer-wins over the entire file), even though the snippet match itself succeeded and reported no error. `cmdReplace` now captures the target's `mtimeMs`/`size` right after the initial read and re-checks them immediately before the rename, aborting with a clear error ("changed on disk ... replace was NOT applied") instead of overwriting the concurrent change. Best-effort, not a lock: a race between the re-check and the rename itself is accepted residual risk, consistent with this codebase's other optimistic-concurrency patterns (e.g. `config set`'s `withFileLock`). See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).
- **The MCP `semantic` tool had no way to override the server process's own (often opaque) cwd.** `semantic` is the only MCP-exposed tool among the just-scoped project-root commands (`map`/`semantic`/`find`/`dead`/`stats` -- the rest of that set are CLI-only, not MCP tools); it always scoped searches to `process.cwd()`, which for an MCP client can be a cwd unrelated to the actual workspace root, silently returning empty or wrong-project results. The tool now accepts an optional `projectRoot` argument (matching `runChanged`'s existing `projectRoot` naming convention) that overrides the default `process.cwd()` scope. See [src/mcp_server.ts](src/mcp_server.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested against the real MCP protocol layer in [tests/mcp_server_semantic_scope.test.ts](tests/mcp_server_semantic_scope.test.ts).
- **The markdown large-file hint suggested sections that don't exist in the file.** The per-basename "well-known sections" shortcut list (e.g. README → Installation/Usage/API/Configuration/Getting Started) was emitted verbatim regardless of whether the target file actually had those headings, sending a `token-goat section` follow-up command straight into a 404. The hint now filters the list down to headings that actually exist in the file (case-insensitive match) before suggesting them. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **`config set` had an unlocked read-modify-write: two concurrent calls could silently drop one key.** `config set` loaded the persisted config, mutated one key in memory, and saved the whole file back — with no locking, a second concurrent `config set` (even on an unrelated key) that loaded before the first one saved would clobber the first writer's change with no error. Now wrapped in the same `withFileLock` primitive `session_store.ts` already uses for its own read-modify-write, falling back to the old unprotected path only if the lock can't be acquired in time. (Along the way, fixed a related bug the regression test surfaced: the lock file's parent directory wasn't guaranteed to exist before the lock was attempted, which made `withFileLock` silently skip locking entirely — `writeFileSync(..., {flag:'wx'})` throws `ENOENT`, not `EEXIST`, against a missing directory.) See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **A truncated diff's hunk header overstated its own line counts.** `buildLineDiff`'s `@@ -x,N +x,M @@` header reported the full pre-truncation removed/added line counts even when the body below it was capped at 50 changed lines, so the header no longer matched what the body actually showed on any diff over that size. The header now reports the counts the (possibly truncated) body actually contains. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **Every hook event double-spawned a node process, up to four spawns per tool call.**
 Each of the six bridges (Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI, OpenClaw, opencode, pi) had its harness-spawned shim or in-process plugin `spawnSync` a *second* full `token-goat hook <event>` process for every hook call. Under sustained tool-calling this process-creation churn was a confirmed structural cause of Windows crashes under Codex (empirically 2/3 crash rate with hooks enabled vs. 0/3 disabled). OpenClaw, opencode, and pi (long-lived in-process plugin hosts) now import a sibling `dist/token-goat-hook.mjs` hook library and call its exported `relayInProcess()` directly, with zero process spawns.
