Codex, Claude Code, and Copilot CLI (harness-spawned shims) now `import()` the same hook library in-process instead of spawning a second process, halving their spawn count; Claude Code's shim also lost its slow `shell: true` spawn path in the same change. Every remaining `spawnSync` fallback (used only when the in-process import fails) now carries an explicit `timeout`/`killSignal` so a stuck fallback degrades to token-goat's own fail-open `{}` rather than being force-killed by the harness's own timeout budget. See [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts), [src/hook_lib.ts](src/hook_lib.ts), [src/bridges/codex.ts](src/bridges/codex.ts), [src/bridges/claudecode.ts](src/bridges/claudecode.ts), [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts), [src/bridges/openclaw.ts](src/bridges/openclaw.ts), [src/bridges/opencode.ts](src/bridges/opencode.ts), [src/bridges/pi.ts](src/bridges/pi.ts); regression-tested end-to-end against the real built bundles in [tests/bridges/inprocess.test.ts](tests/bridges/inprocess.test.ts). Along the way, also fixed a genuine pre-existing syntax bug in the pi extension template (an unescaped `\n` collapsed into a real newline at build time, corrupting the exported script into invalid TypeScript) — regression-tested in [tests/install_pi.test.ts](tests/install_pi.test.ts).
- **A bounded, small offset/limit `Read` of an oversized markdown file was hard-denied anyway.** The markdown large-file intercept denied any first read of a file at or above the large-file deny threshold outright, never checking `offset`/`limit` first — unlike the generic large-file gate and the file-type dispatcher, which both estimate the requested slice's size and let a small bounded window through. A small, targeted `Read` into a huge `.md`/`.mdx`/`.markdown`/`.rst` file now gets served instead of denied when the requested slice itself is comfortably under the deny threshold; a whole-file read (no `offset`/`limit`, or a still-too-large slice) is still denied exactly as before. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **Renamed or deleted directories orphaned index rows forever.** The dirty-queue drain loop only reconciled a deletion when the exact old path had been enqueued via the Edit hook and no longer existed on disk — a `git mv`, directory rename, `git checkout <branch>`, or `git clean` never fires an Edit hook for the old paths, so those rows survived in the index indefinitely and `symbol`/`semantic`/`read` kept resolving deleted files. The worker's drain loop now also runs an opportunistic `pruneDeletedFiles` sweep every 30th drain cycle, scoped to the project root it opportunistically learns from the dirty paths it processes. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/index_prune.ts](src/index_prune.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **Three inconsistent conventions for resolving "the current project root," one of them missing a git/`findProject` step entirely.** `token-goat changed` used `opts.projectRoot ?? process.cwd()` then unconditionally overrode it with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; `token-goat resume` used `findProject(process.cwd())?.root ?? process.cwd()` with no git step; `token-goat context-stats` used a bare `path.resolve(opts.project ?? process.cwd())` with neither a git nor a `findProject` step, so it silently scoped to whatever subdirectory it was invoked from instead of the real project root. All three now call one shared `resolveProjectRoot()` helper (explicit param → git-toplevel/`findProject` resolution → cwd fallback, canonicalized so a Windows uppercase drive letter from `git rev-parse` doesn't drift from the rest of the codebase's path comparisons). See [src/project.ts](src/project.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/resume.ts](src/resume.ts), [src/cli_context_stats.ts](src/cli_context_stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/project.test.ts](tests/project.test.ts).
- **`collectElements` re-descended into a matched element's own subtree, contradicting its own docstring.** The docstring promised it "without descending further into a match's own subtree" (mirroring its sibling `collectTextRuns`), but the code used a bare `if` for the recursive walk instead of `else if`, so a tag nested inside itself was collected twice — once for the outer match, once again for the inner one it should have skipped. Changed to `else if`, matching `collectTextRuns`. See [src/ooxml_extract.ts](src/ooxml_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/ooxml_extract.test.ts](tests/ooxml_extract.test.ts).
- **`csv-profile`/`csv-query` exited 0 with zero output on an empty or header-only CSV.** Every other format handler (`section`, `read`, `symbol`, `xlsx-sheets`, `pdf-meta`) prints a clear message on a miss; these two silently printed nothing at all, indistinguishable from a hang or a broken pipe. Both now print "No data rows found in `<file>`" to stdout (exit code unchanged at 0 — a CSV with no data rows is a valid, non-error result, not a "target not found" miss). See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`xlsx-sheets`/`xlsx-head`/`xlsx-range`/`xlsx-query` leaked ExcelJS's raw internal jszip parse error for a non-`.xlsx`/corrupt file.** A file that isn't a valid zip produced `Can't find end of central directory : is this a zip file ? If it is, see https://stuk.github.io/jszip/documentation/howto/read_zip.html` verbatim on stderr — a jszip-internal message and docs URL, not a token-goat-authored one. The shared `loadWorkbook` read path (used by all four commands) now catches that specific failure and re-throws a clean `not a valid .xlsx file: <path>` error instead; ExcelJS's own already-clean "File not found" message for a missing path is passed through unchanged. See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts).

## [2.6.12] - 2026-07-10

### Fixed

- **`semantic`'s ranked results silently reverted to raw distance order.** `searchSemantic` computed a reranked `adjusted` score (verbatim-token boost, generated-path penalty) but never attached it to the returned hits; `mergeNearbyHits` then re-sorted purely by raw cosine distance, discarding the rerank entirely. A closer-but-generated-path chunk (`node_modules/`, `dist/`) could outrank an intentionally-boosted project-source chunk. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested end-to-end through the real `semantic` command in [tests/semantic_rerank_order_survives_merge.test.ts](tests/semantic_rerank_order_survives_merge.test.ts).
- **Every hook call on a non-Claude-Code harness (Codex, opencode, pi, Gemini, Grok, Copilot CLI, OpenClaw) got a fresh random session id.** `getSessionId()` only read `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, which only Claude Code itself sets; every other bridge delivers session id solely via the wire payload, never seeded into that env var. Since each hook invocation is a separate process, read-dedup, reread-diffing, context-pressure tiering, and manifest continuity all silently reset every call on those harnesses. The relay now seeds `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` from the wire session id on dispatch, before any handler runs. See [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts); regression-tested in [tests/relay.test.ts](tests/relay.test.ts).
- **The pre_compact manifest silently dropped a subagent's edits.** The parent thread's manifest read only its own (unsalted) session-state blob; every subagent spawned during the session writes into a separate `agent_id`-salted blob (introduced in 2.6.11 to fix a false "already read" cross-subagent deny), so a subagent's edits never appeared in the compaction manifest the parent most needed to preserve them across. The manifest builder now merges sibling subagent blobs' file entries in. See [src/hooks_compact.ts](src/hooks_compact.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts).
- **`session-summary`/`compact-hint`/`cost --session` (with no explicit session id) could resolve to a subagent's narrow blob instead of the parent session.** These commands picked the most-recently-modified session file with no filter, and a subagent's salted blob is often the newest file on disk. Latest-session resolution now excludes agent-salted blobs. See [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts), [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts).
- **`token-goat symbol`/`refs`/`skeleton`/`outline`'s `--json` output had no size guard**, unlike their text output (fixed in 2.6.11) -- JSON mode could still emit an unbounded row count. Now caps rows and adds `truncated`/`totalCount` fields when the cap is hit. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/overflow_guard.ts](src/overflow_guard.ts).
- **`semantic`'s own text output had no overflow guard at all**, unlike every other surgical-read command, and its truncation hint (once added) pointed at `symbol`'s `file.py::Class.method`/`--json` remediation, which doesn't apply to semantic search. Now routes through the overflow guard with a dedicated hint pointing at query narrowing and `--limit`. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/overflow_guard.ts](src/overflow_guard.ts).
- **`token-goat config` errors printed twice** -- once from an explicit `emitErr()` call and again when the CLI's generic error wrapper caught and printed the same thrown error. Now prints once; an unrecognized config key also gets a "did you mean X?" suggestion. See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts).
- **GraphQL SDL block-string and single-line descriptions could register as phantom type/operation/fragment symbols** when their text happened to match a declaration pattern (e.g. `"""type Foo represents a user"""`). Descriptions are now masked before the declaration regexes run. See [src/languages/graphql_idx.ts](src/languages/graphql_idx.ts).
- **SQL DDL keywords inside a single-quoted string literal (dynamic SQL, e.g. `EXECUTE 'CREATE TABLE audit_log (...)'`) registered a phantom object.** String literals are now masked before DDL matching -- while leaving double-quoted delimited identifiers (`CREATE TABLE "user"`) untouched, since an initial version of this fix incorrectly masked those too and silently dropped every real symbol with a quoted/reserved-word name. See [src/languages/sql_idx.ts](src/languages/sql_idx.ts).
- **Apex's `//` comment stripping ran before string masking**, so a `//` inside a string literal (e.g. a URL) blanked everything to end-of-line, which could delete a method's closing brace on the same line and corrupt parsing of subsequent symbols. String literals are now masked first. See [src/languages/apex.ts](src/languages/apex.ts).
- **Copilot CLI's session-id fallback used `process.pid`**, which differs on every hook invocation since Copilot spawns a fresh process per call -- any session missing an explicit `sessionId` in its payload never accumulated dedup/state across calls. Now derives a stable fallback from a hash of the working directory. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts).
- **A denied oversized-markdown first read was still recorded as read**, so a follow-up offset/limit retry hit the generic "already read" 2nd-read deny instead of the intended heading-tree guidance. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts).
- **`embed_sha` was never stamped when embeddings were disabled**, so the unchanged-file skip gate never held and every re-touch of an unchanged file needlessly re-entered the embedding check on every drain. Now stamped with a disabled-marker value that still triggers a real first embed once embeddings are re-enabled. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **C# raw-string closer masking used the opener's quote-run length instead of the matched closer's**, leaving stray `"` characters unmasked whenever a closer had more quotes than its opener. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/multiline_string_masking.test.ts](tests/multiline_string_masking.test.ts).

## [2.6.11] - 2026-07-10

### Added

- **`token-goat stats` (bare, no flags) now renders with the same rich TTY header and KPI section as `--full`**, instead of flat plain text on a real terminal. Only the by-source/by-command/by-day/by-project/insights breakdown sections are omitted; a muted hint still points at `--full` for those. Non-TTY (piped) output and `--json` are unchanged. See [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts), [src/render/stats_renderer.ts](src/render/stats_renderer.ts); regression-tested in [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts) and [tests/render.test.ts](tests/render.test.ts).
- **Windows CI job.** `ci.yml` gated only on `ubuntu-latest`, despite this being a Windows-first product with a changelog dominated by Windows-only bugs (`spawnSync shell:true`, bare-`.CMD` argv0, `PROGRAMFILES` env overrides) that Linux CI structurally cannot catch. Added a `windows-latest` job running the full suite. See [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml).
- **`publish.yml` now gates on the test suite and a real tarball smoke test** before publishing, closing the gap that let a prior `dist/.npmignore`-packing bug ship undetected. `npm pack` is installed into a clean prefix on both Windows and Linux shapes and exercised with `--version`, `index`, and `symbol` against the real installed binary. See [.github/workflows/publish.yml](.github/workflows/publish.yml).

### Fixed

- **Windows paths with `%TEMP%` pinned to its 8.3 short-name form (e.g. `JOHNDO~1.ACM`) got two different index/cache keys for the same physical directory.** Every `os.tmpdir()`-based path inherited the short form, while `git` always emits long-form paths, so `changed --symbol` and any other path-keyed lookup (worker `blocked_roots`, doc-compact sidecars, project canonicalization) silently missed matches depending on which side the path came from. `fs.realpathSync` (the POSIX-style implementation) does not resolve 8.3 short names on Windows; only `fs.realpathSync.native` does. Added `expandShortPath`, scoped to just the path segment that looks like a short name so the OS lookup can't silently case-fold the rest of the path (which would otherwise break case-sensitivity behavior), and wired it into `normalizePath` and `project.ts`'s `canonicalize`. Also routed `doc_compact.ts`'s `compactPathFor` through `normalizePath` so its sidecar key stays consistent whether the caller passes a raw or pre-normalized path. See [src/paths.ts](src/paths.ts), [src/project.ts](src/project.ts), [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/paths.test.ts](tests/paths.test.ts).
- **A BOM'd file lost its line-1 symbol on the worker's real shipping path.** `parseFile` stripped a leading UTF-8 BOM before parsing, but `indexFileSync` -- the function the worker's dirty-queue drain actually calls -- did not, so every `^`-anchored extractor (markdown headings, YAML/TOML/INI/env column-0 keys, C#/Kotlin/PowerShell headers) silently dropped whatever was on line 1 of a BOM'd file. The BOM is now stripped once inside `parseContent` itself so both entry points inherit the fix. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested via a real worker-drain (not mock-callback) test in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`token-goat index` exited 0 even when every file in the run failed to index.** `cmdIndex` counted failures but never set `process.exitCode`, so a completely broken index (`indexed: 0, failed: N`) reported success to any script checking `$?`. Now exits nonzero when nothing indexed and at least one file failed. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser_read_failure_swallow.test.ts](tests/parser_read_failure_swallow.test.ts).
- **The embedding model/session was rebuilt from scratch on every file during a bulk index**, since `@xenova/transformers`'s `pipeline()` has no built-in memoization -- a multi-thousand-file index paid full model + ONNX session construction once per file. Now memoized per model name at module scope. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/embeddings_pipeline_memoization.test.ts](tests/embeddings_pipeline_memoization.test.ts).
- **`token-goat index` re-parsed and re-embedded every file on every run, even unchanged ones.** The worker's incremental sha-gate was never hoisted into the bulk CLI path. Now an unchanged file skips both the syntactic reindex and the embedding step, and the run reports how many files were skipped. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cmdindex_unchanged_skip.test.ts](tests/cmdindex_unchanged_skip.test.ts).
- **Embeddings could go permanently stale relative to their file's sha gate.** `makeIndexer` stamped `files.sha` before firing an un-awaited embedding call; a daemon crash or swallowed embed error left the sha "current" while chunks stayed stale or missing forever, since the next touch of identical content was sha-gate-skipped. Parse-freshness and embed-freshness are now tracked independently via a new `files.embed_sha` column, so a crashed/failed embed is retried on the next drain even when the file's content (and parse-sha) hasn't changed. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **Every path-scoped SQL lookup on a case-insensitive filesystem was a full table scan.** `pathEqClause()` emitted `TG_LOWER(file_path) = ?`, and SQLite cannot use a btree index through a custom function -- every symbol/ref/section/embedding lookup by path scanned the whole table, measured at 135ms vs. 0ms on a real 300MB+ global index. Fixed with `CREATE INDEX ... ON table(TG_LOWER(file_path))` expression indexes, verified via `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` to now use `SEARCH ... USING INDEX`. See [src/db.ts](src/db.ts); regression-tested in [tests/db.test.ts](tests/db.test.ts) and [tests/sql_path.test.ts](tests/sql_path.test.ts).
- **A path stuck behind a transient read lock (AV scanner, editor, OneDrive sync) stayed permanently unindexed for the daemon's lifetime, even after a fresh edit.** `resetTransientRetryCount` was called from the short-lived hook CLI process, but the retry counter it reset was an in-memory `Map` living only in the detached daemon process -- the reset never reached the process that actually enforced the cap. Retry counts are now persisted in a `files.retry_count` column, making the database (not per-process memory) the source of truth so a hook-triggered reset is visible on the daemon's next drain cycle. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/db.ts](src/db.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **Multi-line string literals (PHP heredoc/nowdoc, Kotlin/C# triple-quoted raw strings, C# verbatim strings, PowerShell here-strings) desynced brace-depth tracking in the regex-based language adapters**, mis-parenting or dropping every symbol after a `{`/`}` character embedded in one of these string forms. Added a shared, carried-state multi-line string masking pass (mirroring the existing block-comment carried-state design) and wired it into the C#, PHP, Kotlin, and PowerShell adapters. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested across all four adapters in [tests/multiline_string_masking.test.ts](tests/multiline_string_masking.test.ts).
- **Harness misdetection: a bare `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` outranked `CODEX_SESSION_ID`/`GROK_SESSION_ID`/other harness session-id signals**, so any environment carrying both (normal for Grok and Codex, which can ride Claude Code's own credential surface) silently misdetected as `claudecode`, disabling that harness's wire-format translation with zero errors. The bare-API-key fallback now runs after every harness-specific session-id check, matching the treatment already applied for Hermes. See [src/bridges/registry.ts](src/bridges/registry.ts); regression-tested in [tests/bridges/registry.test.ts](tests/bridges/registry.test.ts).
- **Cached build-tool output (`tsc`, `make`, `cargo`, `dotnet`, `mvn`, `webpack`, `vite build`, etc.) was never fingerprinted for staleness**, unlike test/lint/git output -- an entry with no fingerprint is treated as permanently fresh, so a stale build/typecheck result kept being actively recalled as current after a source edit. Fingerprinting now covers every command matched by the existing build-command recognizer. See [src/bash_output_cache.ts](src/bash_output_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts](tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts).
- **A curl re-download deny never checked whether the previously-downloaded file still existed**, so deleting or moving it mid-session made that URL permanently undownloadable for the rest of the session with no recovery path. Now checks existence before denying and clears the stale session record if the file is gone. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), [src/session.ts](src/session.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **Grok's session id was dropped on every hook event except pre/post-tool-use.** Grok's wire payload uses camelCase (`sessionId`), and while it inherits Claude Code's full hook wiring, session-id extraction only checked snake_case `session_id` -- so `stop`/`pre_compact`/`notification`/etc. resolved to an empty session id, breaking compaction manifests and persistence for Grok specifically. Session-id extraction now falls back to `sessionId` when `session_id` is absent. See [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts); regression-tested in [tests/relay.test.ts](tests/relay.test.ts).
- **`token-goat symbol`/`refs`/`skeleton`/`outline` had no output-size guard**, unlike `read`/`section` -- a broad symbol match or a large file's skeleton could dump unbounded output. All four now route through the same overflow guard, activating a previously-unreachable hint case. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`cat file1 file2` bypassed the read-hook deny entirely**, since the extractor only matched a single anchored path -- strictly worse than `cat file1` alone, which was correctly denied. Multi-file `cat` invocations are now detected and denied the same way. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **Cached-artifact recall hints never mentioned `token-goat read "<path>@START-END"`**, the only way to reach an arbitrary middle slice of a large cached artifact -- only `--tail`/`--grep` were advertised. Added to the hint text. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **A subagent's genuinely-first read of a file got falsely denied as "already read" when a sibling subagent in the same session had read it**, since the session-level read-dedup ledger is keyed only on `session_id`, which every subagent sharing a parent session also shares. The ledger key is now salted with an `agent_id` signal when the hook payload carries one, so sibling agents get independent read-tracking. See [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts), [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts); regression-tested with a real spawned-process end-to-end scenario in [tests/session_persistence_e2e.test.ts](tests/session_persistence_e2e.test.ts).
- **The first read of a large `tasks/*.output` file was never size-gated**, unlike every other large-file path in the same handler -- a 57KB+ first read went through unsized with only an advisory hint attached. Large first reads are now denied in favor of `token-goat bash-output --file <path> --tail N`, matching the treatment already given to markdown and generic large files. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **Scoped `git status`/`git diff --stat` reruns with byte-identical output had no recall/dedup**, unlike `gh api` and build-tool output -- a review-loop workflow re-running the same scoped status/diff check several times got no cache hit. Extended the existing recall-dedup gate to cover these, invalidated on a working-tree edit to the scoped path or a HEAD change. See [src/bash_output_cache.ts](src/bash_output_cache.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts](tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts) and [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **A green local pre-push did not reliably predict a green CI.** `.lefthook-scripts/run-test.sh`/`wsl-test.sh` pinned `TOKEN_GOAT_NO_WORKER_SPAWN`, `TOKEN_GOAT_HARNESS_OVERRIDE`, and `TOKEN_GOAT_MEMORY_PRESSURE_MB` for local test runs, but CI ran with none of them pinned. Moved the pins into the shared vitest setup so local and CI runs use the same test environment. See [tests/setup/isolate-home.ts](tests/setup/isolate-home.ts).
- **Gemini CLI's hook deny contract was assumed compatible with token-goat's wire format but never verified.** Confirmed directly against Gemini CLI's own hook reference docs that its `BeforeTool` deny shape (`{"decision":"block"|"deny","reason":...}`) is exactly what `serializeOutput` already emits -- no translation layer was actually missing, but nothing proved it either. Added a regression test driving a real production deny handler through Gemini's detected wire format. See [tests/relay.test.ts](tests/relay.test.ts).


## [2.6.10] - 2026-07-09

### Added

- Grok CLI compatibility: token-goat's existing Claude Code hook install already covers Grok CLI (`grok inspect` confirmed it executes the global `~/.claude/settings.json` hooks config unmodified), but Grok's wire payload is camelCase throughout (`toolName`/`toolInput`/`sessionId`) with its own tool-name vocabulary (`read_file`, `write`, `search_replace`, `run_terminal_command`, `grep`, `list_dir`), unlike Codex/Gemini's snake_case-with-native-tool-names shape. `normalizePayload()` now translates Grok's payload to token-goat's canonical shape, `detectHarness()` recognizes `GROK_SESSION_ID`, and `grok` is a new `HarnessName`. Note: Grok does not honor the PreToolUse exit-code-2 deny contract, confirmed empirically — a denying hook still lets the tool call through.
- **`token-goat stats --full`.** Bare `token-goat stats` now prints only the short totals block (total events / bytes saved / tokens saved / window) plus a hint pointing to `--full` for the previous complete breakdown (by source, by command, by day). `--full` restores the prior default output unchanged; `--json` is unaffected either way. See [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts), [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts) and [tests/cli_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_stats.test.ts).
- **Salesforce Apex and metadata-XML symbol indexing.** New regex adapters index `.cls`/`.trigger` Apex source (classes, interfaces, triggers, methods) and Salesforce metadata XML (`.object`, `.field-meta.xml`, `.validationRule-meta.xml`, `.permissionset-meta.xml`, `.profile-meta.xml`, `.md-meta.xml`, and related suffixes) for CustomObject, CustomField, ValidationRule, PermissionSet, Profile, and CustomMetadata symbols. Metadata files above 512 KB, and all `.profile-meta.xml` files (frequently multi-megabyte, highly repetitive permission dumps), are excluded from embeddings to avoid low-signal vector noise — exact symbol/read/grep access is unaffected. Contributed by @krzysztofwojt. See [src/languages/apex.ts](src/languages/apex.ts), [src/languages/salesforce_metadata.ts](src/languages/salesforce_metadata.ts); tested in [tests/salesforce_languages.test.ts](tests/salesforce_languages.test.ts), [tests/embeddings_index_wiring.test.ts](tests/embeddings_index_wiring.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **`token-goat symbol` returned an empty body preview for Salesforce metadata symbols.** The metadata adapter above stores an empty `body` for these symbols by design (to keep the index small), and `token-goat read` already reconstructed the preview from the file's source span when `body` was empty — but `token-goat symbol` had no equivalent fallback, so every Salesforce metadata match showed a bare header with no preview. Fixed by mirroring `read`'s disk-reconstruction fallback in `runSymbol`. Also replaced the 19-branch `if`/`else if` chain dispatching non-tree-sitter language extraction with a `Partial<Record<Language, extractor>>` lookup table (`NO_TREE_SITTER_EXTRACTORS` in `src/parser.ts`), so adding a new regex adapter is one map entry instead of a new branch. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **A bash here-string (`<<<`) was misdetected as an unterminated heredoc.** `detectUnbalancedShellSyntax` only checked for two `<` characters before parsing a heredoc delimiter, so `<<<` was consumed as a two-char `<<` opener on one loop iteration and re-matched as a second `<<` opener on the next, swallowing the here-string's argument (e.g. `"hello world"`) as a bogus heredoc delimiter that never terminates. Any Bash tool call using a here-string (`cat <<< "$var"`) got a spurious "unbalanced shell syntax" warning. Fixed by treating a third consecutive `<` as a here-string and skipping past it as ordinary bare code. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **The Terraform-plan resource-block compressor's regex never matched real `terraform plan` output.** It required `resource "..."` to follow only whitespace, but real plan output always prefixes changed resources with a `+`/`~`/`-` change marker (e.g. `  + resource "aws_instance" "web" {`), so the `(known after apply)`-noise compression was dead on real input. Fixed to allow an optional change marker before `resource`. See [src/tool_filters/cloud.ts](src/tool_filters/cloud.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_cloud.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_cloud.test.ts).
- **The git-blame author regex broke under `-C`/`-M`/multi-file blame.** It required the commit hash to be immediately followed by the author parenthesis, but `git blame -C`/`-M` and multi-path blame insert a filename column between them, breaking same-commit-run collapsing exactly for the large-output cases (moved/copied hunks, multi-file blame) that most need it. Fixed to optionally consume a filename token between hash and author. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **Pre-push failed-test-output truncation never reset, silently dropping every failure block after the first.** The 30-line error cap latched `inError` permanently true and never re-armed after the one-time "+N omitted" marker, so a second distinct test failure (and any content between failures) vanished with no trace for the rest of the output. Fixed to scope the cap per error block (reset at a blank-line boundary) with an accurate running omitted-line counter instead of a one-shot estimate. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **Pylint's per-error-code output cap was global across the whole run instead of per-module, and could make a later module's output vanish entirely.** Once one module exhausted a code's cap (3 occurrences), every later module's issues of that same code were treated as already over-cap -- and the over-cap path never flushed the pending module header, so a module whose issues were entirely over-cap disappeared from the output with no trace. Fixed by scoping the cap per module and flushing the module header in the over-cap path too. See [src/tool_filters/linters.ts](src/tool_filters/linters.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_linters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_linters.test.ts).
- **A file stuck behind a persistent read lock (AV scanner, editor, OneDrive sync) stayed permanently unindexed for the daemon's process lifetime.** `requeueDirtyPath`'s transient-retry cap (5 attempts) was only cleared on a *successful* read, contradicting its own doc comment's claim that a later edit gives the path "a fresh retry budget" -- the edit-driven re-queue path in a different module never touched the retry counter. Fixed by resetting the counter when a path is freshly re-dirtied by an edit. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts) and [src/hooks_index.ts](src/hooks_index.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).
- **`bash-output` cache staleness detection silently broke on a quoted path with a space, serving stale content forever.** `extractLsTarget`/`extractCatTarget` split the command on raw whitespace, so `cat "release notes.txt"` extracted the garbage token `"release`, which failed to resolve to a real path -- the fingerprint ended up empty, and an empty fingerprint is unconditionally treated as fresh. Fixed both to use the same quote-aware tokenizer already used elsewhere in the same file. See [src/bash_output_cache.ts](src/bash_output_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts](tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts).
- **`token-goat semantic`'s generated-path ranking penalty silently skipped capitalized build directories.** `_isGeneratedPath` compared raw path segments against a lowercase-only set with no case-folding, so projects with `Dist/`/`Build/`/`Target/` (common in .NET/Java-style repos) never got their build artifacts demoted in ranking. Fixed to fold case before the lookup. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/embeddings.test.ts](tests/embeddings.test.ts).
- **The PowerShell adapter misclassified any class whose name merely contains the substring "enum" (e.g. `class EnumHelper`) as an enum.** `kind` was derived from a whole-line `/enum/i` test instead of the actually-captured `class`/`enum` keyword. Fixed to derive `kind` from the captured keyword group. See [src/languages/powershell_idx.ts](src/languages/powershell_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **The PHP adapter misclassified a function nested inside a class method as a direct method of that class.** Method detection had no brace-depth gate relative to the class body (unlike the equivalent kotlin.ts/powershell_idx.ts adapters), so `function baz(){}` nested inside `function bar(){}` inside `class Foo` was indexed as `Foo::baz` instead of a local function. Fixed by gating method classification on brace depth exactly one level inside the class's own body. See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **The Makefile adapter produced spurious `makefile_target` symbols from script code inside a `define...endef` block.** Nothing masked the body between `define` and `endef` before the target-detection regex scanned the whole file, so a self-documenting-Makefile's embedded Python/shell script (a common pattern) could contain a colon-bearing line that looked like a target declaration. Fixed by masking `define`/`endef` block bodies before target detection. See [src/languages/makefile_idx.ts](src/languages/makefile_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

## [2.6.9] - 2026-07-09

### Added

- **`video-chapters` for embedded video chapter markers.** Reads chapter timestamps/titles and subtitle-stream metadata out of a video file via `ffprobe -show_chapters -show_streams`, so an agent can see a video's structure without downloading or transcoding it. Gated on ffprobe being present on PATH (cached availability check); degrades with a clear "ffprobe not found on PATH; video-chapters requires ffmpeg" message when it isn't installed, the same graceful-degradation shape used for optional npm dependencies, just gated on an external binary instead of a package. See [src/video_chapters.ts](src/video_chapters.ts).
- **`sharepoint-resolve` for SharePoint/OneDrive sharing URLs.**
 Resolves a share link to a local synced file path purely from the filesystem and `OneDrive`/`OneDriveCommercial` env vars -- no network call, no Graph API, no credentials, since OneDrive's local sync-folder layout is undocumented and best-effort by nature. Tries the library path as-is, then the "Shared Documents" -> "Documents" local alias, then scans multi-site sync roots for a folder matching the site name; reports an honest "could not resolve" with the paths it tried when nothing matches. See [src/sharepoint_resolve.ts](src/sharepoint_resolve.ts).
- **`csv-profile` and extended `csv-query --where`.**
 `csv-profile` gives a per-column type/null/distinct/range summary of a CSV so an agent understands its shape without reading every row. `csv-query --where` is now repeatable and ANDed, and supports `col!=value`, `col>value`, `col<value`, and `col~=regex` in addition to the original `col=value` equality filter; `--delimiter <char>` and `--no-header` handle non-comma-delimited or headerless files. `xlsx-query --where` gained the same operators and repeatability, since it shares `queryCsv`'s filter engine.
- **`pdf-outline`/`pdf-meta` readers
 and a `pdf-extract --layout` heuristic reconstruction mode.** `pdf-outline` lists a PDF's bookmark tree with page numbers so an agent can jump straight to the relevant section instead of extracting the whole document; `pdf-meta` reports page count, title/author, and whether a PDF has an extractable text layer, so a scanned/image-only PDF is identified before wasting a full `pdf-extract` call on it. `pdf-extract --layout` reconstructs rough reading order from each text item's x/y coordinates (row-grouped, left-to-right) instead of pdfjs's raw content-stream order, which otherwise interleaves columns on multi-column pages; documented as a heuristic, not a real layout engine. All three reuse the existing `pdfjs-dist` loader in [src/pdf_extract.ts](src/pdf_extract.ts).
- **`transcript-outline`/`transcript` narrow-slice readers for WebVTT/SRT transcript files.**
 Meeting recordings and video captions export as `.vtt`/`.srt` and can run to thousands of lines; reading one in full to find what one speaker said, or what was discussed in a time window, wasted most of the read on unrelated cues. `transcript-outline` gives a skimmable speaker list + time-bucketed marker overview; `transcript` filters cues by `--speaker`, `--from`/`--to`, and/or `--grep`. Zero new dependencies — pure string parsing of both formats' `TIMESTAMP --> TIMESTAMP` cue-block shape. `.vtt`/`.srt` files above 10 KB are now intercepted by the pre_read hook the same way large CSVs are. See [src/transcript_extract.ts](src/transcript_extract.ts); tested in [tests/transcript_extract.test.ts](tests/transcript_extract.test.ts).

- **`xlsx-sheets`/`xlsx-head`/`xlsx-range`/`xlsx-query`, `pptx-outline`/`pptx-slide`/`pptx-notes`/`pptx-text`, and `docx-outline`/`docx-text` narrow-slice readers for Excel, PowerPoint, and Word files.** Reading an entire spreadsheet or slide deck as raw text was the largest single-file token cost this tool didn't yet address; these commands mirror the existing `pdf-extract`/`csv-query` pattern (list structure first, then extract a bounded slice) instead. `xlsx-query`/`pptx-text` reuse the existing `queryCsv` filter engine and regex-grep dispatch rather than duplicating them. New optional dependencies: `xlsx` (SheetJS) for spreadsheets, `fflate` + `fast-xml-parser` for the shared pptx/docx OOXML zip+XML core (`src/ooxml_extract.ts`). See [src/xlsx_extract.ts](src/xlsx_extract.ts), [src/pptx_extract.ts](src/pptx_extract.ts), [src/docx_extract.ts](src/docx_extract.ts); tested in [tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts](tests/xlsx_extract.test.ts), [tests/pptx_extract.test.ts](tests/pptx_extract.test.ts), [tests/docx_extract.test.ts](tests/docx_extract.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **The pre_read hook redirected .xlsx/.pptx/.docx reads to `pandoc`, a tool this project never installs and which cannot read .xlsx at all.** `handleOfficeBinary` in `src/hints/file_type_handler.ts` blocked every Office binary read with a `pandoc "<file>" -t plain` suggestion regardless of format — for `.xlsx` this was never viable (pandoc's plain-text writer doesn't extract spreadsheet cell data), and for all three formats it assumed an external binary this project doesn't ship or check for. Fixed by splitting the dispatch: `.xlsx`/`.pptx`/`.docx` now route to the new dedicated `handleXlsx`/`handlePptx`/`handleDocx` handlers, which redirect to the new narrow-slice commands above; `.odt`/`.ods`/`.ott`/`.odp` (no dedicated reader yet) keep the original pandoc-redirect message. See [src/hints/file_type_handler.ts](src/hints/file_type_handler.ts); regression-tested in [tests/file_type_handler.test.ts](tests/file_type_handler.test.ts).

- **`pptx-outline`/`pptx-slide`/`pptx-notes`/`pptx-text` numbered slides by `slideN.xml` filename order instead of the deck's actual display order.** PowerPoint never renames `slideN.xml` parts when a deck is reordered, slides are duplicated, or slides are deleted — the physical filename reflects creation order, not display order, so any deck edited after its slides were first added (extremely common) had every slide number silently wrong. Fixed by resolving the real order from `ppt/presentation.xml`'s `<p:sldIdLst>` via `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels`, falling back to filename order only when those parts are missing. See [src/pptx_extract.ts](src/pptx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pptx_extract.test.ts](tests/pptx_extract.test.ts).
- **`sharepoint-resolve` dropped the first library-path segment when falling back to a multi-site sync root, and joined URL segments without filtering `.`/`..`.** The site-fallback branch reused a `.slice(1)`-truncated path meant only for the alias-substitution case, so a resolved path like `Contoso - TeamSite/Documents/Reports/budget.xlsx` was tried as `Contoso - TeamSite/Reports/budget.xlsx` and silently failed to resolve for any multi-site sync root; separately, `libraryPath` segments were joined via `path.join` with no `.`/`..` filtering, which is unreachable through `parseShareUrl`'s own `new URL()` normalization but was still an unguarded boundary for any caller constructing a `ParsedShareUrl` directly. Fixed the fallback to try the full segment list before the alias-substituted one, and added an explicit `.`/`..` filter at `resolveLocalPath`'s own boundary. See [src/sharepoint_resolve.ts](src/sharepoint_resolve.ts); regression-tested in [tests/sharepoint_resolve.test.ts](tests/sharepoint_resolve.test.ts).
- **`pdf-meta`'s text-layer detection only probed page 1**, so a PDF with a blank cover page or scanned first page but real searchable text later would be misreported as "no (likely scanned/image-only)". Fixed to sample the first, middle, and last pages. See [src/pdf_extract.ts](src/pdf_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pdf_extract.test.ts](tests/pdf_extract.test.ts).
- **`readOoxmlZip` (shared by the xlsx/pptx/docx readers) had no size guard before calling `fflate.unzipSync`**, which fully decompresses a zip eagerly and unstreamed — a crafted or corrupted archive near DEFLATE's ~1032:1 worst-case ratio could balloon memory well past the input's on-disk size. Added a 50MB compressed-input cap as a proportionate sanity check (not a hardened defense against a deliberately engineered zip bomb, which would need streaming decompression with an abort threshold). See [src/ooxml_extract.ts](src/ooxml_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/ooxml_extract.test.ts](tests/ooxml_extract.test.ts).
- **`docx-outline`/`docx-text` silently glued words together across a formatting boundary.** `parseOoxmlPart` left fast-xml-parser's `trimValues: true` default in place, which collapses a whitespace-only `<w:t xml:space="preserve"> </w:t>` run — Word's own way of holding just the inter-word space when a sentence is split across multiple `<w:r>` runs at a bold/italic/hyperlink boundary — down to an empty string with no `#text` key at all, dropping the space entirely (`"Hello" + "world"` instead of `"Hello world"`). Fixed by setting `trimValues: false`. See [src/ooxml_extract.ts](src/ooxml_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/ooxml_extract.test.ts](tests/ooxml_extract.test.ts).
- **`pptx-outline`'s `hasNotes` flag reported true for slides with no actual speaker notes.** It checked mere presence of the `notesSlideN.xml` ZIP part, but PowerPoint auto-creates that part for essentially every slide on save whether or not the user typed anything into the notes pane — the same distinction `pptx-notes` already accounted for by checking the notes body's actual text length. Fixed `pptxOutline` to use the same content check. See [src/pptx_extract.ts](src/pptx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pptx_extract.test.ts](tests/pptx_extract.test.ts).

- **Markdown semantic-embedding boundaries were capped at 40 headings, collapsing all later sections into one chunk range.** `buildEmbeddingBoundaries` reused `extractMarkdownHeadings`, which has a hard cap of `MAX_HEADINGS = 40` for display hints. For markdown files with >40 headings (large API references, changelogs, multi-section docs), only the first 40 boundaries were produced; every section from heading #41 to end-of-file was lumped into a single boundary with `end=Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so `chunkFile` windowed it purely by `MAX_CHUNK_CHARS` instead of heading granularity, diluting semantic-search relevance. The indexing critical path (symbol extraction and embedding) is the highest-priority subsystem. Fixed by adding an optional `limit` parameter to `extractMarkdownHeadings`, defaulting to `MAX_HEADINGS` for display hints but set to `Infinity` in `buildEmbeddingBoundaries` so all headings produce section boundaries. See [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts) and [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/markdown_embedding_boundaries_fix.test.ts](tests/markdown_embedding_boundaries_fix.test.ts).
- **Dotted Class.method disambiguation returned the wrong same-named method for regex-parsed languages.** `resolveSymbolSpec` disambiguates an ambiguous `Class.method` spec (two classes each defining `method` in one file) by filtering to candidates whose line range falls inside a symbol named Class. This works for tree-sitter languages with multi-line class spans, but regex-parsed languages (php, csharp, kotlin, powershell) store the parent class name in the symbol's `docstring` field and use single-line spans (lineStart === lineEnd). A method declared on any line after the class header would fail the containment check `c.lineEnd <= cls.lineEnd`, leaving the scoped set empty and falling through to `candidates[0]` (the FIRST same-named method). Concrete repro: index a PHP file with `class A { function foo(int $aParam){} } class B { function foo(string $bParam){} }` then `token-goat read "a.php::B.foo"` would return A's method body instead of B's. Fixed by checking the docstring field first — if a candidate's docstring (case-insensitively) matches symBase, it is the right method. This works for both regex adapters (single-line class spans with parent in docstring) and tree-sitter output (empty docstring, line-containment check). See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **Kotlin adapter indexed local functions and local vals inside a method body as if they were class members.** `extractKotlin` gated member detection with `depthInClass >= 1`, but a class method body itself sits at `depthInClass 1` — anything declared inside that body (a local `fun`, a local SCREAMING_SNAKE `val`) sits at `depthInClass 2+` and was ALSO matched, unlike the csharp/powershell adapters which correctly gate on `depthInClass === 1`. Fixed by changing the check to `=== 1`. See [src/languages/kotlin.ts](src/languages/kotlin.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **CSS symbol extraction indexed selectors from inside `/* */` block comments.** `extractCssSymbols` scanned raw lines for a leading `.`/`#` selector without stripping block comments first, so a commented-out selector (e.g. disabled legacy CSS) was indexed as if it were live. Fixed by running the shared `stripCstyleComments` helper (already used elsewhere for comment-aware scanning) over the content before the per-line scan, preserving line numbers. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser_languages.test.ts](tests/parser_languages.test.ts).
- **HTML/Liquid headings were computed but never indexed or reachable via the live `section` command.** `extractHtml`/`extractLiquid` compute `<h1>`-`<h6>` headings into a `.sections` array, but `extractSymbolsNoTreeSitter` only consumed `.symbols`, so headings never entered the index (unreachable via `symbol`/`skeleton`/`outline`) — unlike markdown/proto/graphql/sql, which push headings into both symbols and sections. Separately, the live `token-goat section` command's `findHeaders` had no HTML-aware finder, so html/liquid files fell through to the generic sniff logic (which only recognizes markdown `#` headings and `[table]` headers) and landed on the key-value finder, which never matches `<hN>` tags. Fixed by mapping `.sections` into indexable `SymbolEntry` rows in `extractSymbolsNoTreeSitter`, and adding an explicit `findHtmlHeaders` finder routed for the `html`/`liquid` languages in `findHeaders`. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts) and [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts) and [tests/section_reader.test.ts](tests/section_reader.test.ts).
- **TOML symbol extraction indexed spurious keys from inside multi-line `"""`/`'''` strings.** `extractTomlSymbols` scanned every line for a `key =` pattern with no awareness of an open multi-line string, so a value like `description = """\nfake_key = "x"\n"""` indexed `fake_key` as a real TOML key. Fixed by tracking whether a triple-quote span opened on an earlier line is still open (based on parity of `"""`/`'''` occurrences per line) and skipping key/section matching for lines fully inside that span. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser_languages.test.ts](tests/parser_languages.test.ts).
- **`csv-profile` crashed with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on numeric columns over ~65k rows.** `profileCsv` computed min/max via `Math.min(...nums)`/`Math.max(...nums)`, spreading every value as a separate function argument — V8 throws once the argument count crosses its call-stack-sized limit, well within the row counts of a realistic export (transaction logs, analytics dumps). Fixed by using `reduce` instead of spread. See [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts).
- **`pptx-notes`/`pptx-outline`'s `hasNotes` check could resolve the wrong slide's notes, or miss real notes entirely.** `notesPathFor` derived a slide's notes part by reusing the slide's own filename number (`slideN.xml` → `notesSlideN.xml`), but notes-slide numbering is a separate counter from slide numbering in OOXML — duplicating, deleting, or reordering slides (the same category of edit the presentation-order fix above was written to handle) can decouple the two, so a slide's real notes part could sit at a differently-numbered file, or the guessed filename could belong to a different slide's notes entirely. Fixed by resolving the notes part through the slide's actual `notesSlide` relationship in `ppt/slides/_rels/slideN.xml.rels` instead of guessing from the filename. See [src/pptx_extract.ts](src/pptx_extract.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pptx_extract.test.ts](tests/pptx_extract.test.ts).

- **`extractDocCompact` matched a `--heading` spec by substring instead of exact equality, silently returning the wrong section.** The heading branch used `(m[1] ?? '').includes(heading)`, so a shorter heading name (e.g. `Setup`) matched the first heading line that merely *contained* it as a substring (e.g. `## Setup Guide`), returning that unrelated section's content instead of the actual `## Setup` section or a no-match result -- with no error indicating the wrong content was returned. `resolveHeading` in `src/section_reader.ts` already does exact/normalized equality for this same reason; `extractDocCompact` did not follow that pattern. Fixed by requiring an exact match of the heading text. See [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_compact.test.ts](tests/doc_compact.test.ts).
- **The pi bridge's PATH-fallback hook call omitted `shell: true`, silently disabling every hook on Windows whenever the entry-path sidecar was missing or stale.** `callHook`'s fallback branch (taken when `resolveEntryPath()` can't find/verify the installed entry point) ran `spawnSync("token-goat", ["hook", event], ...)` with no `shell: true`; on Windows the global `token-goat` binary is a `.cmd` shim, and Node's `spawnSync` does not resolve `PATHEXT` extensions without `shell: true`, so the call threw `ENOENT` internally. Because `callHook` wraps everything in try/catch and returns `null` on error, this didn't crash -- it just made every pre/post-tool-use hook for pi (image-shrink, read-hints, dirty-queue updates) silently no-op with no visible error. The sibling Codex and Copilot CLI bridges were already fixed for this exact class of bug; pi's fallback was left on the old array-args, no-shell form. Fixed to match: a single shell-invoked command string with `shell: true`. See [src/bridges/pi.ts](src/bridges/pi.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_pi.test.ts](tests/install_pi.test.ts).
- **`snapshots.ts`'s `store()` wrote via a hand-rolled fixed `<path>.tmp` temp filename instead of the shared atomic-write helper, risking corruption from concurrent writers and no retry on Windows file locks.** `store()` built `tempPath = p + '.tmp'`, wrote it, then renamed it directly, rather than using `atomicWriteBytes` from `util.ts` -- the helper used elsewhere in the codebase (`project_memory.ts`, `skill_cache.ts`, `disk_cache.ts`) specifically to avoid this: it names the temp file with `<dest>.<pid>.<hrtime>.tmp` so concurrent writers to the same path can't collide, and wraps the rename in `withRetryOnLock` to survive transient Windows `EBUSY`/`EPERM` errors. This exact bug class was already fixed once in `project_memory.ts`'s `save()`; `snapshots.ts`'s `store()` was never migrated to match. Fixed by switching to `atomicWriteBytes`. See [src/snapshots.ts](src/snapshots.ts); regression-tested in [tests/snapshots.test.ts](tests/snapshots.test.ts).

- **`isInsideStringLiteral` only checked the single character before a quote to decide if it's escaped, instead of counting consecutive backslashes for escape parity.** A closing quote preceded by an escaped trailing backslash (e.g. a Windows path literal `"C:\Users\\"`) was misclassified as still escaped, so the string was never marked closed and a real trailing `/* comment */` was left unrecognized as a comment opener for csharp/kotlin/php/proto/sql language adapters. Fixed to skip escape pairs two characters at a time while inside a string, matching `stripStringLiterals`'s existing approach. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages_common.test.ts](tests/languages_common.test.ts).
- **`stripSqlLineComments` blanked everything after `--` with no awareness of quoted string literals, unlike every sibling comment-stripper in the same file.** A `--` inside a SQL string literal (e.g. `COMMENT ON COLUMN foo.bar IS 'discount -- see note'; CREATE TABLE Baz (id INT);`) silently deleted the rest of that physical line, including real SQL after it, so a table's symbol could go unindexed even though it exists in the source. Fixed to skip past `--` occurrences that fall inside a string literal, matching `stripHashComments`/`stripLineComment`. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages_common.test.ts](tests/languages_common.test.ts).
- **`writeCompact`/`markCompactStale` wrote the doc-compact sidecar with a raw `fs.writeFileSync` instead of the shared atomic-write helper.** A crash or Windows sharing-violation mid-write could leave an intact header (with the correct source-hash) paired with a truncated body, which `isCompactFresh` would still report as fresh and serve to the model as truncated content — silent data loss. Fixed by switching both to `atomicWriteText`. See [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_compact.test.ts](tests/doc_compact.test.ts).
- **`extractNamedSection` in the skill cache matched a `::heading` query by prefix instead of exact equality**, the same bug class already fixed once in `extractDocCompact`'s `--heading` handling. A shorter heading name (e.g. `Setup`) could silently match a longer, unrelated heading that merely starts with it (`## Setup Guide`), returning the wrong skill section. Fixed to exact match. See [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/skill_cache.test.ts](tests/skill_cache.test.ts).

- **`token-goat read "file::symbol"` silently returned the wrong body for an ambiguous, unqualified symbol name.** `resolveSymbolSpec` picked `candidates[0]` whenever multiple distinct symbols matched a bare name — most commonly same-named methods on sibling classes in one file (e.g. several tool-filter classes each defining `compress`), but also same-named top-level symbols across different files sharing a basename. Fixed to detect true ambiguity and return a clear error listing every candidate (file, parent, line) with a working, individually-resolvable retry command per candidate, instead of guessing. Exact single-match and already-qualified `Class::method` lookups are unaffected. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts) and [tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts](tests/worker_index_e2e.test.ts).
- **Case-insensitive path comparisons in the SQLite layer only folded ASCII casing, while the JS layer folded full Unicode — the two could disagree on non-ASCII filenames.** `pathEqClause` relied on SQLite's built-in `COLLATE NOCASE`/`LOWER()`, both ASCII-only, while `foldPath()` (used for the same case-insensitive-filesystem guarantee everywhere else) is Unicode-aware. Fixed by registering a custom deterministic SQL function (`TG_LOWER`) on the database connection that shares the exact same folding primitive as `foldPath()`, so SQL-side and JS-side comparisons can no longer diverge. See [src/db.ts](src/db.ts), [src/sql_path.ts](src/sql_path.ts), and [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested in [tests/sql_path.test.ts](tests/sql_path.test.ts).
- **MCP tool-call caching/dedup could misclassify a genuinely mutating tool as read-only, silently blocking a needed retry.** `isMcpReadOnly` used a fixed blocklist of mutating verbs, so any mutating method using a verb outside that list (`finalize_plan`, `approve`, `cancel`, `deploy`, `toggle`, `pin`, `grant`, `sync`, `commit`, `apply`, `trigger`, and others) was treated as safe to cache and dedupe — a second identical call within the TTL window got denied with a "recall the cached result" message even when the mutation genuinely needed to re-run. Fixed by inverting to a fail-safe allowlist of read verbs, with a second guard rejecting compound names that also contain a mutating-verb token (e.g. `get_or_create`, `search_and_update`) so those still correctly classify as mutating. See [src/mcp_cache.ts](src/mcp_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_cache.test.ts](tests/mcp_cache.test.ts).
- **The Gemini, OpenClaw, and OpenCode bridges could silently fail to invoke any hook on a global Windows install.** Gemini's installer wrote a bare `token-goat hook <event>` command into `~/.gemini/settings.json`, and OpenClaw/OpenCode's plugin scripts called `spawnSync("token-goat", ...)` directly — neither works against a global npm install's `.cmd`/`.ps1` shim without `shell: true`, the same class of bug already fixed for the Codex and Copilot CLI bridges. Fixed by porting the established exec-path + entry-path sidecar pattern to all three: Gemini's hook command now resolves `process.execPath` and the real entry path (with detection hardened to verify the path actually identifies token-goat, not just match the command's shape); OpenClaw/OpenCode's plugins read a `token-goat-entry.json` sidecar written at install time, falling back to a `shell: true` invocation if the sidecar is missing. See [src/bridges/gemini_install.ts](src/bridges/gemini_install.ts), [src/bridges/openclaw.ts](src/bridges/openclaw.ts), [src/bridges/openclaw_install.ts](src/bridges/openclaw_install.ts), [src/bridges/opencode.ts](src/bridges/opencode.ts), and [src/bridges/opencode_install.ts](src/bridges/opencode_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_gemini.test.ts](tests/install_gemini.test.ts), [tests/install_openclaw.test.ts](tests/install_openclaw.test.ts), and [tests/install_opencode.test.ts](tests/install_opencode.test.ts).
- **`installOpenclaw()` could leave a stray sidecar file behind after a failed install.** The entry-path sidecar was written before the config file's strict JSON parse, so a corrupt `openclaw.json` caused the install to abort *after* already writing to disk — breaking the function's own documented "abort before any write" guarantee. Fixed by moving the sidecar write to after the parse succeeds. See [src/bridges/openclaw_install.ts](src/bridges/openclaw_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_openclaw.test.ts](tests/install_openclaw.test.ts).
- **The PHP language adapter mis-parented every method of a class whose header spanned multiple lines** (e.g. `class Foo` followed by `implements Bar, Baz` on its own line before the opening brace) — the context frame popped immediately since net brace count was still zero on that line, so every method indexed as a top-level function instead of a member of `Foo`. Fixed by adding the same `bodyEntered` gate already used correctly in the sibling csharp/kotlin/powershell adapters. See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **The C# language adapter never indexed Allman-style auto-properties** (`public int Foo`, brace on its own line, `get; set;` on the next). `PROPERTY_RE` required the brace/accessor on the same line as the declaration, so any property written in standard Microsoft brace style was silently omitted from the index. Fixed by peeking ahead when a property-shaped header has no trailing brace, detecting the Allman-style accessor block on the following lines. See [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`DiffFilter` could split one file's diff into two spurious blocks.** Its file-boundary regex matched any `--- `-prefixed line, including a *removed* source line that happened to start with `-- ` (a SQL/Lua/Haskell comment, or a markdown rule) — corrupting the per-file hunk/truncation accounting. Fixed to require a real `---`/`+++` header pair (or a `diff `-prefixed line) before treating a line as a file boundary. Several tool-filter binary-dispatch checks (`grep`, `eza`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `jq`, `yq`, `curl`/`wget`) were also comparing the invoked binary's name case-sensitively, so a differently-cased invocation on Windows (`Bat.exe`) silently bypassed its intended filter — fixed to fold case before comparing. See [src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts](src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_shell_file.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_shell_file.test.ts).
- **A pre-push test-failure block truncated at 30 lines with no indication anything was cut**, unlike every other truncation path in the same compressor. Fixed to emit a `[+N more error lines omitted]` marker once the cap is hit, matching the existing marker style. Separately, the ESLint output compressor's file-header regex only recognized an uppercase Windows drive letter (`C:\...`), silently misattributing issue lines under a lowercase-drive-letter path as unattached output. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts) and [src/tool_filters/linters.ts](src/tool_filters/linters.ts).
- **`token-goat stats --home-dir <dir>` was ignored for the default human-readable output**, only the `--json` branch actually read from the specified home directory — the human-readable path always read the default global DB regardless of the flag. Fixed by threading `homeDir` through `renderStats()`. The `--by-project`/`--by-command`/`--top` flags on `stats` were also removed: they were parsed but never read anywhere, since the underlying `stats` table has no project column to break them down by. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts), and [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts).
- **`skill_cache.ts`'s `storeOutput` never pruned old cached skill output, contradicting its own documented bounded-LRU-retention guarantee.** Pruning only ran via the manual `prune-cache` CLI command. Fixed by calling `pruneSkillOutputs()` at the end of every `storeOutput`. Dead, unreachable-in-shipping-path glob/grep result-cache code in `bash_output_cache.ts` was also removed (an in-memory `Map` in a tool whose hooks run as a fresh process per invocation, so nothing written to it could ever be read back). See [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts) and [src/bash_output_cache.ts](src/bash_output_cache.ts).

## [2.6.8] - 2026-07-07

### Fixed

- **Overflow-guard hint for line-range reads suggested wrong syntax (`::` instead of `@`).** The hint returned by `getHintFor('lines')` was "Request a smaller line range, e.g. 'file.py::100-150'." but token-goat's actual line-range spec uses `@` as the separator (e.g. `file.py@100-150`). The `::` syntax routes through symbol parsing, producing "Symbol '1-5' not found" errors when a user followed the suggestion. Root cause: only this hint was wrong; every other documentation string and docstring in the codebase already used the correct `@` syntax. Fixed by updating the hint text to use the correct separator. See [src/overflow_guard.ts](src/overflow_guard.ts); regression-tested in [tests/overflow_guard.test.ts](tests/overflow_guard.test.ts).
- **`skeleton`/`outline` --min-lines with a non-numeric value silently returned zero symbols instead of erroring.** The --min-lines flag was wired via `Number.parseInt` with no validation, unlike --limit which uses `requireNonNegativeInt`. A non-numeric value like `--min-lines abc` yields NaN, and the filter `>= NaN` is always false, so every symbol was filtered out silently. Result: `# Skeleton: file (0 symbols, 0 lines)` with exit 0 instead of an error message. Fixed by validating with `requireNonNegativeInt` like other numeric flags. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts](tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts).
- **`parseDiffHunks` misattributed a deleted file's hunk to the previous file.** The function only updated `currentFile` on lines matching `/^\+\+\+ b\/(.+)$/`, but a deleted file in a diff emits `--- a/z.ts` followed by `+++ /dev/null` (with no `+++ b/...` line). This left `currentFile` pointing at the previously-seen modified file, causing the deletion's hunk header `@@ -1,10 +0,0 @@` to be parsed and attached to the wrong file. In `runChanged symbolMode`, this meant symbols at line 1 of a file alphabetically preceding a deleted file were falsely reported as changed. The function now resets `currentFile` to null when it encounters `+++ /dev/null`, ensuring deleted files are correctly excluded from the result. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`extractMarkdownHeadings` advertised sections inside fenced code blocks as real headings.** The function iterated raw lines and matched any line with `/^(#+)\s+/`, completely bypassing the fenced-code-block tracking that its sibling extractors (`extractMarkdownSymbols` and `findMarkdownHeaders`) implement via `eachUnfencedLine`. Concrete failure: a markdown file with a code fence containing comment lines like `# Install` or `# TODO` (very common in bash/python/toml samples) would be advertised as sections in pre-read hints via `hooks_read`, but when the user ran the suggested `token-goat section "file::# Install"` command, the section reader (which correctly skips fenced content) would report "not found". The same broken boundaries also fed `buildEmbeddingBoundaries` in the indexing pipeline, placing semantic-chunk cut points inside code fences. Fixed by switching to `eachUnfencedLine` to skip fence content like the other two extractors.
  See [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts); regression-tested in [tests/fenced_heading.test.ts](tests/fenced_heading.test.ts).
- **The Codex CLI and pi bridges had the same bare-PATH single-point-of-failure the Copilot CLI bridge was fixed for.** Codex's outer hook command still invoked a bare `node` (never hardened to `process.execPath` in the first place), and its shim's inner `token-goat hook <event>` call shelled out to a bare `token-goat` on PATH -- both now resolved via `process.execPath` plus a token-goat entry path baked into the generated hook command at install time, mirroring the Copilot fix. pi has no per-invocation command line to bake a path into (its extension is loaded once as a module, not spawned with fresh argv per event), so `installPi` now writes a small `token-goat-entry.json` sidecar next to the extension file, and the extension reads it at runtime (`resolveEntryPath()`) to invoke the baked entry directly instead of depending on PATH; `uninstallPi` removes the sidecar too. Both fall back to the old PATH-based lookup when no baked value is available (an older cached install).
  See [src/bridges/codex.ts](src/bridges/codex.ts), [src/bridges/codex_install.ts](src/bridges/codex_install.ts), [src/bridges/pi.ts](src/bridges/pi.ts), and [src/bridges/pi_install.ts](src/bridges/pi_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_codex.test.ts](tests/install_codex.test.ts), [tests/install_pi.test.ts](tests/install_pi.test.ts), and [tests/bridges/shims.test.ts](tests/bridges/shims.test.ts).
- **Every Windows Copilot CLI hook invocation failed with a PowerShell `ParserError`, denying every tool call ("(hook errored)"), even after v2.6.7's PATH-hardening fix.** Per GitHub's hooks reference, a hook entry's cross-platform `command` field is only a fallback -- it's copied verbatim into `bash` and `powershell` when those are absent, and on Windows Copilot CLI feeds the `powershell` string directly to PowerShell as a script, not to cmd.exe. `hookCommandFor()`'s output (`"C:\...\node.exe" "...\shim.js" preToolUse ...`) is valid cmd.exe command-line syntax but not valid PowerShell: two adjacent quoted string literals with no call operator are a parse error there ("Unexpected token '"...\token-goat-shim.js"' in expression or statement"), confirmed via Copilot CLI's own logged `ParserError`. This is a distinct bug from the PATH-resolution class already fixed in v2.6.6/v2.6.7 -- the absolute paths were correct, the syntax around them wasn't. The generated hook config now sets explicit `bash` and `powershell` fields: `bash` gets the same command text (POSIX shells don't need a call operator for a quoted path), and `powershell` is prefixed with `&`, PowerShell's call operator, required to invoke a quoted path as a command rather than evaluate it as a string expression. `command` is kept, unchanged, as a fallback for older Copilot CLI builds. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).

## [2.6.7] - 2026-07-07

### Fixed

- **`token-goat stats` showed events as happening "tomorrow" once UTC crossed midnight, ahead of the local calendar day.** `summarize()`'s day-bucket key and the rich stats renderer's header date were both derived via `toISOString()`, which always renders in UTC -- so any event recorded in the evening in a negative-UTC-offset zone (where UTC has already rolled to the next day) got bucketed and displayed under tomorrow's date. Both now derive the calendar day from local `Date` getters via a shared `toLocalDateKey` helper; `skill-history`'s timestamp column got the same local-time treatment via a new `formatLocalTimestamp` helper. See [src/stats.ts](src/stats.ts), [src/render/stats_renderer.ts](src/render/stats_renderer.ts), and [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/stats.test.ts](tests/stats.test.ts) against a fixed UTC-5 timezone so the day-boundary crossing is deterministic regardless of the host machine's real timezone.
- **The Copilot CLI hook shim's *inner* call still depended on PATH resolution, unlike its already-hardened outer command.** The outer hook command invokes the shim via a baked `process.execPath`, but the shim's own inner `token-goat hook <event>` call shelled out to a bare `token-goat` (`shell: true`), which depends on the npm global bin being on whatever PATH Copilot spawns the hook subprocess with -- and Copilot's `preToolUse` fails *closed* on a non-zero exit or crash, denying every tool call for the rest of the session with no mid-session recovery (Copilot caches hook configs at startup, so renaming/reinstalling the config has no effect until a full restart). `token-goat install --copilot` now bakes the running token-goat entry's absolute path into the generated hook command as a third argument, and the shim invokes it directly via `process.execPath` for the inner call too, falling back to the old PATH-based lookup only when that argument is absent (an older cached config). Every generated hook entry also now sets an explicit `timeoutSec: 60`, doubling Copilot's own 30s default as headroom for a cold first invocation (bundle load + DB open) on the four events that lack `preToolUse`'s documented fail-*open*-on-timeout carve-out -- per GitHub's hooks reference, a `preToolUse` timeout itself already fails open, so this is not what causes the deny-all class, just cheap insurance for the other events. `token-goat doctor` gained a `checkCopilotCli` check that runs the exact installed `preToolUse` command end-to-end with a synthetic payload (through a shell, the same path Copilot uses) and separately verifies the baked node binary still exists on disk, since an nvm/fnm/volta node upgrade can silently make it stale. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts), [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts), [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts), and [README.md](README.md) (documents the rename-and-restart recovery path); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts) and [tests/cli_doctor.test.ts](tests/cli_doctor.test.ts).


## [2.6.6] - 2026-07-07

### Fixed

- **The GitHub Copilot CLI hook shim denied every single tool call.** The installed hook command invoked a bare `node` on PATH, which real Copilot CLI hook execution environments don't always resolve -- and Copilot CLI fails *closed* on any hook launch/exit failure, so a PATH miss silently denied 100% of tool calls with "(hook errored)". The generated command now embeds the absolute Node binary path (`process.execPath`, captured at install time) instead of relying on PATH resolution, and the shim's `main()` is now wrapped in a hard top-level safety net so it can never exit non-zero for any reason. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts) and [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **The Copilot CLI bridge mapped the wrong tool names.** Real Copilot CLI tool names (`view`, `create`, `edit`, `bash`, `powershell`, `grep`, `glob`, `web_fetch`) never matched the shim's docs-guessed mapping (`shell`/`read`/`write`/`url`) -- `write` in particular was never a real tool name at all, only a permission-pattern keyword -- so token-goat's deny/dedup logic silently never engaged for real tool calls. The mapping is now corrected to the real tool names, confirmed via `@github/copilot-sdk`'s published type definitions and real payload examples. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **`preCompact`/`agentStop`/`subagentStop` sent Copilot CLI a response shape it silently discards.** `preCompact` is notification-only (no response is ever processed) and `agentStop`/`subagentStop` only accept `{decision, reason}`, never `additionalContext` -- but the shim was sending `additionalContext` for all three, so Copilot ignored it every time with no error surfaced. Responses are now shaped per event to match Copilot's real schema. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **`userPromptSubmitted` was a real Copilot CLI hook event with zero handling.** Now registered and translated like the other five events (notification-only, matching its documented schema). See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts) and [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **`--copilot --local` (project-scope hook install) was dead code.** `installCopilotCli`/`uninstallCopilotCli` already implemented project-scope (`.github/hooks/`) vs. user-scope (`~/.copilot/hooks/`) installs, but `src/cli.ts` never passed the `--local` flag through, so project-scope install was unreachable from the CLI. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **Copilot CLI's `toolArgs` can arrive as a JSON-encoded string rather than a parsed object** (confirmed via an open upstream issue), which would silently break every downstream tool-input lookup with no error surfaced. The shim now parses a string `toolArgs` defensively, falling back to `{}` on any parse failure. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **Reinstalling the Copilot CLI hook config silently destroyed any hand-edited fields** (e.g. a user-adjusted `timeoutSec`), since the installer always regenerates the file from scratch with no backup. It now backs up the existing config before overwriting it, mirroring the Codex installer's convention. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).
- **The PHP and C# adapters counted braces inside a trailing `//`/`#` line comment as real code**, desyncing scope tracking for every declaration after a line like `const X = 1; // resets the } counter`. Both adapters now strip trailing line comments before brace-counting, matching the Kotlin adapter's existing correct handling.
