See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts), [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts), and [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`VaultFilter` never actually collapsed real `vault list` output.** Three compounding bugs -- a list-item regex requiring indentation real vault output never has, a table-divider regex that never matched vault's real single-dash divider, and a command-name check that didn't reduce a full path or `.exe` suffix to a bare command name -- meant the `>10`-item truncation never fired on real output. All three are fixed together. See [src/tool_filters/cloud.ts](src/tool_filters/cloud.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_cloud.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_cloud.test.ts).
- **`PsqlFilter`'s migration summary silently dropped counts for functions, views, types, sequences, triggers, and alterations**, since only `CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE INDEX` lines were tallied even though the suppression regex also stripped the others -- e.g. a migration creating 3 tables and a function collapsed to "Created 3 tables" with no mention of the function. All suppressed DDL categories are now counted. See [src/tool_filters/misc.ts](src/tool_filters/misc.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts).
- **`JsonArrayFilter` deduplicated objects by field-name shape instead of value**, collapsing distinct same-shaped records (the common case for a homogeneous JSON array, e.g. `[{"id":1,...},{"id":2,...}]`) down to just the first -- real data loss on the filter's primary use case. Dedup is now based on actual value content. See [src/tool_filters/misc.ts](src/tool_filters/misc.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts).
- **`inferSessionGoal`'s token-budget truncation was unreachable dead code.** The guard required more than one goal-string part to ever exist, but the assembly logic can only ever produce zero or one part, so a long directory/symbol name could exceed the intended token budget with no truncation applied. See [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/compact.test.ts](tests/compact.test.ts).
- **An explicitly-set `auto_trigger_multiplier` could be silently overridden by harness-default logic.** `getEffectiveAutoTriggerWindow` never told `getAutoTriggerMultiplier` whether the configured value was user-set or a fallback, so a user explicitly setting a value matching *some other harness's* default (e.g. `2.0` on `gemini`, whose own default is `3.0`) had that explicit value discarded. The real "was this explicitly set" signal is now threaded through from the raw config file. See [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/compact.test.ts](tests/compact.test.ts).
- **A `<#` block-comment opener appearing after real code on the same line silently discarded that code and desynced the PowerShell adapter's brace counter**, dropping every subsequent top-level symbol in the file (e.g. `function Foo { <# doc` with no same-line `#>`). The opener's own line is now correctly split into leading code plus the comment, instead of the whole line being swallowed. See [src/languages/powershell_idx.ts](src/languages/powershell_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **`token-goat read`/`brief` could never resolve a symbol whose indexed name literally contains a dot** (TOML sections like `tool.poetry`, CSS selectors like `.btn`), since `resolveSymbolSpec` always split the requested name on `.` and looked up only the trailing segment, treating every dot as a Class.method separator. An exact match on the full name is now tried first. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **The SQL/Protobuf block-comment stripper could close a comment against its own opening asterisk.** `stripCstyleComments` searched for the closing `*/` starting at the same index as the `/*` opener it had just found, so a comment like `/*/ ... */` closed after only 3 characters instead of at the real closing delimiter, leaking the "commented-out" text back in as live code. The close search now correctly starts 2 characters past the opener. See [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Copilot CLI recorded zero read/edit activity in any session.** The `view`/`edit`/`create` tool argument objects carry the file path under the key `path`, but every token-goat handler these three tools reach (`getFilePath` in [src/hooks_common.ts](src/hooks_common.ts)) only ever looks for `file_path` -- so the path was always invisible, `recordFileRead`/`recordFileEdit` never ran, and the session's `files` array stayed empty no matter how much work happened. The shim now adds a `file_path` key alongside the original `path` for these three tools. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).

## [2.6.5] - 2026-07-07


### Added

- **An MCP stdio server (`token-goat mcp-serve`)** exposing `read`, `symbol`, `section`, `outline`, `skeleton`, and `semantic` as tools, calling the same surgical-read logic the CLI commands use in-process (no subprocess spawn per call). The five `run*` handlers in `read_commands.ts` were refactored to return `{ text, code }` instead of printing directly, and `cmdSemantic` was extracted into a new `runSemantic` export, so both the CLI and the MCP server share one implementation instead of two. See [src/mcp_server.ts](src/mcp_server.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), and [README.md](README.md); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_server.test.ts](tests/mcp_server.test.ts) and [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **A Copilot CLI hook bridge (`token-goat install --copilot`).** Registers `~/.copilot/hooks/token-goat.json` (a `{ version, hooks }` config covering `preToolUse`, `postToolUse`, `preCompact`, `agentStop`, and `subagentStop`, per GitHub's [hooks reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference)) plus the shim script it points at, `~/.copilot/hooks/token-goat-shim.js`. Unlike the Codex bridge, Copilot's event names and response schema (`permissionDecision`/`modifiedArgs` for `preToolUse`, `modifiedResult`/`additionalContext` for `postToolUse`) are genuinely different from Claude Code's `hookSpecificOutput`-nested shape, so the shim translates rather than mostly passes through; it also sets `TOKEN_GOAT_HARNESS_OVERRIDE=copilot_cli` itself before invoking `token-goat hook`, since no documented ambient env var identifies a Copilot CLI subprocess the way Codex/opencode's session-id vars do. `--copilot --local` installs into the project-scoped `.github/hooks/` directory instead of the user-scoped one. See [src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli.ts), [src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts](src/bridges/copilot_cli_install.ts), and [README.md](README.md); regression-tested in [tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts](tests/install_copilot_cli.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **`Grep` calls were inflating the Read-only re-read deny counter.** `preReadHandler` recorded every tool call as a "read" of the file, including `Grep`, even though the deny check itself explicitly exempts `Grep` -- so a few `Grep` passes over a file followed by a genuine first `Read` could be wrongly denied as an "already read N times" repeat. Reads are now only recorded for actual `Read` calls. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **pytest failure detection missed `N errors` summaries.** The summary-capture and failure-detection checks only matched `passed`/`failed` substrings, so a run ending in `"3 errors in 0.42s"` (collection errors, fixture errors) was silently dropped instead of being flagged as a failure. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`git diff --stat` compression undercounted insert/delete totals on large diffs.** Counts were derived by counting literal `+`/`-` glyphs in the width-scaled bar graph rather than reading the real numeric total column, undercounting by up to ~20x once git scales the bar down to fit the terminal width. Counts are now reconstructed from the true numeric total scaled by the bar's `+`/`-` glyph ratio. See [src/tool_filters/git.ts](src/tool_filters/git.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_git.test.ts).
- **`symbols_read` and `created_ts` were dead fields.** `compact.ts` read both from session state to compute a caller-context bonus and a session-age budget multiplier, but neither was ever written anywhere, so the bonus was permanently zero and the multiplier was stuck at its "young session" tier forever. Both are now recorded -- `symbols_read` from surgical `read`/`section` commands carrying a `::symbol`/`::heading`/`@range` suffix, `created_ts` stamped once on a session's first save. See [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), and [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/session_store.test.ts](tests/session_store.test.ts) and [tests/compact.test.ts](tests/compact.test.ts).
- **The Kotlin adapter dropped every top-level declaration after a class whose body opened and closed on the same line** (e.g. `class Empty {}`). Brace depth was tracked as a batched net delta per line, so a same-line open+close never registered as "entered the body," leaving the class frame stuck open and swallowing everything parsed afterward. Depth is now tracked character-by-character so a transient same-line open is caught. See [src/languages/kotlin.ts](src/languages/kotlin.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).
- **Project-directory matching had no path-separator boundary check**, so `isProjectFrame` and `hot --project` treated a sibling directory sharing a prefix (e.g. `token-goat-fork` matching project dir `token-goat`) as inside the project. A match now requires either an exact match or a path separator immediately following the prefix. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).
- **Bash-output cache keys could be corrupted by a backslash-escaped quote near a pipe.** Quote-tracking in `stripOutputPipeline` toggled on every raw `"`/`'` with no escape awareness, so a command like `git log --grep="fix: replace \" | \" separator" | head -20` was misparsed, risking a cache-key collision. Quote state now tracks backslash parity so an escaped quote no longer toggles it. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **Markdown fence detection matched by marker character only, not run length**, so a nested 3-backtick example inside an outer 4-backtick fence closed the outer fence early, corrupting section/heading detection for the rest of the file. Fences now only close on a marker of the same character with a run length at least as long as the opener's, per CommonMark. See [src/markdown_lines.ts](src/markdown_lines.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser_markdown_fence.test.ts](tests/parser_markdown_fence.test.ts).
- **The "did normalization alone help?" check compared against the wrong baseline.** It reused the true pre-truncation byte size instead of the post-truncation, pre-normalization size, so whenever truncation alone already cleared the 40% threshold, normalization was wrongly credited for a reduction it didn't cause. See [src/tool_filters/base.ts](src/tool_filters/base.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters.test.ts](tests/tool_filters.test.ts).
- **Snapshot storage evicted an unrelated entry when just updating an existing key.** Eviction ran unconditionally on every `store()` call, even when the call only overwrote an existing key's content rather than adding a new one, wrongly discarding an unrelated snapshot at capacity. Eviction now only runs when the key is actually new. See [src/snapshots.ts](src/snapshots.ts); regression-tested in [tests/snapshots.test.ts](tests/snapshots.test.ts).
- **`parseLineRange` hijacked real filenames containing an `@<digits>` suffix**, e.g. a file literally named `notes@2024` was parsed as `{file: "notes", start: 2024}` instead of being read literally. It now checks whether the full original spec already resolves to a real file before treating `@` as a line-range marker. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **The PowerShell adapter counted braces inside `<# ... #>` block-comment prose.** An unbalanced `{` in comment-based help text (common in real `.ps1`/`.psm1` files) permanently desynced `braceDepth`, silently dropping every top-level function/class declared after it from the index. Comment-interior lines no longer count braces at all, and the line where a comment closes now processes only the code after `#>`. See [src/languages/powershell_idx.ts](src/languages/powershell_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

## [2.6.4] - 2026-07-06

### Added

- **`token-goat brief "file::symbol"`** bundles a symbol's body, resolved callers (grouped by enclosing function, not raw reference sites), and its containing doc section into one round-trip, replacing three separate `read`/`callers`/`section` calls for the common "understand this function" pattern. `--limit <n>` caps callers shown (default 20); the true caller count is always reported even when the display is truncated. Caller resolution and symbol-spec parsing were extracted out of `runCallers`/`runRead` into shared `resolveCallers`/`resolveSymbolSpec` helpers so `brief` reuses the real enclosing-function-aware logic rather than a second, weaker implementation. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), and [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts) and [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts).
- **`--stats` on `outline`/`skeleton`** adds a per-symbol reference count and doc-coverage flag, computed live (one batched query, not per-symbol) so it can never go stale relative to the index. See [src/index_reader.ts](src/index_reader.ts) and [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **WebFetch responses are now converted from HTML to readable text** before reaching the model instead of passing raw markup, and **`token-goat pdf-extract <file>`**/**`token-goat csv-query <file>`** pull plain text or projected/filtered rows straight from a PDF or CSV instead of a raw Read, with the same `--head`/`--tail`/`--grep`/`--section` slicing conventions as `bash-output`/`web-output`. **`token-goat screenshot <url> <destPath>`** captures a local headless-browser screenshot shrunk through the same image-shrink pipeline as any other image read. See [src/web_extract.ts](src/web_extract.ts), [src/pdf_extract.ts](src/pdf_extract.ts), [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts), [src/screenshot.ts](src/screenshot.ts), and [src/hooks_fetch.ts](src/hooks_fetch.ts) (hint routing); regression-tested across [tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts](tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts), [tests/pdf_extract.test.ts](tests/pdf_extract.test.ts), [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts), and [tests/screenshot.test.ts](tests/screenshot.test.ts).
- **A new `tool_filters` collapse for PowerShell's `CommandNotFoundException`.** Running a PowerShell command from the Bash tool where bash pre-expands an unescaped `$_` before PowerShell ever sees it produces a multi-KB `ErrorRecord` stack trace with a formulaic, low-information shape; it's now collapsed to a one-line diagnosis naming the likely cause (bash pre-expansion of `$_`) and the fix (backtick-escape or single-quote the `-Command` string). See [src/tool_filters/languages.ts](src/tool_filters/languages.ts); regression-tested in [tests/tool_filters_languages.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_languages.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **`withFileLock` could steal a lock from a still-legitimately-running holder.** Staleness was judged purely from the lock file's mtime, so a holder blocked past `LOCK_STALE_MS` (5s) by slow synchronous I/O or a GC pause -- with no way for its own thread to refresh the mtime, since a same-process timer can't fire while that thread is pinned in a non-yielding call -- would have its lock stolen by a second caller, and both would then believe they held exclusive access. A detached child process now heartbeats the lock file's mtime independently of the holder's own event loop, so a live holder can never be judged stale; if the holder crashes, the heartbeat dies with it (self-exits promptly cross-platform, not just via Windows Job Object semantics) and the lock is still reclaimed once real staleness elapses. See [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested in [tests/util.test.ts](tests/util.test.ts) against a real spawned child process holding the lock through a synchronous busy-spin past `staleMs`.
- **`pre_compact`'s manifest could be silently suppressed by a future change to an unrelated handler.** Two handlers register for `pre_compact`: a side-effect-only snapshot writer and the handler that produces the real compaction manifest. `runHook` short-circuits on the first non-pass result, so the manifest only ever ran because of today's import order and the snapshot writer happening to always pass -- nothing structurally prevented a later change to the snapshot writer from returning non-pass and swallowing the manifest with no error. `registerHook` now takes an `advisory` option: a non-pass result from an advisory handler is remembered as a fallback but never short-circuits the loop, so every later handler for the event still always runs regardless of import order. See [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts) and [src/hooks_index.ts](src/hooks_index.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hook_registry.test.ts](tests/hook_registry.test.ts).
- **`runBrief`'s caller count hid its own truncation.** The query itself was capped at the same limit used for display, so the "N more elided" note could never fire even when far more callers actually existed. The query now uses `resolveCallers`'s full internal cap independent of the display limit, and the true total caller count is reported alongside whatever's shown. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts) and [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`runFind` silently dropped matches beyond its internal scan limit**, presenting a partial result as complete with no indication anything was cut. A `truncated` flag is now set and surfaced (plain-text warning, `truncated` field under `--json`) whenever the scan limit is hit. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).
- **`config-get`'s section-header detection rejected a header with a trailing inline comment** (e.g. `[tool.ruff] # comment`), silently missing keys under it. The comment is now stripped before the header check. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/test_configget_bug.test.ts](tests/test_configget_bug.test.ts).
- **`csv-query`'s table formatter had no RFC 4180 quoting**, so a cell containing a comma, quote, or newline silently misaligned every column after it. Cells are now quoted and embedded quotes doubled per spec. See [src/csv_query.ts](src/csv_query.ts); regression-tested in [tests/csv_query.test.ts](tests/csv_query.test.ts).
- **`config`'s boolean coercion silently defaulted an unrecognized value to `false`** instead of rejecting it, so a typo'd config value (e.g. `enabled = "yse"`) would silently behave as disabled. It now throws, naming the invalid value. See [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).
- **The dirty-reindex queue had no retry cap**, so a file stuck permanently unreadable (a locked, deleted-but-still-open, or directory-shaped path) got requeued forever, every drain cycle, indefinitely. Retries now cap at 5 attempts per path, logging once and giving up rather than looping forever; the counter clears on a successful read. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts) against a real `EISDIR` condition, not a mocked failure.
- **`chunkFile`'s gap-fold-forward path mislabeled a folded chunk's kind**, keeping the absorbed boundary's original `kind` instead of relabeling it to the established generic/mixed `'window'` kind once non-boundary content was folded in. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/embeddings.test.ts](tests/embeddings.test.ts).
- **The MCP dedup cache ignored state-changing input flags.** `isMcpReadOnly` classified any call as safely cacheable purely by tool-name verb, with no awareness of the call's actual input. Per Anthropic's own Claude-in-Chrome documentation (v2.1.199+), `createIfEmpty` (`tabs_context_mcp`), `clear` (console/network readers), and `save_to_disk` (screenshots) each turn an otherwise read-only call into a state-changing one -- so a repeated `read_console_messages({clear: true})` call was getting silently served the *first* call's pre-clear cached output instead of re-executing, which is wrong rather than merely stale, since clearing isn't idempotent. `isMcpReadOnly` now also inspects the input and treats any of these three flags as disqualifying, regardless of the tool-name check. See [src/mcp_cache.ts](src/mcp_cache.ts) and [src/hooks_mcp.ts](src/hooks_mcp.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_cache.test.ts](tests/mcp_cache.test.ts) and [tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts](tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts).

### Removed

- **The `session_start` hook event is retired.** `sessionStartHandler` had been a complete no-op since the TypeScript port (every branch just returned `passOutput()`), yet Gemini's `SessionStart`, and pi's and OpenClaw's own `session_start` lifecycle subscriptions, still forwarded to it on every session start -- a `token-goat hook` subprocess spawned for zero effect. `'session_start'` is removed from `HOOK_EVENTS` (`src/types.ts`), `sessionStartHandler` and its registration are deleted (`src/hooks_session.ts`), and its `CLAUDE_CODE_EVENT_NAMES` entry is removed (`src/hook_registry.ts`). Gemini's installer no longer writes a `SessionStart` entry at all (`src/bridges/gemini_install.ts`), and the dead forwarding calls are removed from the pi and OpenClaw bridge templates (`src/bridges/pi.ts`, `src/bridges/openclaw.ts`) while keeping their subscriptions to the *host's* own `session_start` lifecycle event, which those bridges still need to refresh `sessionId`/`cwd` for every other bridged call. `runHook` already passes through `{}` for any unregistered event name, so a not-yet-reinstalled Gemini/pi/OpenClaw integration that still sends `session_start` keeps behaving exactly as before (a no-op), with no crash. See [src/hooks_session.ts](src/hooks_session.ts), [src/types.ts](src/types.ts), [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts), [src/bridges/gemini_install.ts](src/bridges/gemini_install.ts), [src/bridges/pi.ts](src/bridges/pi.ts), and [src/bridges/openclaw.ts](src/bridges/openclaw.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install_gemini.test.ts](tests/install_gemini.test.ts), [tests/install_pi.test.ts](tests/install_pi.test.ts), [tests/install_openclaw.test.ts](tests/install_openclaw.test.ts), and [tests/bridges/shims.test.ts](tests/bridges/shims.test.ts).

## [2.6.3] - 2026-07-05

### Added

- **`token-goat grep` now accepts multiple paths and a `-C, --context <n>` flag.** `grep <pattern> [paths...]` takes zero or more paths (variadic, matching the existing `pack`/`tokens`/`budget` convention): zero still walks cwd, one behaves exactly as before, and two-plus are searched in argument order with all hits merged into one list before the existing `--max-lines` cap runs once across the combined set, never truncated per file. `-C, --context <n>` captures `n` lines before and after each match (clamped to the file's real range); JSON output includes a structured `context` array per hit, plain text renders it with grep's own `:`/`-` convention, and the field is entirely absent — output byte-identical to before — when `-C` is omitted. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts) and [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **`token-goat config-get` resolves keys from YAML frontmatter in Markdown files.** A `.md` file's leading `---`-fenced frontmatter block (Jekyll/Hugo/SKILL.md-style `key: value` lines) previously fell into the TOML/INI fallback, which expects `key = value` and never matched — locating a version marker in a SKILL.md required a manual grep plus an offset/limit read instead. `runConfigGet` now checks for a fence pair first, before extension dispatch, and runs the existing YAML lookup against just the fenced slice; a `.md` file with no frontmatter, or an unclosed fence, falls through unchanged to the normal TOML/INI lookup. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **`token-goat read`, `skeleton`, and `outline` gained a `--force-refresh` flag.** Files touched by git operations, external tools, or direct filesystem writes bypass the normal post-edit indexing hook and were served stale symbols until the background worker's next drain cycle. `--force-refresh` synchronously re-parses the target file from disk and updates the index before querying, guaranteeing the result reflects current file content regardless of index staleness. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **Embedding chunk boundaries now snap to symbols and headings instead of blind byte windows.** A fixed-byte window could land mid-function, diluting or splitting a symbol's embedding across two chunks and degrading `semantic` search relevance. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts).

- **Every remaining harness now has real `install`/`uninstall` wiring: `--codex`, `--pi` (plus `--pi --local` for a project-only install), `--gemini`, `--opencode`, `--hermes`, and `--openclaw`.** Most of these were previously documented in the README with no corresponding `cli.ts` command at all, or shipped a bridge file that was never referenced by `install`. Highlights: the pi bridge (`bridges/pi.ts`) and opencode bridge (`bridges/opencode.ts`) are real, hook-tested TypeScript templates written against each harness's actual event vocabulary; `--hermes` is verification-only, since Hermes delegates to Claude Code via `claude -p` and inherits `~/.claude/settings.json` directly; `--openclaw` (`src/bridges/openclaw.ts`, `openclaw_install.ts`) is the first fully-implemented OpenClaw plugin writer, built against OpenClaw's documented `before_tool_call`/`after_tool_call` shape and `definePluginEntry` registration (not yet dogfooded against a live gateway). A single canonical `detectHarness()` in `bridges/registry.ts` replaces two previously conflicting implementations that disagreed on environment-variable names and which harnesses they recognized. See [src/bridges/registry.ts](src/bridges/registry.ts), [src/bridges/pi.ts](src/bridges/pi.ts), [src/bridges/opencode.ts](src/bridges/opencode.ts), [src/bridges/openclaw.ts](src/bridges/openclaw.ts), and [src/install.ts](src/install.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding `tests/bridges_*.test.ts` and `tests/install*.test.ts` files.

- **Base `install` now writes the `CLAUDE.md` block and the token-goat skill, as the README always documented.** Both were real in the Python-era install but silently dropped during the TypeScript port; base install had been leaving every new user without the skill or the CLAUDE.md nudge the rest of the docs assume is present. See [src/install.ts](src/install.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install.test.ts](tests/install.test.ts) — fixing this also closed a test-isolation gap where two e2e cases would otherwise have written into a real `~/.claude`.

### Fixed

- **Three harness bridges spoke hook protocols that didn't exist, so their integrations were complete no-ops once installed.** pi's shipped bridge called `token-goat hook <event>` with fabricated per-tool event names (`"pre-read"`, `"post-bash"`, etc.); `relay()` silently returns `"{}"` for anything it doesn't recognize, so bash compression, re-read denial, image shrinking, post-edit indexing, and the compaction manifest all silently did nothing after a `--pi` install. openclaw's bridge subscribed to an invented `session_end` hook (not a real `HOOK_EVENTS` member) and both opencode and openclaw kept a dead `Glob` entry in `PRE_HOOK_TOOLS` with no handler behind it. Gemini's input-key remap table was keyed backwards, so it never fired, and separately never remapped `list_directory`'s real `dir_path` argument to `file_path` at all — every `list_directory` call left `tool_input` untouched, so node_modules/large-file denies, hints, and dedup tracking silently never applied to that tool. All three bridges now use each harness's verified real event names and argument shapes. See [src/bridges/pi.ts](src/bridges/pi.ts), [src/bridges/openclaw.ts](src/bridges/openclaw.ts), [src/bridges/opencode.ts](src/bridges/opencode.ts), and [src/hooks_cli.ts](src/hooks_cli.ts); regression-tested in the corresponding `tests/bridges_*.test.ts` and [tests/hooks_cli.test.ts](tests/hooks_cli.test.ts).

- **`pi` never resolved through `detectHarness()`.** `'pi'` was missing from `HarnessName`/`KNOWN_HARNESS_NAMES` entirely, so every pi session misdetected as `'generic'` and lost harness-specific behavior (auto-compact multiplier, per-harness README claims) regardless of the bridge fixes above. See [src/bridges/registry.ts](src/bridges/registry.ts).

- **Per-harness auto-compact multipliers were fully implemented and configured but never actually consulted.** `getContextPressure`'s window computation now calls `getAutoTriggerMultiplier`, so each harness's documented multiplier changes its effective auto-compact trigger point instead of every harness being treated identically. Verified end-to-end against the built binary at three multiplier values. See [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts).

- **Base install/uninstall and Codex/Gemini's marker-based safety checks had several gaps.** `installHooks`/`uninstallHooks` never backed up `settings.json` before writing to it (every other bridge writer did); an existing-but-unparseable `settings.json` was silently clobbered instead of aborting; `isCodexTokenGoatCommand`/`isGeminiTokenGoatCommand` used a plain substring match, so an unrelated user hook whose command happened to contain the marker text could be wrongly stripped on uninstall; `installHooks`/`isInstalled` treated a leftover legacy hook entry as "already installed," silently skipping the real hook wiring on upgrade; and Codex's own shim used a snake_case `hookEventName` fallback instead of matching Claude Code's PascalCase convention. See [src/install.ts](src/install.ts) and [src/bridges/codex.ts](src/bridges/codex.ts); regression-tested in [tests/install.test.ts](tests/install.test.ts).

- **A dozen-plus case-folding gaps let differently-cased but identical paths silently miss each other on Windows and macOS.** The rest of the codebase already follows an established `foldPath`/`isCaseInsensitiveFs` pattern (`parser.ts`, `index_prune.ts`, `sql_path.ts`, `walk_index.ts`, `worker.ts`); this batch closed the remaining stragglers one at a time as each was found: the three read-dedup caches and manifest merge in `session.ts`/`compact.ts`, `session_store.ts`'s concurrent-state merge, `paths.ts`'s duplicated drive-letter lowercasing and `isNodeModulesPath` (previously gated on `isWindows()` alone, missing macOS), `project.ts`'s temp-boundary guard and `projectHash`, `session.ts`'s `_fileLineRanges` keys, `hooks_read.ts`'s cross-session manifest scan and reread-count lookups, `snapshots.ts`'s `pathKey()` hash input, UNC host/share segments in `paths.ts`, import-to-file resolution in `graph_commands.ts`'s `arch` command, `memory_prune.ts`'s duplicate-target detection, `openclaw_install.ts`'s plugin-path membership checks, and `text_commands.ts`'s `isProjectFrame` (regressed by routing through a drive-letter-only `canonicalize()`). See [src/paths.ts](src/paths.ts), [src/project.ts](src/project.ts), [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts), [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts), [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts), [src/snapshots.ts](src/snapshots.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), [src/memory_prune.ts](src/memory_prune.ts), [src/bridges/openclaw_install.ts](src/bridges/openclaw_install.ts), and [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files for each.

- **Several worker/indexing paths silently produced wrong results instead of failing loudly.** Two near-simultaneous `worker start` calls could both pass the startup pre-check and spawn duplicate daemons (a TOCTOU race, now closed, with the dead `worker_daemon.ts` removed); `indexFileSync` counted any read failure — not just a missing file — as successfully indexed, so a transient AV/editor lock silently stored a stale SHA with no error; `cmdIndex`'s walk had no per-file try/catch, so one locked or unreadable file aborted indexing the entire project; the dirty-reindex queue permanently dropped an entry for a file confirmed to exist but temporarily unreadable, instead of requeuing it; `cleanup_stale` was exported but never called from the periodic sweep loop, so stale session-snapshot directories accumulated forever; `indexFileSync` hashed the UTF-8-decoded string rather than the raw bytes, so any non-UTF-8 file could never SHA-match and was fully reparsed on every drain cycle; and `chunkFile` could silently drop every embedding chunk from a symbol-dense file (barrel/index re-exports, enum members), removing it entirely from semantic search with no warning. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), and [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts), [tests/worker_daemon_e2e.test.ts](tests/worker_daemon_e2e.test.ts), and [tests/embeddings.test.ts](tests/embeddings.test.ts).

- **Several language adapters silently mis-parsed real source.** `.tsx` files were parsed with the plain TypeScript grammar instead of the tsx grammar, corrupting JSX syntax into ERROR nodes; a brace character inside a string literal permanently desynced brace-depth tracking in the C#, PHP, Kotlin, and PowerShell adapters; nested classes in Kotlin and C# either went unrecognized or were measured against the wrong depth (both now track scope with a stack); a decorated Python `def`/`class`'s range excluded its decorator lines; proto (nested messages), HTML/Liquid (multi-line headings), and INI (quoted subsection headers) each silently dropped a class of real symbols; and the TS/JS import regex matched per line instead of against the whole file text, missing any Prettier-style multi-line import statement. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts) and the individual adapters under `src/languages/`; regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts) and the corresponding per-language test files.

- **A first-match-wins dispatch bug let a generic filter silently shadow several dedicated `tool_filters` compressors**, so the specialized parser never actually ran except in its own unit tests: Gradle/Maven/Bazel output fell through to generic Make parsing, `eza --tree` fell through to a generic tree filter, and npm/pnpm/yarn's `list` subcommand was caught by a broader package-manager filter before the dedicated 30-line-cap `DepListFilter` ever saw it. See [src/tool_filters/build.ts](src/tool_filters/build.ts), [src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts](src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts), and [src/tool_filters/package_managers.ts](src/tool_filters/package_managers.ts); regression-tested in the corresponding `tests/tool_filters_*.test.ts` files.

- **Several `tool_filters` compressors corrupted or discarded the exact output they were supposed to preserve.** `capBytes`/`capLongLines` could split a UTF-8 multi-byte character or a UTF-16 surrogate pair at the truncation boundary, corrupting a CJK character or emoji; `GcloudFilter` collapsed an entire single `describe` document — the actual answer the command was run for — to a one-line placeholder; the MySQL DDL-skip state machine had the blank-line anchor on the wrong side, so every "collapsed" `CREATE TABLE` statement actually survived unfiltered while the summary falsely claimed compression happened; `ESLintFilter` misread each violation line as an empty file header under compact/unix format and dropped every violation; the go-test race filter didn't recognize primary race-condition stack headers (`Write at`/`Read at`), leaving the most important part of every `-race` report uncollapsed; git's rename-dir rollup mis-parsed the brace-compressed form (`src/{old => new}/file.ts`) and `--oneline --stat`/`-p` handling tore commit bodies mid-way; Docker's legacy (non-BuildKit) intermediate-layer hashes weren't recognized, leaving one noise line per build step; `gh run log` lines retained a stray tab field that broke every downstream regex; `tox -e ...` and `uv tool run <bin>` were misclassified by a shared two-token-prefix check and ran fully unfiltered; `PipFilter` had no truncation at all; PhpStan's path split truncated any path containing a space, Pylint/Oxlint/Ktlint hardcoded a literal "+?" placeholder instead of a real elided count, and ruff's newer full-format output wasn't recognized; Python traceback frames were sliced by raw line instead of grouped header-plus-context, producing torn fragments on truncation; and pytest's filter could orphan a warning header (flushed before its message was known to survive dedup) or get stuck in "slow section" state when a coverage table interjected directly after it. See the individual filters under `src/tool_filters/`; regression-tested across the corresponding `tests/tool_filters_*.test.ts` files.

- **`bash-output`/`web-output --grep` with no `--head`/`--tail` bypassed truncation entirely**, printing unbounded output for the single most common recall pattern. Regression-tested against 200- and 250-line scratch files, confirmed failing before the fix via `git stash`. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **A batch of config knobs were fully implemented and validated but never actually wired to a consumer.** `bash_compress`/`webfetch` cache-size overrides, `overflow_guard` in the symbol/line-range/section emit paths (dropped by the TypeScript port), and `repomap.exclude_tests`/`worker.blocked_roots` all silently had no effect regardless of what was configured. Separately, `large_file_symbol_only_kb` is now clamped to never exceed `large_file_skip_kb`, and `bash_compress.cache_max_bytes_per_output` is clamped to the total cache budget and excludes a freshly-written blob from its own eviction pass. A dead `PREFER_AVIF` env override (no corresponding feature ever existed) was removed, along with a dead 500-line regex-based skeleton engine (`compressToSkeleton`/`compressPython`/`compressBraceLang`, deleted entirely — zero callers outside its own test file since the Python-era wiring was dropped during the TS port) in favor of the real tree-sitter `skeleton`/`outline` commands, and 17 dead hint-builder exports with no real caller. See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/disk_cache.ts](src/disk_cache.ts), [src/bash_runner.ts](src/bash_runner.ts), [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts), [src/repomap.ts](src/repomap.ts), and [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files.

- **A README claim about the total filter-rule count had no automated check behind it.** `TOTAL_FILTER_COUNT` was computed in `filter_counts.ts` but never consulted, so the README's number was an unverified, manually-bumped figure. A new guard test now fails if the README's count drifts from the real total. See [tests/guards/filter_count_readme_sync.test.ts](tests/guards/filter_count_readme_sync.test.ts).

- **Several rendering paths dropped or miscounted real data.** `stripAnsi` leaked unterminated OSC sequences and bare Fe escapes into rendered output; colored CI/pytest output broke every failure-detection anchor regex in `failures.ts`, silently reporting zero failures when real ones existed; `stats_renderer.ts` dropped an "Other"-bucketed kind entirely from one view while `insights` could still name it, and computed its by-project percentages from a filtered top-N slice instead of true totals, inflating the numbers; and `overflow_guard.ts` charged raw line length instead of ANSI-stripped length, letting ANSI-heavy content silently exceed its nominal budget. See [src/render/ansi.ts](src/render/ansi.ts), [src/failures.ts](src/failures.ts), [src/render/stats_renderer.ts](src/render/stats_renderer.ts), and [src/overflow_guard.ts](src/overflow_guard.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files.

- **`fetch-image` had no SSRF protection at all**, and the already-wired WebFetch SSRF check had two latent bugs of its own: a literal-IP bypass, and a crash on every real non-literal-IP fetch from a Happy-Eyeballs callback shape mismatch in `ssrfPinnedLookup`. All three are fixed. See [src/webfetch.ts](src/webfetch.ts) and [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in the corresponding test files.

- **`doctor`'s disk-space check silently reported "could not determine" on stock Windows** (it shelled out to `df`, which isn't present) instead of actually reading available space; a 0-byte or truncated `global.db` was reported as healthy instead of flagged; and animated GIF/WEBP images were silently collapsed to a single frame by image-shrink, a content-destroying change left undisclosed in the savings summary. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and [src/image_shrink.ts](src/image_shrink.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files.

- **A collection of smaller CLI/util correctness bugs.** `replace --old-b64`/`--new-b64` silently rewrote non-UTF-8 bytes to U+FFFD instead of doing a byte-exact replacement, defeating the flag's whole purpose; `section_reader.ts` didn't treat a lone CR as a blank line when trimming, leaving a trailing blank line on CRLF files; spawned git calls lacked `-c core.quotepath=false` and `runBlame`'s exit-code handling was wrong; npm v1 lockfiles (nested `dependencies` tree, no `packages` map) reported "Total: 0 packages"; `cmdWriteFile` re-inlined its own path/size validation instead of reusing the shared helpers, producing inconsistent error messages; `spawnSync` calls were missing `maxBuffer`, silently truncating large git output (ENOBUFS); WSL/MSYS-style frame paths weren't recognized as project files by `trace`; `requireInt` silently truncated numeric-prefixed garbage ("5abc" became 5) instead of rejecting it, and the same fix was applied to `--max-lines`; `config-get`'s bare-key lookup matched any section instead of requiring genuine top-level placement, and separately failed to match aligned/tab-indented keys before `=`; concurrent hook processes recording a genuine new read for the same file each lost one increment via `Math.max` instead of reconciling; the web-fetch manifest map was keyed on URL alone instead of `(url, prompt)`; expired cross-session manifest files were skipped instead of deleted, accumulating on disk forever; `compact-hint` always returned a fake "cool 0%" reading instead of validating `--limit` and loading the real session cache; `webFetches`/`bashOutputs` were discarded from the session cache, so neither contributed to context-pressure/adaptive-budget calculations regardless of actual activity; session snapshot storage ignored `TOKEN_GOAT_HOME`; `semantic`'s near-hit merge ran after truncating to `--limit` instead of before, so it could only shrink an already-capped result set; a monorepo with several submodules had their `.git` pointer files miscounted as nested repos, walking past the real project root; and `SOURCE_EXT_RE` had drifted from `parser_types.ts`, wrongly including `.swift` and omitting `.cs`, `.mjs`/`.cjs`/`.mts`/`.cts`, `.cc`/`.cxx`/`.hpp`/`.hxx`, `.kts`, and `.pyi`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts), [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts), [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts), [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts), [src/snapshots.ts](src/snapshots.ts), [src/project.ts](src/project.ts), and [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files.

- **A notebook edited via the `NotebookEdit` tool wasn't tracked in the post-edit pipeline** (only `Write`/`Edit` were registered), leaving `.ipynb` files permanently misclassified as unmodified; separately, `hooks_read.ts`'s already-implemented notebook-output-stripping regressed to a no-op after the TypeScript port because it was never actually called from `pre_read`, silently losing the documented 60-95% savings on notebook reads. See [src/hooks_edit.ts](src/hooks_edit.ts) and [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files.

- **Screenshot tools were treated as read-only and cached like an idempotent read**, dedup-suppressing repeat screenshot calls for 45 seconds and defeating the `pre_screenshot` hook added in 2.6.2; the tool-name pattern used to detect a screenshot call was also too narrow, missing real MCP naming conventions like `puppeteer_screenshot`. Separately, `Grep` on a large file was still hitting two size-gates meant only for whole-file `Read`, since `estimateRequestedSlice()` always reports "unbounded" for `Grep`; that hard-deny path is now correctly scoped to `Read` only. See [src/mcp_cache.ts](src/mcp_cache.ts), [src/hooks_screenshot.ts](src/hooks_screenshot.ts), and [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested across the corresponding test files.

- **A `cd`-prefixed Bash command's read hints resolved against the raw path instead of the `cd` target.** See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **Two dead code paths were removed with no behavior change**, closing out a batch of internal cleanup alongside the fixes above: `indexFile`/`indexFiles` (async, zero production callers, and their doc comment describing matching error handling to `indexFileSync` was itself wrong) and `HookOutput`'s `update` variant (zero producers, and a wire shape that didn't match any real Claude Code hook contract). Test scaffolding for hook-event/bundle/`runCli` setup was also consolidated across test files, incidentally fixing 41 `force: true` sites that had been masking real assertion failures. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts) and [src/types.ts](src/types.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts) and across the consolidated test helpers.
## [2.6.2] - 2026-07-03

### Added

- **SQLite schema-version check and migration scaffolding.** `db.ts` now stamps `PRAGMA user_version` with a `SCHEMA_VERSION` constant on init, refuses to open a DB whose stored version is newer than the running build supports (a clear error instead of silent corruption), and walks a `MIGRATIONS` table for any older on-disk schema — currently a no-op walker since no migrations exist yet, but it closes a real gap: index DB format changes had no upgrade path at all. See [src/db.ts](src/db.ts); regression-tested in [tests/db.test.ts](tests/db.test.ts).

- **The `pre_screenshot` hook — documented in the README and CHANGELOG since the Python-to-TS port, but never actually implemented — now exists.** `image_shrink.screenshot_redirect` (default on) was fully wired into config with no handler behind it, so MCP screenshot calls without a destination file landed raw in context. `hooks_screenshot.ts` denies `mcp__*take_screenshot` calls that omit a destination argument, naming the correct parameter for the specific tool — chrome-devtools-mcp's `take_screenshot` takes `filePath`, while Microsoft's `@playwright/mcp` `browser_take_screenshot` takes `filename`, a discrepancy from what the shipped docs implied. See [src/hooks_screenshot.ts](src/hooks_screenshot.ts) and [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_screenshot.test.ts](tests/hooks_screenshot.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **The background worker daemon never actually stayed running.** `--worker-daemon` was rejected outright by commander before `workerEntry()`'s dispatch logic ever ran, so incremental reindexing driven by the detached daemon process was entirely non-functional. `cli.ts::run()` now checks for the flag and dispatches straight to the daemon loop before commander parses argv. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker_daemon_e2e.test.ts](tests/worker_daemon_e2e.test.ts), which spawns the real built bundle and confirms the daemon stays alive and drains a seeded dirty-queue entry.

- **A missing export broke the build on HEAD.** `hooks_read.ts` imported `BYTE_RANGE_ADVICE` from `file_type_handler.ts`, which never exported it — `npm run typecheck` and the bundle build were broken, silently invalidating every test run made against that state. See [src/hints/file_type_handler.ts](src/hints/file_type_handler.ts).

- **`dispatchFileTypeHandler` ignored the narrowed offset/limit size hint for three of its five handlers.** `contentLengthHint` was already threaded through `handlePdf`/`handleGenericLarge` but not `handleHtml`/`handleTxt`/`handleCsv`, so a narrowed read of a large HTML/text/CSV file was still gated on the full file's size instead of the requested slice. See [src/hints/file_type_handler.ts](src/hints/file_type_handler.ts); regression-tested in [tests/file_type_handler.test.ts](tests/file_type_handler.test.ts) and [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).

- **The worker silently counted a genuinely failed reindex as a success.** A caught indexing exception returned the same falsy sentinel as "file unchanged, skip," so `processDirtyBatch` treated a real parse/write failure identically to a no-op. Failures are now logged to `worker-errors.log` next to `global.db` and returned as a distinct sentinel; the file's stored SHA is left untouched so the next edit naturally retriggers reindexing. See [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts); regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts).

- **`read_commands.ts`'s partial-path symbol fallback didn't fold case on case-insensitive filesystems.** Every other path-comparison site in the codebase (`parser.ts`, `index_prune.ts`, `sql_path.ts`, `walk_index.ts`, `worker.ts`) already uses the established `foldPath`/`isCaseInsensitiveFs` pattern; this one fallback filter compared raw paths, so a symbol lookup by a differently-cased path could silently miss on Windows/macOS. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands_collation.test.ts](tests/read_commands_collation.test.ts).

- **A UTF-8 BOM on a markdown/YAML/TOML file could hide its first heading or top-level key from symbol extraction.** `parseFile`, `readSection`, `listSections`, and `listAllSections` now strip a leading BOM before parsing. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts) and [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts); regression-tested in [tests/section_reader.test.ts](tests/section_reader.test.ts).

- **A `mkdirSync` race between two processes creating the same directory could throw `EEXIST` and crash a write path.** A new shared `ensureDirSync()` helper swallows `EEXIST` (still propagating every other error) and replaces five raw `mkdirSync` call sites across `config_commands.ts`, `project_memory.ts`, and `install.ts`. See [src/util.ts](src/util.ts); regression-tested in [tests/util.test.ts](tests/util.test.ts) with a synthetic-EEXIST injection — the initial test only exercised the native `recursive: true` path and never actually reached the catch block, since strengthened to genuinely fail without the fix.

- **A CRLF-terminated heredoc closing delimiter was false-flagged as unbalanced shell syntax.** `detectUnbalancedShellSyntax` now strips a trailing `\r` before comparing the closing line to the delimiter. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **Truncation in `bash_compress.ts`/`overflow_guard.ts` could split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**, corrupting an emoji or other astral character sitting at the truncation boundary. Both now use a `safeSlice` helper that backs off one code unit when it would land inside a low surrogate. Regression-tested in [tests/bash_compress.test.ts](tests/bash_compress.test.ts) and [tests/overflow_guard.test.ts](tests/overflow_guard.test.ts).

- **`diagnoseNearMiss`'s CRLF/LF mismatch diagnostic only checked one direction.** A file using LF whose search text used CRLF was silently missed. Both directions are now normalized and compared. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).

- **A stale test still asserted removed `ImageShrinkConfig` fields** (`prefer_avif`, `avif_quality`) instead of the current schema. See [tests/config.test.ts](tests/config.test.ts).

## [2.6.1] - 2026-07-02

### Added

- **A new `token-goat replace <file>` CLI command closes the "Read denied → Edit permanently blocked" trap.** Claude Code's Edit tool requires a prior successful Read; several of token-goat's own `pre_read` denials (markdown re-read, source-file re-read, generic re-read, files over the large-file first-read cap, and both truncated-file re-read sites) leave no way to ever successfully Read a file again this session, permanently blocking Edit on it too — reproduced live multiple times this session, independently, across unrelated projects. `token-goat replace <file> --old-from <oldfile> --new-from <newfile>` (or `--old-b64`/`--new-b64`, plus `--all` to replace every occurrence) edits the file directly via Node `fs`, bypassing Read/Edit and their hooks entirely; it requires the old string to match exactly once by default, erroring clearly on zero or multiple matches, and writes back atomically via the existing `atomicWriteBuffer`. The six deny messages that actually block Edit now point at it. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts) and [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).

- **A `sed -n` command with multiple semicolon-joined ranges (`sed -n '24,28p;65,84p' file`) now gets one hint covering every range, not just the first.** `extractSedRange` parses each `N,Mp` clause independently and validates it; each range is checked against this session's already-read line ranges for that file, so a mix of overlapping and fresh ranges in one command reports an overlap hint for what's already been read and a fresh-range hint (`token-goat read "file@start-end"`) for the rest, joined with an Oxford comma for three or more ranges. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **`pre_compact` emitted an invalid hook wire shape, silently breaking the compaction manifest on every `/compact`.** `serializeOutput()` wrapped every `context` `HookOutput` in a `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` object tagged with the current event name, but per the harness's docs, `PreCompact` (and `Notification`) reject `additionalContext` there entirely — the harness rejected the output outright for `pre_compact`, so the session manifest this hook exists to inject was never delivered before a compaction. Fixed to route those two events through the top-level `systemMessage` field instead, driven by an explicit `EVENTS_WITHOUT_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT` table (verified against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) rather than a single hardcoded event check, so a future handler on either event can't silently reproduce the bug. A prior test asserted the broken shape as correct; it's corrected, and a matrix test now covers every hook event's serialized shape rather than a hand-picked subset. See [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts) and [tests/hook_registry.test.ts](tests/hook_registry.test.ts).

- **`write-file` (and the new `replace`) never told the background indexer a file had changed.** Only the Edit tool's `postEditHandler` called `appendDirtyPath`; both CLI-side write commands wrote directly via `atomicWriteBuffer` with no equivalent enqueue, so a file edited through either command stayed stale in the symbol index until a manual `token-goat index` — caught live while testing `replace` against token-goat's own source. A new `enqueueDirtyPathSafe` helper (fail-soft — a queue-append error never blocks the write it follows) is now called from all four write paths (`write-file`'s `--from`/`--b64`/stdin modes and `replace`). See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).

## [2.6.0] - 2026-07-02

### Added

- **Cross-agent read deduplication: token-goat can now warn when a sibling session already read a file.** Multiple subagents working the same project each independently paid the full cost of reading a file no other session had told them about. When enabled (opt-in, default off), `preReadHandler` checks whether any sibling Claude Code session recently read the file and emits an informational hint instead of denying the read; `postReadHandler` writes each session's reads to a per-project manifest (`<dataDir>/projects/<hash>/sessions/<sessionId>.json`) for sibling discovery. Config: `hints.cross_session_read_dedup` (default `false`) and `hints.cross_session_read_dedup_ttl_secs` (default 2700s), overridable via `TOKEN_GOAT_CROSS_SESSION_READ_DEDUP`/`_TTL_SECS`. Handles missing projects, stale manifests, and corrupt JSON gracefully. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts) and [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cross_session_read_dedup.test.ts](tests/cross_session_read_dedup.test.ts).

- **A bash command with unbalanced quotes or an unterminated heredoc now gets a context hint before it runs.** `detectUnbalancedShellSyntax` tracks single-quote toggling (outside double-quote regions), double-quote escaping, and heredoc termination (respecting the `<<-` indentation modifier), and `preBashHandler` emits a non-blocking hint suggesting the Write tool for multi-line strings with special characters when it finds a mismatch. Common patterns like `git commit -m "don't forget"` are recognized as balanced and don't false-positive. Config: `hints.warn_unbalanced_shell_quoting` (default `true`), overridable via `TOKEN_GOAT_WARN_UNBALANCED_SHELL_QUOTING`. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/shell_quote_hint.test.ts](tests/shell_quote_hint.test.ts).

- **Optional observability for whether large-file hints actually change model behavior.** When `hints.log_large_file_hint_outcomes` is enabled (default off), token-goat now records `large_file_hint_ignored` (the file was read twice — the hint fired but a full re-read happened anyway) and `large_file_hint_followed` (the hint fired, then a surgical `token-goat read` was used instead), persisting pending-hint state across session boundaries via `session_store`. Overridable via `TOKEN_GOAT_LOG_LARGE_FILE_HINT_OUTCOMES`. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts) and [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts); regression-tested in [tests/finding3_hint_outcomes.test.ts](tests/finding3_hint_outcomes.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **The indexer's critical path — dirty-queue draining and symbol/embedding correctness — had several silent-data-loss bugs.** In [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), `drainOnce` deleted the claimed `.draining` queue file *before* processing its batch, so a crash mid-batch lost every path it named; cleanup now happens only after the batch is durably processed, for both crash-recovery and live-claim paths, and a leftover `.draining` file from a failed cleanup is now tracked instead of silently reprocessed forever. [src/hooks_index.ts](src/hooks_index.ts)'s pre-compact handler stopped deleting the live dirty queue out from under a concurrent append, `appendDirtyPath` now starts its write with a newline when the queue doesn't already end in one (so a crash-torn last line can't merge with the next appended path), and `postEditHandler` now fails soft on a transient `appendDirtyPath` error (disk full, permission, Windows lock) instead of crashing the whole handler and leaving the session cache out of sync with the dirty queue. Separately in [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts), a JSON property's `lineEnd` understated multi-line values, a function declared inside another function was indexed as a top-level symbol, and a transient read failure on the async `indexFile` path wiped a file's existing rows instead of no-op'ing like the sync path; the file's stored SHA is now hashed from the actual buffer that was parsed rather than a second, possibly-stale disk read, so incremental reindexing can no longer get permanently stuck comparing against the wrong content. [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts)'s `upsertChunks` now delegates to the BigInt-coercing `insertChunkVector` (a plain-number rowid bind threw against a real `vec0` table) and runs its delete-then-insert as one transaction so a failed insert can't leave a file's embeddings deleted with nothing to replace them. [src/db.ts](src/db.ts) now closes a just-opened handle if a later `initConnection` setup step throws, instead of leaking the file descriptor. Regression-tested in [tests/worker.test.ts](tests/worker.test.ts), [tests/worker_draining_rmfail.test.ts](tests/worker_draining_rmfail.test.ts), [tests/hooks_index.test.ts](tests/hooks_index.test.ts), [tests/hooks_edit.test.ts](tests/hooks_edit.test.ts), [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts), [tests/parser_sha_race.test.ts](tests/parser_sha_race.test.ts), and [tests/embeddings_vec_insert.test.ts](tests/embeddings_vec_insert.test.ts).

- **The pre-compact manifest was rendering garbage (`- 0`, `- 1`) instead of the files a session actually read or edited.** `SessionCacheObject.files`/`editedFiles` were still typed as the old Python-era path-keyed dict format, but the real writer (`session_store.ts`'s `saveSessionState`) had long since moved to a `FileEntry[]` array with a per-entry `wasEdited` flag. `Object.keys()` on that array returned numeric indices instead of paths, so every manifest built from a real on-disk session — `compact-hint`, `buildManifest`/`buildManifestAdaptive` — rendered nonsense. The existing test suite drove `buildManifest` against hand-built dict-shaped fixtures and never against real `saveSessionState` output, an injected-seam trap that couldn't have caught this. Fixed by adding `session_store.ts::readSessionStateFile`, a non-mutating export that reuses the module's existing array/legacy-dict normalization, and having `compact.ts`'s `_loadSessionCache` delegate to it; every downstream call site (`pressureRawTotal`, `inferSessionGoal`, `eventCount`, `_editedFileCount`, `_buildManifestText`, `computeAdaptiveBudget`, `buildManifestWithCount`) now derives read/edited files from the array via `wasEdited`, and `_buildManifestText` tags truncated reads using `wasTruncated`. See [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts) and [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts); regression-tested in [tests/compact.test.ts](tests/compact.test.ts), stash-verified to fail against the pre-fix reader and pass against the fix.

- **Session identity, session-directory resolution, and cross-process session-state merging had several independent bugs.** `getSessionId()` read the nonexistent `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` env var instead of the real `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, so every call fell back to a freshly generated random id and session state could never correlate across process launches in the same Claude Code session; `cmdInstall`/`cmdSkillCompact` now resolve the session via `getSessionId()` instead of an unrelated in-memory map that always fell through to a hardcoded `'default'` bucket, and `compact.ts`'s `findLatestSessionId`/`_loadSessionCache` now resolve the sessions directory via `tokenGoatHome()` (where `session_store.ts` actually writes) instead of the unrelated `dataDir()` XDG path, which had never had anything written to it. On the merge side, `session_store.ts` had a family of resurrection/eviction bugs in how concurrent processes reconcile a shared disk snapshot: a consumed `pendingLargeFileHints` entry could be resurrected by a process that only loaded it and never acted on it (fixed by tracking keys actually acted on this run); `recordFileEdit` silently dropped the `wasTruncated` flag when rebuilding an entry instead of spreading the prior one; and `mergeLineRanges` evicted already-disk-persisted ranges from other processes to make room for local reads instead of just capping local growth. `recordFileEdit` also now clears a file's recorded sed line-range history when it's edited, since post-edit line numbers no longer describe the pre-edit ranges. Two smaller compact-manifest gaps: `eventCount` omitted `webHistory` from its total (diverging from the actually-shipped `buildManifestWithCount` computation), and the read-files section could double-list a file that was also edited. See [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts), and [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/session.test.ts](tests/session.test.ts), [tests/session_store.test.ts](tests/session_store.test.ts), and [tests/compact.test.ts](tests/compact.test.ts).

- **`compact-doc` and the compact-sidecar hooks are now fully wired end to end, closing out a feature that had shipped only partially.** `buildExtractiveCompact`/`writeCompact`/`isCompactFresh` had no callers: the `compact-doc` CLI command only ran an older `COMPACT_END`-marker extractor, and its own help text described hook-serving as a planned future feature. `compact-doc` now takes `--force`/`--sentences`/`--show`, backed by a new `compactPathFor()` sidecar-path helper, and actually builds and reuses the sidecars the README already documented (`--heading` keeps working for the legacy marker-extraction mode). `pre_read` now checks for a fresh compact sidecar (gated on `hints.stable_doc_compacts`) and serves its body in place of a full read of a large reference doc, matching the existing doc-diff-on-reread pattern of embedding real content in the deny message. `post_edit` now marks a file's sidecar stale (via `markCompactStale`, which previously had no caller) right after the dirty-queue append, so a changed source file falls through to a normal full read instead of serving a stale compact. See [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts), [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts), and [src/hooks_edit.ts](src/hooks_edit.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_compact.test.ts](tests/doc_compact.test.ts) and [tests/doc_compact_hook.test.ts](tests/doc_compact_hook.test.ts).

- **Extractive compacts for docs and notebooks had three correctness bugs.** `extractDocCompact` returned the text *after* the `COMPACT_END` marker instead of before it, inverting the documented convention (everything above the marker is the compact form) that `skill_cache.ts` already follows correctly — the existing tests encoded the inverted behavior as correct and never caught it. Separately, `extractDocCompact`'s heading lookup used a plain `line.includes(heading)` substring check, so ordinary prose mentioning a heading's text ("See the Setup guide below") could match before the real `## Setup` heading and return the wrong slice; it now requires a real markdown heading line. `notebook_compact.ts`'s `getOrCreateSidecar` keyed each cached sidecar on the source notebook's content hash with no eviction path, so every distinct version of a notebook that was ever compacted left its sidecar behind forever; a new `pruneSidecars` (mirroring `disk_cache`'s write-then-prune convention) now runs after each write, bounded by count and age. See [src/doc_compact.ts](src/doc_compact.ts) and [src/notebook_compact.ts](src/notebook_compact.ts); regression-tested in [tests/doc_compact.test.ts](tests/doc_compact.test.ts) and [tests/notebook_compact.test.ts](tests/notebook_compact.test.ts).

- **`pack`'s file-collection could be tricked into reading outside the project root via a symlink swapped mid-request.** `collectFiles`/`estimateBudget` validated a candidate path's containment via `fs.realpathSync`, then separately re-touched the same path with `fs.statSync`/`fs.readFileSync` — a TOCTOU window in which a concurrent process could retarget a symlink between the check and the read, so the bytes actually read were never guaranteed to be the bytes that were validated. Both functions now open the candidate once via `openWithinRoot`, binding a file descriptor to one specific inode up front and cross-checking the resolved real path's device/inode against that fd before trusting it; all subsequent size/content reads go through the fd. A related, earlier fix in the same area resolved real paths before the root-containment check in the first place, to close a plain (non-race) symlink escape. See [src/pack.ts](src/pack.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pack_toctou_race.test.ts](tests/pack_toctou_race.test.ts).

- **`pack`'s comment stripping corrupted URLs and CSS colors inside string literals, and its secret scanner missed common unquoted assignments.** `stripComments` stripped everything from the first `//` or `#` onward with no awareness of whether that sequence sat inside a quoted string, mangling the `//` in `https://example.com` and `#fff` CSS hex colors that happened to appear in string literals across TS/JS, shell, Ruby, and similar languages; it now tracks quote state per line (mirroring `text_commands.ts`'s `isInsideStringLiteral`) and leaves a comment-like sequence untouched inside an open string. The "Generic API key" secret pattern's boundary character class was `["\s]` — a literal quote, backslash, or the letter `s`, not the intended `\s` whitespace shorthand — and never included a single quote, so assignments like `api_key='...'` or `api_key = ...` passed through unflagged; the class is now `[\s"']`. `bash_compress.ts`'s git-diff fast path also bypassed the same `maxLines`/`maxLineLength` caps every other output path is bound by, so a diff touching many files could still emit thousands of lines, and it reported a misleading "0 files changed" summary for a valid diff with no `diff --git ` header; `compressGitDiff` now returns `null` (falling back to general truncation) when it doesn't recognize the format, and its output is capped like everything else when it does. See [src/pack.ts](src/pack.ts) and [src/bash_compress.ts](src/bash_compress.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pack.test.ts](tests/pack.test.ts) and [tests/bash_compress.test.ts](tests/bash_compress.test.ts).

- **Three SSRF gaps closed in the (currently unwired) `webfetch.ts` fetch pipeline, plus a live redirect-bomb gap in `config_commands.ts`.** `isPrivateIPv6` matched `fc00::`/`fe80::` as literal string prefixes instead of the true `fc00::/7`/`fe80::/10` CIDR ranges, and never unwrapped IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) or IPv4-translated (`::ffff:0:a.b.c.d`) addresses before checking them, so a private IPv4 address wrapped in either IPv6 notation sailed through; it now does real bitwise prefix matching on the parsed 16-bit groups and routes embedded IPv4 through `isPrivateIPv4`, which itself was missing the `0.0.0.0/8` and `100.64.0.0/10` (carrier-grade NAT) ranges. `ssrfPinnedLookup`'s `ALLOW_UNRESOLVED` fallback ran a raw `dns.lookup` and handed the result straight to the connecting socket with no private-IP check at all — a classic DNS-rebinding bypass — and is now validated like every other path. A second pass on the same file closed a cached `.meta` JSON's `shrunk_path` being read back with no containment check (a cache-directory write access could plant a path pointing anywhere on disk), replaced the SSRF check-then-fetch (TOCTOU) pattern with raw `http`/`https` requests pinned to a single resolved address via a custom DNS `lookup` option, kept a single wall-clock deadline armed across redirects/headers/body instead of clearing it once headers arrived (previously an unbounded slow-loris body download), and added conditional-header revalidation (`If-None-Match`/`If-Modified-Since`, extending the cache entry on a 304 instead of a blind re-fetch). Separately, `config_commands.ts`'s `fetchBuffer` recursed on every HTTP redirect with no depth limit, unlike `webfetch.ts`'s own 5-redirect cap — an unbounded or malicious redirect chain could recurse indefinitely; it now mirrors the same `MAX_REDIRECTS`/`redirectsLeft` pattern. None of the `webfetch.ts` gaps had direct test coverage before this pass — `isPrivateIPv6` wasn't even exported. See [src/webfetch.ts](src/webfetch.ts) and [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/webfetch.test.ts](tests/webfetch.test.ts) and [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).

- **WebFetch, Google Drive, and `resume` caching had several cross-cutting correctness bugs.** The WebFetch dedup cache key was derived from the URL alone, ignoring the prompt — since a WebFetch answer is prompt-specific, a second fetch of the same URL with a different question was denied and pointed at the first, unrelated answer; the cache id is now a `(url, prompt)` composite. The dedup lookup also only checked an in-memory, process-scoped map, so a cached answer written by one process was invisible to a different CLI invocation even though it was already on disk; `preFetchHandler` now derives the cache id the same pure-function way `getWebOutput`'s disk fallback does. A cached-URL hit previously only emitted a non-blocking hint, so the model's WebFetch call ran the real network fetch anyway; it now denies the redundant fetch outright, matching the deny-on-hit convention used elsewhere. `web_cache.ts` also gained a TTL check on disk reads, so an expired entry is no longer served as fresh. `gdrive.ts`'s `fetchDoc` looked up cached fetches through the deliberately memory-only `getWebOutputByUrl`, so `gdrive-sections` always re-fetched from the network even when the doc was already cached on disk from an earlier run; a new `getWebOutputByUrlFromDisk` reads through the existing disk fallback instead. And `resume`'s recovery packet named cached bash-output entries by an opaque hash fingerprint instead of the actual command text. See [src/hooks_fetch.ts](src/hooks_fetch.ts), [src/web_cache.ts](src/web_cache.ts), [src/gdrive.ts](src/gdrive.ts), and [src/resume.ts](src/resume.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts](tests/hooks_fetch.test.ts), [tests/hooks_fetch_persistence.test.ts](tests/hooks_fetch_persistence.test.ts), [tests/web_cache.test.ts](tests/web_cache.test.ts), [tests/gdrive.test.ts](tests/gdrive.test.ts), and [tests/resume.test.ts](tests/resume.test.ts).

- **MCP result caching mis-cached errors and never expired a stale-but-technically-read-only dedup.** `postMcpHandler` cached every read-only `mcp__` result unconditionally, including `CallToolResult` responses carrying `isError: true` — a normal protocol round trip signaling a tool-level failure, not a transport failure — so a transient or already-resolved error could never be retried until the TTL aged out; a new `isMcpErrorResponse` check now skips caching those. Separately, `isMcpReadOnly`'s verb list was missing browser-automation verbs (`click`, `fill`, `navigate`, `drag`, `hover`, `wait_for`, ...), so calls that mutate page/browser state were being cached and deduped as read-only, and the dedup deny had no expiry at all — unsound even for genuinely read-only tools whose results can legitimately change (search, inbox, live-page reads). Added a configurable `mcp_dedup_ttl_secs` (default 45s, `TOKEN_GOAT_MCP_DEDUP_TTL_SECS`) so a repeat is only denied inside the TTL window. See [src/hooks_mcp.ts](src/hooks_mcp.ts) and [src/mcp_cache.ts](src/mcp_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts](tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts) and [tests/mcp_cache.test.ts](tests/mcp_cache.test.ts).

- **Skill-cache filenames had five distinct collision bugs, plus a lost-update race and unbounded growth.** `sanitizeSkillId`'s `:`→`_` substitution (plus an `n` discriminator suffix) was not injective — `test:a` and `test_an` both sanitized to `test_an`, silently colliding two skills' compact/hit caches; it now maps `:` to `~`, a character outside the allowed skill-name charset, so no legitimate name can collide with it. `hasSessionOutput` used a raw filename `startsWith` prefix check, so a skill like `ralph-loop` could false-positive-match an already-cached `ralph-loop-extended`; `getCompactAnySession(Sync)` used `filename.includes(name)`, a substring test with the same problem; and `listSkills` recovered a session fragment via `split('-')[0]`, which truncates a UUID-shaped session id at its first hyphen. All four now use exact or delimiter-bounded matching. `incrementSkillHit`/`readSkillHits` also skipped the `safeSkillName` validation every other cache-writing path applies, and are now guarded against a TOCTOU lost-update: two concurrent callers reading the same pre-increment hit count could both bump it locally and lose one hit to whichever write landed last, closed with an mkdir-based lock (atomic on both POSIX and Windows) with bounded retry and stale-lock reclamation. Finally, the `'skills'` cache subdirectory had no eviction path at all (the generic `pruneBlobs` only understands single-blob caches, not `skill_cache.ts`'s per-entry `.txt`/`.meta`/`.gz` groups under a different base directory), so cached skill bodies accumulated forever; `prune-cache`/`clean-cache` now route skill outputs through a dedicated `pruneSkillOutputs` pass. See [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts) and [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/skill_cache.test.ts](tests/skill_cache.test.ts) and [tests/cache_session_commands_skills.test.ts](tests/cache_session_commands_skills.test.ts).
