- **More brace-depth and scope-tracking edge cases fixed across the regex-based language adapters, continuing the pattern from 2.3.0.** PowerShell dropped symbols after a same-line `<# ... #>` inline comment (which short-circuited the whole line into brace-counting-only mode) and lost every top-level declaration after a one-liner class (`class Foo { }`, which never raised `braceDepth` above `classStartDepth`); a `<#` inside a string literal was also mistaken for a real comment opener, swallowing everything until an unrelated `#>` appeared later in the file. Kotlin's `currentClass` stuck on a multi-line primary-constructor header (common with ktlint formatting) and the adapter had no block-comment awareness at all, so a stray brace inside a `/* */` comment desynced the counter for the rest of the file. C# had the same one-liner/brace-less-header sticking bug for records and single-line classes, and counted braces inside a full-line `//` comment. PHP's block-comment scanner treated a bare `/*` substring as an opener even inside a string literal (`glob('src/*.php')`), permanently swallowing the rest of the file as "inside a comment." And the shared `isInsideStringLiteral` helper counted single- and double-quote occurrences as two independent parity counters instead of tracking one open-quote state, so an apostrophe inside a double-quoted string (`"don't panic"`) flipped the single-quote parity and made a real `/*` later on the line invisible to block-comment detection. See [src/languages/powershell_idx.ts](src/languages/powershell_idx.ts), [src/languages/kotlin.ts](src/languages/kotlin.ts), [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts), [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts), and [src/languages/common.ts](src/languages/common.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` are now parsed.** `INDEX_RE` didn't account for the optional `CONCURRENTLY` keyword, so `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_foo ON ...` captured the wrong token as the index name, and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` statements weren't recognized as a symbol kind at all. See [src/languages/sql_idx.ts](src/languages/sql_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **`code_compress.ts` mishandled nested and multi-line template literals.** `stripComments` and `skipBraceBody` scan line by line, tracking "inside a template literal" as a single flag or resetting string-tracking state at the start of every line. A template literal nested inside another literal's `${...}` interpolation broke the flag-based tracking: the inner literal's opening backtick got paired with the outer one as if it closed the string, so a `//` inside the exposed nested string was stripped as a fake comment, and a stray `{`/`}` inside it was counted toward brace depth, silently truncating the enclosing function. A template literal that opened on one line and closed on a later one had the same problem across line boundaries. Both functions now track a stack of per-nesting-level interpolation brace depths and carry "still inside an unclosed backtick" state between lines. See [src/code_compress.ts](src/code_compress.ts); regression-tested in [tests/code_compress.test.ts](tests/code_compress.test.ts).

- **Several index and dedup-key lookups missed on Windows due to inconsistent path normalization.** `repomap.ts`'s `buildMap` passed the raw, backslash-joined path from `getTrackedFiles` straight into `querySymbols` instead of resolving through `resolveIndexPath` first (every other caller does), so `token-goat map`'s `topSymbols`/`symbolCount` were wrong or empty for every file on Windows. `index_prune.ts`'s `pruneDeletedFiles` compared the stored path and root prefix with a raw case-sensitive `startsWith` instead of the `foldPath` convention used elsewhere, leaking stale rows for deleted files on case-insensitive filesystems. The CLI surgical-read dedup key (`extractTgSurgicalRead`) normalized drive-letter case and slash direction but never resolved a relative spec against the command's working directory, so two different projects reading their own relative `src/foo.ts` collided under one dedup key; it's now resolved against `cwd`, and two invocations differing only in drive-letter case or slash direction are now deduped instead of tracked as distinct keys. See [src/repomap.ts](src/repomap.ts), [src/index_prune.ts](src/index_prune.ts), and [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/repomap.test.ts](tests/repomap.test.ts), [tests/index_prune.test.ts](tests/index_prune.test.ts), and [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **Six more pre/post-Bash-hook correctness bugs.** `extractPythonFileRead`'s python-command regex matched anywhere in the command instead of being anchored to the start, false-positiving on commands that merely mention "python" in passing (e.g. a commit message) while an unrelated `open(...)` call elsewhere went undetected. `detectUnbalancedShellSyntax` false-flagged escaped quotes outside a string (`\"`), arithmetic shifts inside `$(( ... ))`, and apostrophes inside a real `#` comment as unbalanced syntax. The sed line-range dedup and the CLI surgical-read dedup (`skill-body`/`skill-compact --path`) both now normalize the tracked file path via `resolveIndexPath` before using it as a dedup key, so a relative and an absolute reference to the same file collide under one key instead of tracking separate, never-overlapping ranges; the surgical-read dedup for `read`/`section` also now strips a `@N-M` line-range suffix before deriving the file path, so a range-scoped read cross-references the plain-path ledger correctly. And `postBashHandler`'s `curl -o` download recording only marks a download successful (enabling the recall-deny on a repeat) after confirming the exit code was 0/unknown *and* the claimed output file actually exists on disk — a failed download (network error, 404) was previously recorded as if it succeeded, permanently blocking a retry of the same command. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **Several CLI commands were unreachable, silently mis-parsed, or degraded instead of erroring on bad input.** `context-stats` was fully implemented in `cli_context_stats.ts` but never registered in the CLI dispatcher; `stats` bypassed the full `StatsOptions` implementation (`--json`, `--window-days`, `--by-project`, `--by-command` were all unavailable) via a separate inline handler; and `section --list` was rejected outright by Commander because `read_commands.ts`'s `runListSections` was never wired to a flag — all three are now registered and routed correctly. `guard()`, the wrapper around every guarded command, also unconditionally reset `process.exitCode = 0` after a handler resolved, so a handler that deliberately set a non-zero exit without throwing (e.g. `skill-section` on a missing heading) was silently reported as success. On the input side, numeric flags across `grep --max-lines`, `call-chain --depth`, `pack`/`context-for --budget`, `history --limit`, `--limit`/`--top` on `symbol`/`refs`/`callers`/`impact`/`similar`/`dead`/`types`/`arch`, `skeleton`/`outline --min-lines`, and `prune-cache --maxCount`/`--maxAgeHours` parsed with a bare `Number.parseInt` instead of the shared `requireInt` validator, so an invalid value silently produced `NaN` and downstream degraded behavior (empty output, a disabled cap, or an opaque SQLite "datatype mismatch") instead of a clean error; all now route through `requireInt`. `pack`'s absolute-glob handling also mis-joined an already-absolute glob match against the project root, and silently fell back to reading stdin whenever an explicit pattern matched zero files instead of erroring; and `skill-section`'s spec parser rejected a skill name or heading containing its own `::` by splitting on the first occurrence instead of the shared last-occurrence `findSpecSeparator()` helper. `bash-output`/`web-output --section` also left content unchanged (silently printing the full unfiltered output) instead of erroring when the requested heading wasn't found, unlike every other `--heading` command. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [src/cli_context_stats.ts](src/cli_context_stats.ts), [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts), and [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts), [tests/cli_context_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_context_stats.test.ts), [tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts](tests/cli_limit_validation.test.ts), [tests/cli_skill_section.test.ts](tests/cli_skill_section.test.ts), [tests/cli_output_section_notfound.test.ts](tests/cli_output_section_notfound.test.ts), and [tests/cli_section_list.test.ts](tests/cli_section_list.test.ts).

- **`token-goat doctor`'s config check and diagnostics silently misreported real state.** `checkConfigValid()` parsed the project config file with `JSON.parse()`, but the real format is TOML (see `constants.ts`'s `configPath()`); since a file written by `config set` is never valid JSON, `doctor` reported a permanent spurious failure after any config write — the existing tests wrote JSON fixtures against `.json` paths, matching the bug instead of production reality. `checkWorkerRunning` used a `tasklist` grep instead of the existing `isWorkerRunning` helper, `checkDbExists` still looked for the retired `index.db` instead of the current `global.db`, and `cli_stats`'s session-format check read the old Python `file_access_counts` object instead of the current TS `files` array. See [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts) and [src/cli_stats.ts](src/cli_stats.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli_doctor.test.ts](tests/cli_doctor.test.ts) and [tests/cli_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_stats.test.ts).

- **The bash-output cache served stale results and mis-tracked several fields.** Cached entries were only checked against an in-memory command-hash index with no awareness of cwd or git/directory/lockfile state; `preBashHandler`'s four recall sites (monitoring, curl GET, `gh api`, generic build-command) now check the stored fingerprint via `isBashEntryStale` and treat a mismatch as a miss instead of serving it. The fingerprint itself only covered git-mutable/dir-listing/dep-list commands, leaving the most commonly monitored ones (pytest, vitest, jest, go test, eslint, ruff, `npm run`, `git push`, `cat <file>`) with no fingerprint at all — stale output for these could be recalled indefinitely; those now route through the same working-tree-aware git fingerprint, and a new `file` fingerprint kind (mtime+size) covers a single `cat <file>` target. The git fingerprint itself only hashed the HEAD sha and `.git/index`'s mtime, missing unstaged/untracked changes and racily self-invalidating (`git status` refreshes the index's own mtime as a side effect); it now folds in a hash of `git status --porcelain` instead, and a directory-listing command's fingerprint now uses the command's actual working directory instead of the process's. `normalizeCommandForCacheKey` also collapsed whitespace and rewrote backslashes inside quoted arguments, so `echo "a   b"` and `echo "a b"` collapsed to the same cache key; it's now a quote-tracking scanner that copies quoted spans verbatim. Three smaller correctness bugs: `sedOverlapHint` only computed a trailing delta, so a `sed` read starting *before* a previously-served range but only partially overlapping it (prior 50-100, new 40-60) was wrongly reported as fully served; the generic monitoring/build/curl-GET cache write hardcoded `exitCode: 0` regardless of the real result, so a failed build/test cached and recalled as if it had succeeded; and a differently-piped re-run of the same base command (deliberately cache-shared, e.g. `curl url | jq '.a'` then `| jq '.b'`) now names the command that actually produced the cached content when it differs, instead of silently implying it matches. A heredoc terminator also failed to advance the shell-syntax scanner past the body, so a stray apostrophe in heredoc prose ("it's", "don't") could flip a false unbalanced-quote warning. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts) and [src/bash_output_cache.ts](src/bash_output_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts) and [tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts](tests/bash_output_cache.test.ts).

- **Large-file and binary-file read gating in the pre-read hook had several inconsistencies.** The two large-file thresholds — `LARGE_FILE_BYTES` (102,400) and `FILE_TYPE_THRESHOLDS.generic` (100,000) — were separate literals meant to be the same boundary, so a file sized between them got a hard block instead of the softer nudge; `LARGE_FILE_BYTES` now derives from the generic threshold directly. A qualifying large markdown file (>=8KB, >=3 headings) was first changed to hard-deny even the *first* read, which combined with Claude Code's Read-before-Edit precondition meant Edit could never succeed on such a file at all; a follow-up fix corrected this so only a *re-read* within the session is denied and the first read returns a context hint. Re-reading a same-size-or-larger image fell into the generic re-read-dedup branch and got a meaningless "use token-goat read/section/symbol" deny (images are now exempted, matching the existing large-file and universal-file-type exemptions), and `preReadHandler`'s generic large-file deny fired at 500KB — below `image_shrink`'s own 512KB "worth shrinking" threshold — so it always denied a 500-512KB image outright before `preReadImageHandler` (registered second) ever got a chance to run; images are now exempted from both size-based branches so they fall straight through to the shrink handler. `.markdown` (as opposed to `.md`) files were excluded from the doc-diff-on-reread regex, so a changed `.markdown` re-read fell through to a generic "already read" deny instead of serving a diff. The `.improve-state-*.json` re-read deny pointed at `token-goat bash-output <id>`, but these files are exempted from bash-output caching entirely, so the remedy could never resolve to anything — it now points at `sessionArtifactRecall()`. `preReadHandler` is also registered as a pre-hook for the Grep tool, but only ever read the tool's `file_path` field; the real Grep schema names its search target `path`, so a real Grep call never resolved a path and the registration was a guaranteed no-op — a Grep-specific fallback to `path` is now checked. The large-file/universal-file-type denies also called `recordFileRead` right before telling the caller to retry with offset/limit, so that retry hit the "already read" dedup path instead of the same actionable deny; a blocked read is no longer recorded against re-read dedup. Separately, the PDF handler's deny message promised an `offset`/`pages` Read retry that PDFs never honor (every PDF read is blocked unconditionally regardless of size) — an inescapable loop; it now points at `pdftotext` extraction instead, mirroring the existing pandoc pattern for office documents. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts) and [src/hints/file_type_handler.ts](src/hints/file_type_handler.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts) and [tests/file_type_handler.test.ts](tests/file_type_handler.test.ts).

- **Symbol, refs, call-chain, and section lookups had several correctness and completeness bugs.** `refs --callers` scoped its search to the symbol's own defining file (correct for plain `refs`, since the file half of a `file::symbol` spec disambiguates *which* symbol, not *where* its callers live), so a symbol with 20+ real callers spread across the codebase reported no results; `--callers` now searches the whole index. `runRead`'s partial-path fallback matched `utils.ts` against an indexed `myutils.ts` with no path-separator boundary check, and a dotted spec (`ClassName.methodName`) computed but never used the class qualifier, so an ambiguous method name could resolve to the wrong class's method. `find <pattern>` did an exact-name SQL lookup despite its own help text promising pattern-style matching; it now does a case-insensitive substring scan. `bfsCallChains` (backing `call-chain`/`impact`) mislabeled a legitimate cross-branch revisit as a "cycle" instead of a "visited" dedup, and separately double-emitted a chain when every one of a node's callers turned out to be a cycle (the `expanded` flag was only set on the "queued" branch, not the "cycle" branch); `runTypes`/`runScope` also checked JSON-output emptiness after branching into JSON format instead of before, unlike their sibling commands. `querySymbols`'s default 100-symbol limit silently truncated results for files with more symbols, affecting `scope`/`callers`/`test-for`; callers of `buildFileSymCache` now pass an explicit `limit: 10000`. `section --list` (via `listSections`) filtered to only the shallowest heading level present in a document, hiding nested subsections — it now matches `listAllSections`'s all-levels behavior — and a heading spec ending in a literal `#<digits>` ("Issue #42") was always parsed as an ordinal disambiguator and could never resolve; the parser now checks for a verbatim match before falling back to ordinal-stripping. `file::symbol`/`file::Heading` specs also split on the *first* `::` instead of the last, so a POSIX/WSL path legitimately containing `::` mis-split. Finally, `token-goat ask`'s resolved backend (`claude`/`codex`) is a `.cmd`/`.bat` wrapper on Windows with no standalone `.exe`, and `spawnSync`ing it directly without `shell: true` threw an `EINVAL` that a catch block silently swallowed, degrading to a non-backend fallback; it's now detected and run through a shell. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts), [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts), and [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts), [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts), and [tests/section_reader.test.ts](tests/section_reader.test.ts).

- **`config.toml` persistence, validation, and project/memory-file path resolution had several data-integrity bugs.** `loadConfig()` baked any active `TOKEN_GOAT_*` env override directly into the returned `Config` object, so a transient override active for one invocation (e.g. `TOKEN_GOAT_BASH_COMPRESS=0` for a single command) got written to `config.toml` permanently the next time `config set`/`project exclude`/`project prune` saved; a new `loadPersistedConfig()`/`buildPersistedConfig()` (env-cleared) is now used by all three mutate-then-save commands. `config set` also had three related coercion/validation gaps: a comma-separated number-array field (e.g. `hints.backoff_thresholds`) was split into strings with no numeric parsing, silently emptying to `[]` once the load-time int-list validator filtered every entry out; targeting a whole config section (not a leaf field) coerced the raw string in place of the section object, silently wiping every field in it on save; and an out-of-range numeric value wrote successfully with no feedback, only getting clamped on the next load. All three are now rejected or corrected before the value reaches disk. `coerce()` separately lost the "this is a number list" type once an array field was emptied to `[]` (it inferred type from the existing value's length), and `saveConfig` dropped `warn_unbalanced_shell_quoting`/`cross_session_read_dedup`/`cross_session_read_dedup_ttl_secs` from its hints block on every save, silently resetting them to defaults; `loadConfig`'s cache fingerprint also didn't include the cross-session-read-dedup env vars, so toggling them mid-process had no effect until the config file's mtime changed. On the project/memory side, `canonicalize()`'s WSL/MSYS-mount-path rewrite (`/mnt/c/foo` → `c:/foo`) ran unconditionally instead of gated to `win32`, producing garbage on real POSIX Node; `isRepoContainer()` built a candidate path from `Dirent.path` (Node 20.1+ only, undefined on this package's declared Node 18+ minimum), silently disabling detection; `project_memory.ts`'s `save()` hand-rolled a fixed, non-unique temp filename instead of the shared `atomicWriteText` helper, risking two concurrent writers colliding; `memoryPath()`'s home-dir fallback chain landed on a relative `.` when neither `HOME` nor `USERPROFILE` was set instead of `os.homedir()`; and `findMemoryMd`'s project-root slug trimmed leading/trailing dashes, which the real Claude Code project-dir naming convention never does, missing the real `MEMORY.md` for any root that itself starts with non-alphanumeric characters (e.g. a UNC path). See [src/config.ts](src/config.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/project.ts](src/project.ts), and [src/project_memory.ts](src/project_memory.ts); regression-tested in [tests/config.test.ts](tests/config.test.ts), [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts), [tests/project.test.ts](tests/project.test.ts), [tests/project_memory.test.ts](tests/project_memory.test.ts), and [tests/cli_context_stats.test.ts](tests/cli_context_stats.test.ts).

- **The hook relay's dispatch path skipped tool-name normalization and emitted a response shape Claude Code silently drops.** `hooks_cli.ts::normalizePayload()` (Codex/Gemini tool-name aliasing to canonical names, e.g. `bash` → `Bash`) was fully implemented and tested, but nothing in the real dispatch path (`relay()`) ever called it — its only caller, `safeRun()`, was dead code — so a Codex hook invocation's snake_case `tool_name` never got normalized, silently no-opping every handler registered for a specific tool name under Codex. `relay()` now detects the harness and runs `normalizePayload()` before building the event, scoped to the two tool-scoped events. Separately, `hook_registry.ts`'s `serializeOutput` emitted a bare top-level `{"context": "..."}` key for a context hint, which isn't part of Claude Code's documented hook response schema and is silently dropped; the hint now nests under `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` with the correct PascalCase `hookEventName`. And `readStdinJson` accumulated stdin with no size limit (relying solely on a 5s timeout) and, once a size cap was added, didn't tear down the underlying stream when the cap was hit, leaving it flowing at the OS/event-loop level after the app stopped consuming it; it now rejects at 64 MiB and destroys the stream. See [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts) and [src/hook_registry.ts](src/hook_registry.ts); regression-tested in [tests/relay.test.ts](tests/relay.test.ts) and [tests/hook_registry.test.ts](tests/hook_registry.test.ts).

- **`todo` and traceback parsing had a regex-injection bug and two frame-mapping bugs.** `todo`'s `--kinds` flag is documented as a literal comma-separated marker list, but its values were interpolated into a `RegExp` unescaped, so a value containing a regex-special character (e.g. an unbalanced paren) threw `Invalid regular expression` instead of matching literally; kinds are now escaped first. `parseTracebacks`' frame-context peek mis-assigned context when two `File ...` lines appeared consecutively (a frame with no printed source line), pushing the next frame's header as this frame's context; a peeked line is now only consumed as context when it isn't itself a frame header. It also only flushed trailing EOF-terminated frames when the *global* blocks array was still empty instead of scoping the check to the current block, silently dropping a later traceback in multi-traceback input; and `isInsideStringLiteral`'s escaped-backslash counting used a fixed-width lookbehind that only inspects one preceding character, undercounting a string ending in an escaped backslash and misclassifying trailing text as still inside the string — replaced with a per-character backslash-parity counter. See [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).

- **The subagent hallucination-completion warning was rewritten to read a field that doesn't exist, then fixed to read the right one.** An earlier fix in this cycle gated the warning on action verbs found in `event.raw['prompt']` — a field that doesn't exist on the real Claude Code `SubagentStop` payload (`relay.ts` passes the parsed stdin JSON verbatim; the real fields are `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `last_assistant_message`, `agent_id`/`agent_type`/`effort`) — so the check always evaluated false, silently turning the warning off entirely: a 100% false-negative, worse than the original always-fires bug it was meant to fix. It now reads `last_assistant_message`, the subagent's own final report text, which is also a better signal than the original task prompt: it captures what the agent *claims* to have done ("fixed the bug and committed the change") rather than what it was merely asked to do, so a claim of completed changes against a clean git status is a genuine inconsistency. The verb regex was also widened to match past-tense inflections (fix/fixed/fixing, commit/committed) since self-reports are typically past tense. See [src/hooks_session.ts](src/hooks_session.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_session.test.ts](tests/hooks_session.test.ts).

- **`extractChangelogVersionHint` returned the wrong version when scanning past `[Unreleased]`.** It used `OR` instead of `AND` when checking whether it had already passed the `[Unreleased]` heading, so it returned the *first* version heading anywhere in the file — including ones before `[Unreleased]` — instead of the first one that actually follows it. See [src/hints/markdown_hints.ts](src/hints/markdown_hints.ts); regression-tested in [tests/markdown_hints.test.ts](tests/markdown_hints.test.ts).

- **`skill-history` and `skill-diff` no longer error on a fresh install with no cached skills.** Both commands re-implemented the skill-outputs directory scan with a `catch` that turned the missing-directory `ENOENT` (the normal state before any skill has been loaded, and on a fresh CI checkout) into a fatal `Failed to list skill history` / `Failed to diff skill` exit-1. They now reuse the shared, missing-dir-tolerant `listOutputs()` from [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts): an absent cache yields an empty listing (exit 0), removing duplicated readdir logic in the process. Regression-tested against a never-created cache in [tests/skill_history_diff_empty.test.ts](tests/skill_history_diff_empty.test.ts).

- **Concurrent writers to the shared index no longer fail with "database is locked".** token-goat runs as multiple processes against one `global.db` (the worker daemon draining the dirty queue alongside CLI invocations from hooks), so concurrent writers are the normal case. The connection enabled WAL but relied on better-sqlite3's default 5000ms busy timeout, which was exhausted under heavy parallel indexing and surfaced as an intermittent `SqliteError: database is locked` (reproducible in the full test suite against a fresh data directory). The connection now sets an explicit `busy_timeout = 15000`, so a writer waits for a held write lock instead of erroring immediately. Guarded in [tests/db.test.ts](tests/db.test.ts).

- **The test suite no longer reads or writes the developer's real symbol index.** The global test setup isolated `TOKEN_GOAT_HOME` (the bash/web/session cache home) but not `LOCALAPPDATA`/`XDG_DATA_HOME`, which resolve `DATA_DIR` — so any test that indexed wrote token-goat's own symbols into the real `global.db` and raced the live worker daemon writing to that same file, an intermittent `database is locked` that passed on CI (no daemon, fresh checkout) but flaked at pre-push locally. [tests/setup/isolate-home.ts](tests/setup/isolate-home.ts) now points both platform data-dir env vars at a per-worker temp dir, making every local run hermetic and identical to CI's fresh-data-dir condition. Guarded in [tests/data_dir_isolation.test.ts](tests/data_dir_isolation.test.ts).

- **`bash_compress` now re-runs the wrapped command under bash on Windows instead of cmd.exe.** The pre-bash hook rewrites a Bash tool call into `token-goat compress -c '<cmd>'`, and the wrapper re-ran `<cmd>` via `spawnSync` with `shell: true` — which on Windows is `cmd.exe` (`ComSpec`), not the Git-Bash the harness wrote the command for. Bash constructs (`$VAR` / `$(...)` expansion, `2>/dev/null` redirects, single-quote quoting) then failed or returned silently wrong output, and commands whose tool resolved only to a non-`.exe` shim surfaced as `The system cannot execute the specified program`. A new [src/shell.ts](src/shell.ts) resolves the harness's Git-Bash `bash.exe` (skipping the WSL `System32` / `WindowsApps` launchers, which run the Linux filesystem) and [src/bash_runner.ts](src/bash_runner.ts) passes it as the `spawnSync` `shell`; POSIX is unchanged. When no bash is resolvable on Windows the rewrite in [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts) declines, leaving the command to run normally (uncompressed) in the harness bash rather than under cmd.exe. Regression-tested in [tests/shell.test.ts](tests/shell.test.ts) and [tests/bash_runner_shell.test.ts](tests/bash_runner_shell.test.ts).

- **A skill's full body no longer bypasses the compact slice on its first load in a session.** `preSkillHandler` only gated *repeat* loads (a skill already cached this session); the very first `Skill` invocation always let the whole body through, even when a `COMPACT_END` marker made an ~85-90% smaller compact available — on `oss-pr-contribution/SKILL.md` that meant 118.8KB landing in context instead of a 14.7KB compact. The pre-tool-use hook in [src/hooks_skill.ts](src/hooks_skill.ts) now reads the on-disk skill before the first load and denies it too when the body exceeds 6000 bytes (matching the existing `skill-size` staleness threshold) and a compact marker is present, pointing at `token-goat skill-body <name> --compact`; skills with no marker are never gated. `token-goat install` pre-generates each skill's compact from the extracted pre-marker slice rather than the raw body, and `skill-body --compact`/`skill-compact` now use the same `extractCompactFromMarker` helper consistently, fixing a latent bug where `skill-body --compact` returned the content *after* the marker instead of before it. Oversized first-load denials get their own `skill_oversized_first_load` kind in `token-goat stats`. Regression-tested in [tests/hooks_skill.test.ts](tests/hooks_skill.test.ts).

- **Removed `compact_assist.lazy_skill_injection`, a config flag no registered hook ever read.** The [1.0.1](#101) entry describes it as live behavior ("the compaction manifest emits a `token-goat skill-body --compact` recall pointer"), but neither registered `pre_compact` hook ([src/hooks_compact.ts](src/hooks_compact.ts), [src/hooks_index.ts](src/hooks_index.ts)) ever reads it, and the one manifest builder that does reference it, [src/compact.ts](src/compact.ts), is not wired into any hook or CLI path — dead code. The flag and its `TOKEN_GOAT_LAZY_SKILL_INJECTION` env override are removed from [src/config.ts](src/config.ts) and [src/constants.ts](src/constants.ts). This is superseded by the fix directly above: gating full skill bodies at load time in `hooks_skill.ts` is a stronger and now-real enforcement point for the same goal. Regression-tested in [tests/config.test.ts](tests/config.test.ts).

- **`canonicalize()` and `resolveIndexPath()` resolved Windows drive-letter paths incorrectly on non-Windows hosts.** Both gated their Windows-specific handling on `process.platform`/an `isWin32` flag but then called the ambient `path.resolve()`, which follows the real host OS rather than that flag — on Linux (CI's `ubuntu-latest`, or a test that mocks `process.platform` to simulate `win32`), a `C:/...` path in either argument was treated as relative and joined onto the other argument instead of recognized as absolute, corrupting the resolved path and, for `resolveIndexPath`, the CLI surgical-read dedup key. Both now switch to `path.win32.resolve()` when a Windows-drive-absolute path is detected in either argument, which is a no-op on real Windows (where the two resolvers already agree) and correct on any other host. Guarded against regressing silently on a Windows dev machine (where the ambient resolver already happens to be win32-native, masking the bug) by asserting on which resolver gets called rather than only the output value, in [tests/project.test.ts](tests/project.test.ts) and [tests/paths.test.ts](tests/paths.test.ts).

### Changed

- **Removed confirmed-dead code paths.** `src/ask.ts`'s `runAsk` (superseded by `graph_commands.ts`'s FTS-based `runAsk`, which the CLI's `ask` command actually uses) and its test file; `hooks_cli.ts`'s `safeRun`/`denormalizeResponse`/`failSoft`/`readStdin`, which had no production callers now that `relay()` dispatches directly (`denormalizeResponse` is left unwired deliberately — it targets an older wire contract that no longer matches `hook_registry.ts`'s current output shape, and wiring it in now would break serialization rather than fix anything); and two dead bridge config functions, `getClaudeCodeHookConfig`/`getCodexHookConfig`. `baseline.ts`'s directory-walking grep now imports the existing `SKIP_DIRS` set instead of hardcoding a second copy. Also corrected two stale doc references: `CLAUDE.arch.md` described a hook-dispatch path (`safeRun`/`denormalizeResponse`) that no longer exists (the real entry point is `relay.ts::relay()`), and a code comment claimed a Gemini tool-name-normalization branch was reachable when no Gemini bridge exists in this build. See `src/ask.ts` (removed), [src/hooks_cli.ts](src/hooks_cli.ts), [src/baseline.ts](src/baseline.ts), and [CLAUDE.arch.md](CLAUDE.arch.md).

- **README corrected against actual current CLI behavior.** `token-goat map --budget` and `symbol --all-projects` don't exist (`map --compact` is the only budget lever, fixed at 2000 tokens, not 300); `bash-output`/`web-output`/`skill-body` don't have a `--full` flag (head(30)+tail(80) elision has no opt-out short of oversizing `--head`/`--tail`; `skill-body` has no slicers at all); `grep` doesn't shell out to `rg` or cache anything (`history` doesn't track "grep patterns" either); and `semantic`/`similar` are full-text search over symbol names and bodies, not embedding-vector similarity — `--mode`, `--max-distance`, `--no-rerank`, and the "downloads a 130 MB embedding model on first call" claim (including in the security/outbound-network section) describe an `embeddings.ts` pipeline that exists but has no caller anywhere in the indexer or CLI. `context-stats` is now documented; it was a real, working, registered command missing from the table.

## [2.5.0] - 2026-06-30

### Added

- **Skill compact lifecycle is now observable and managed end to end.** Six commands the README documented but the CLI never registered are now wired and tested: `skill-compact --all` batch-regenerates every cached skill's compact, skipping ones already fresh and reporting regenerated/skipped/total; `skill-history` lists cached compact versions newest-first; `skill-diff <name>` shows a unified diff between a skill's two most recent cached versions; `skill-section "<name>::<heading>"` extracts one heading from a skill body; `skill-list` gains `compact_stale` (`true`/`false`/`null`), `hit_count`, and `age`/`age_ms`; and `skill-size` prints a per-skill body/compact breakdown. Staleness compares the `<!-- source_sha: ... -->` embedded in each cached compact against the SHA of the current skill body. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/skill_cache.test.ts](tests/skill_cache.test.ts) and [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).
- **`token-goat install` pre-generates skill compacts as its final step.** After installing hooks, install scans the installed skills directory, caches a compact for each `SKILL.md` (stamped with its source SHA), and records the set in `pregen.json` so `doctor --context` can report which skills were added since. Fail-soft: a pre-gen error never fails the install. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts).
- **A reading hook now flags a stale skill compact at read time.** When a `SKILL.md` is read and its cached compact's embedded source SHA no longer matches the file, the pre-read hook emits a one-line `token-goat skill-compact <name>` hint instead of silently serving a stale compact later. Hit counts increment on both skill load and `skill-body` recall. See [src/hooks_read.ts](src/hooks_read.ts) and [src/hooks_skill.ts](src/hooks_skill.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_read.test.ts](tests/hooks_read.test.ts).
- **`token-goat doctor --context` is now wired to report the session's context footprint.** The `--context` flag is registered on the `doctor` command and connected to the existing context-stats path, adding a section that breaks down CLAUDE.md and memory token usage and lists skills added since the last install pre-gen, with the exact command to refresh them. See [src/cli_doctor.ts](src/cli_doctor.ts).

- **Code-graph commands for navigating the symbol index without reading whole files.** `callers`/`call-chain`/`impact`/`scope` resolve a ref to its enclosing symbol via `[lineStart, lineEnd]` containment — `call-chain` walks transitive callers with a cycle guard, `impact` walks forward dependents by hop depth, and `scope` names the symbol whose range contains a given line. `dead` lists zero-ref symbols, excluding entry-point names and private members; `deps` and `arch` build the internal import graph from `extractImports` (`arch` reports hubs, entry points, and import cycles); `types` filters to the type/interface/enum/struct/trait kinds plus the Python `BaseModel`/`TypedDict`/`Protocol`/`@dataclass` heuristic. `similar`, `context-for`, and `ask` retrieve over the FTS symbol index (`searchSymbolsFts`, not the dormant embeddings path) and emit ranked `token-goat read` pointers; `ask` degrades to those pointers when no `TOKEN_GOAT_ASK_BACKEND` is on PATH, so it never hard-fails. `test-for` and `coverage-gaps` map a file's symbols to (or away from) their test-file refs; `blame` resolves a `file::symbol` line range and shells `git blame -L`. Every command is enforced by the README-driven registration guard. See [src/graph_commands.ts](src/graph_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/graph_commands.test.ts](tests/graph_commands.test.ts) and [tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts](tests/command_matrix_e2e.test.ts).

- **Text and file-utility commands.** File bundling and budgeting: `pack` builds an md/xml/text bundle of matched files (`--scan-secrets` exits 2 when it finds a planted credential, `--budget <n>` exits 3 when the estimate exceeds the cap), `tokens` prints a per-file token table, and `budget` estimates total token cost against a context window — all over the existing `pack.ts` collector and token estimator. Log and failure triage: `failures` extracts failing test blocks (pytest/jest/go/cargo) from stdin or a file, `trace` condenses a Python traceback to project frames, `logfold` reuses the `filters.ts` log-noise filters and folds duplicate lines after normalizing timestamps/UUIDs/IPs/hex, `todo` scans TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX/NOTE markers while skipping matches inside string literals, and `lockdeps` summarizes a poetry/uv/pip/npm/Cargo/yarn lockfile. Session and project utilities: `note set/get/unset/list/clear` is a per-project key-value store, `recent` lists files touched in the current session, `hot` aggregates read frequency across persisted session files, and `ignores` reports the active walk-exclusion set. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts) and [src/text_commands.ts](src/text_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/pack_cli.test.ts](tests/pack_cli.test.ts) and [tests/text_commands.test.ts](tests/text_commands.test.ts).

- **Cache, session, and config operations — the final commands, completing the documented surface.** Cache and history: `bash-history` and `web-history` list cached command/fetch outputs newest-first over a new shared `listBlobs` blob-directory scanner, `clean-cache` prunes every cache subdir to the default floor and `prune-cache` evicts by caller-supplied count/age (both reuse the existing `pruneBlobs`), and `cache-audit` scans the Claude settings for patterns that defeat token-goat caching. Session and cost: `resume <session_id>` builds a recovery packet from a persisted session blob (edited files, top-read files, the last bash commands, and `git diff --stat`) capped at ~8000 chars — this implements the previously stubbed `buildResumePacket`; `compact-hint` previews context pressure via `getContextPressure` against the autocompact threshold, `session-summary` reports current/latest session state, `cost` reframes the `runStats` tokens-saved breakdown, and `baseline` emits the project map via `buildProjectMap`. Config, project, doc, and image: `config list/get/set/validate` reads and writes token-goat's own `config.toml` through `loadConfig`/`saveConfig` with dotted-path access, type-coerced sets, and a levenshtein did-you-mean on unknown keys (distinct from the general-purpose `config-get <file> <key>` reader); `project list/exclude/prune` manages the `worker.blocked_roots` exclusion set; `compact-doc <path>` prints the extractive compact via `compactDoc`; and `fetch-image <url>` fetches an image and runs it through the `shrinkImage` pipeline. This empties the README-driven registration guard's PENDING set: every command documented in the README is now registered, and the guard fails CI the instant the two diverge again. See [src/cache_session_commands.ts](src/cache_session_commands.ts), [src/config_commands.ts](src/config_commands.ts), [src/disk_cache.ts](src/disk_cache.ts), and [src/resume.ts](src/resume.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts](tests/cache_session_commands.test.ts) and [tests/config_commands.test.ts](tests/config_commands.test.ts).

- **`--max-matches <n>` bounds `--grep` output on `token-goat bash-output` and `web-output`.** `--grep` alone filters lines with no upper bound, so a broad pattern over a large cached output still floods the context the recall was meant to spare. `--max-matches 20` caps the result to the first 20 matching lines and appends a one-line notice naming the total match count, so the recall stays cheap and the caller knows to raise the cap when they need more. Opt-in and only active alongside `--grep`. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).

- **`token-goat bash-output --file <path> --transcript` reads a subagent `.output` JSONL transcript as plain assistant text.** A `local_agent` task output file is a JSONL conversation transcript, so reading it raw drips thinking blocks, tool-use payloads, and user records into the context the recall was meant to spare. `--transcript` parses the file line by line, keeps only `type:"assistant"` records, and joins their `text` content blocks (or a plain-string `content`) in order, discarding thinking/tool_use/tool_result blocks and malformed lines; `--grep`/`--head`/`--tail`/`--max-matches` then compose over the extracted text. Returns nothing on a non-transcript file, so the flag is harmless when misapplied. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts) and [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts) and [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).

- **Read-only `gh api` GET responses are cached for recall.** A repeated identical `gh api` GET (same endpoint and flags, ignoring output pipes/redirects) now gets a `token-goat bash-output <id>` recall hint instead of re-fetching, mirroring the existing curl-GET recall. Caching is gated to read-only calls: a mutating `gh api` (`-X POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`, or the `-f`/`-F`/`--field`/`--raw-field`/`--input` field flags that make gh default to POST), the `graphql` endpoint, and any call carrying an `Authorization` header are never cached — the last avoids persisting a credential into the on-disk cache. Error and permission bodies stay out of the cache via the shared 512-byte floor and an exit-0 gate. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **`git push` and read-only `gh pr`/`gh issue` views are cached for recall.** Their output was never cached because none matched a monitoring pattern: `git push` output is dominated by the pre-push hook (the full test suite, often 10K+ chars), and `gh pr view`/`gh pr list`/`gh issue view` are read-only queries run repeatedly. All four are now in `MONITORING_COMMAND_PATTERNS`, so a repeated identical call gets a `token-goat bash-output <id> --grep` recall hint instead of re-running, keyed on the base command (ignoring output pipes/redirects). Over-matching is guarded: `git pushd` is not cached. See [src/hints/lang_patterns.ts](src/hints/lang_patterns.ts) and [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/monitoring_patterns.test.ts](tests/monitoring_patterns.test.ts).
- **The first read-only `gh pr view`/`gh issue view` of a session now gets a one-time field-batching advisory.** When the model inspects a PR or issue field-by-field (`gh pr view 37836 --json title`, then `--json body`, then `--json labels`...), each call is a separate round-trip the model pays for. After the first successful un-batched view this session, the post-bash hook emits a one-time context note naming a concrete batched command (`gh pr view 37836 --json number,title,state,body,labels,reviews,files`, sliceable with `--jq`) so the remaining fields come back in one call. The advisory is suppressed when the view already batches a multi-field `--json a,b` list (the model is doing the right thing), fires at most once per session via the persisted hint-shown set, and caches the view output inline so a later identical view still recalls. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **`skill-compact --path <file>` and an optional skill name.** `token-goat skill-compact --path ~/.claude/skills/ollama/SKILL.md` caches a skill straight from a file, bypassing name resolution; the cache name is the explicit argument when given, else the file's parent directory name. The command is now `skill-compact [name]` (name optional when `--path` is supplied). See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).

- **`skill-list --json` now includes a `skill_name` field** carrying each skill's invocation name explicitly, so consumers don't have to infer it. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).

### Changed

- **`token-goat refs` accepts a comma-separated spec for a merged multi-symbol view.** Looking up the references of several symbols meant running `refs` once per symbol or falling back to a raw `rg "a|b|c"` that loses the index's caller grouping. `refs "a,b,c"` (bare symbols) or `refs "file::a,b"` (file-scoped) now queries each symbol and prints its references under its own header in a single call; `--json` returns a `{symbol: refs[]}` map and `--callers` groups each symbol's hits by enclosing caller. A comma-free spec keeps the original single-symbol output verbatim, and a multi-spec with no hits for any symbol exits 1. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **`sed -n 'N,Mp' file` line-range reads now point at `token-goat read "file@N-M"`.** The pre-bash hook already detected this form but emitted a generic `token-goat section "<file>::Heading"` hint: the wrong tool for a numeric range (sections are heading-addressed), carrying placeholder values the user had to fill in. It now extracts the real path and line numbers and names the exact `read "file@N-M"` command, the line-range syntax added in 2.4.0. Single-address `sed -n '5p'`, piped `sed`, and temp-path reads are left untouched. The hint is also tailored to the file's language: Markdown points at `token-goat section "file::heading"`, structured config (TOML/JSON/YAML/INI) at `token-goat config-get`, and source code at a `token-goat symbol`/`read "file::Symbol"` read that survives line shifts, keeping the numeric range as the fallback. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **Repeated `sed -n 'N,Mp'` reads that overlap a range already served this session now get an overlap-aware recall hint.** token-goat records each served line range per file in session state (persisted across hook processes via the session store, then unioned and capped on merge), and when a later `sed` range overlaps an earlier one it names the prior range and points at a `token-goat read "file@<delta>"` that fetches only the not-yet-seen lines, instead of re-emitting the generic line-range hint. This closes the sliding-window duplication where paging through a file re-served the overlapping lines at each step. See [src/session.ts](src/session.ts), [src/session_store.ts](src/session_store.ts), and [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/session_store.test.ts](tests/session_store.test.ts) and [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **`token-goat section` now resolves an unambiguous heading prefix instead of failing.** A lookup that misses exact and normalized matching but is a prefix of exactly one heading (e.g. `section "f::Business"` against a lone `Business / logic`, or `::postMessage` against `postMessage abuse & Service Worker persistence`) auto-redirects to that heading, annotated with a `(redirected from: '<query>')` marker in plain output and a `redirectedFrom` field under `--json`. The strip-normalizer already handled em-dash/parenthetical/numeric subtitles; this covers the slash- and ampersand-separated cases it does not. Ambiguous prefixes (two or more distinct matching headings) and ordinal specs (`::Heading#2`) still miss, so the redirect fires only when it is unambiguous. See [src/section_reader.ts](src/section_reader.ts) and [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/section_reader.test.ts](tests/section_reader.test.ts) and [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

- **`.output` task-transcript reads now route to `bash-output --file <path> --transcript` instead of being read whole.** Two read paths that touch a subagent/task `.output` JSONL transcript now point at the transcript-recall mode added this release. `extractPythonFileRead` gained a `.output` branch: `python open(r"…/tasks/<id>.output")` was silently passing through (the extension was absent from the source/doc whitelist) while the model hand-parsed the JSONL; it now emits a hint naming `token-goat bash-output --file "<path>" --transcript`. The existing `cat`/`tail` task-output hint, which previously suggested only `--tail N`, now leads with `--transcript` since these files are transcripts. Write-intent `open(path, "w")` and orchestrator state files are still excluded. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).
- **Stale `bash-output`/`web-output` IDs now return a recovery path, not a dead end.** `no cached bash output for id: X` adds that a background-task id can be recalled directly with `token-goat bash-output --file <path-to-output-file>`, and the web variant notes the cache may have expired and a re-fetch repopulates it. The bare id-not-found message left the caller with no next step. See [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).
- **Re-loading a skill already loaded this session is denied with a compact-recall pointer.** Once a skill body is cached this session (the post-Skill hook persists it), a second `/skill` invocation re-injects the entire body — the exact waste the cache exists to prevent. The pre-Skill hook now detects a same-session prior load by matching the session's output-id prefix against the cached metas and denies the re-load with a `token-goat skill-body <name> --compact` hint (or the full-body recall), so the model recalls the slice it needs instead of paying for the whole skill again. The detection is conservative: cross-session dedup can suppress a same-session meta, so a miss never fires a false advisory, and the first (cold) load always passes. See [src/hooks_skill.ts](src/hooks_skill.ts) and [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_skill.test.ts](tests/hooks_skill.test.ts).
- **`Get-Content` wrapped in a `powershell -Command`/`pwsh -c` invocation now gets the same read-hint as a bare `Get-Content`.** On Windows the model routinely reads a file with `powershell -Command "Get-Content 'src/auth.ts' -Raw"`, which bare `extractCatFile` rejected (its regex demands end-of-string right after the path, so a trailing `-Raw`/`-Encoding` slipped through) and the whole file then loaded into context unhinted. A new `extractPowerShellWrappedGetContent` unwraps the inner `Get-Content`/`gc`/`cat`/`type` from the quoted `-Command`/`-c`/`-EncodedCommand` payload, tolerates leading and trailing flags, classifies the path (source/doc/config/sql/env), and emits the matching surgical-read pointer (`token-goat read "file::Symbol"`, `section`, or `config-get`). Temp-path reads are size-gated: a small scratch read stays silent, but one >=16 KB still floods context and gets the hint. Unknown extensions with no surgical-read alternative (e.g. a `.b64` blob) are left untouched. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

### Fixed

- **Skills loaded via the Skill tool are now cached, and `skill-compact`/`skill-body`/`skill-list` resolve installed skills from disk.** Loading a skill (e.g. `/ollama`) then running `token-goat skill-compact ollama` returned `skill 'ollama' not found`, and `skill-list` never showed it. Two defects combined: the Skill post-tool hook extracted the skill name and body but never persisted them (`postSkillHandler` was a no-op stub with zero production callers, masked by tests that only inspected the event object), and `getSkillFilePath` resolved names only from cached metas with no on-disk fallback, so an installed-but-not-yet-loaded skill was unreachable. The hook now stores the loaded body under the real skill name (`toolInput.skill`), and `getSkillFilePath` falls back to `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. `skill-compact` also writes the body meta (not just the compact slice), so a skill compacted straight from disk is listable and recallable like one loaded via the hook. See [src/hooks_skill.ts](src/hooks_skill.ts), [src/skill_cache.ts](src/skill_cache.ts), and [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_skill.test.ts](tests/hooks_skill.test.ts), [tests/skill_cache.test.ts](tests/skill_cache.test.ts), and [tests/cli.test.ts](tests/cli.test.ts).

- **Read-only MCP tool results are now cached across hook processes and recalled instead of re-fetched.** `mcp_cache.ts` shipped with a fatal defect: it stored results only in an in-memory map and was imported by no hook, so — because each hook invocation is a fresh process — it could never produce a cross-process hit, and in fact never ran at all. The module is rewritten to persist results into the shared bash-output blob store (the one proven cross-process path) under a deterministic, session-scoped `mcp_<hash>` id, and a new `hooks_mcp.ts` is wired into the relay: `post_tool_use` stores a read-only `mcp__*` result, and an identical later `pre_tool_use` call is denied with a `token-goat bash-output <id>` recall hint (sliceable with `--grep`/`--tail`/`--head`) instead of repeating the round trip. Caching is gated to read-only tools (a mutating verb in the tool's method segment is never cached), skips results above 2 MB, and is scoped per session. The dead in-memory persistence, its JSON sidecar metadata, and the unused byte-budget constant are removed. See [src/mcp_cache.ts](src/mcp_cache.ts), [src/hooks_mcp.ts](src/hooks_mcp.ts), and [src/relay.ts](src/relay.ts); regression-tested in [tests/mcp_cache.test.ts](tests/mcp_cache.test.ts) and [tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts](tests/hooks_mcp.test.ts).

## [2.4.0] - 2026-06-29

### Added

- **Line-range reads in `token-goat read` (`file@N-M`).** `read "file.ts@10-40"` returns lines 10 to 40 inclusive, and `read "file.ts@42"` returns a single line. Ranges read straight from disk with no index lookup, so they work on any file, including paths outside every indexed project (whole-file `read` already allowed those, but the line-range syntax from the Python build had not been ported). An end past EOF clamps to the last line; an inverted range or a start below 1 is a clear error. See [src/read_commands.ts](src/read_commands.ts); regression-tested in [tests/read_commands.test.ts](tests/read_commands.test.ts).

## [2.3.0] - 2026-06-29

### Fixed

- **Whole-file-read hints now cover `bat`, `type`, and PowerShell `Get-Content`/`gc`, as documented.** The hint that steers `cat <file>` toward a surgical read advertised coverage of `bat`, `type`, and PowerShell `Get-Content`/`gc`, but the matcher was anchored to `cat` alone, so those four commands silently got no hint. The leading-command match now covers all five and names the actual command in the hint. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **`upsertChunks` and `searchSemantic` tolerate a missing `chunk_vectors` table.** The sqlite-vec `chunk_vectors` virtual table is an independent optional dependency, but both functions gated only on `isAvailable()` (the `@xenova/transformers` model, a separate hard dependency), so on a vec-absent install they threw `no such table: chunk_vectors`. Both now reuse the existing `chunkVectorsTableExists` gate that `deleteFileEmbeddings` already uses: `upsertChunks` skips entirely (chunk rows have no independent reader, so this also avoids the embed cost) and `searchSemantic` returns no hits. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/embeddings_novec_upsert_search.test.ts](tests/embeddings_novec_upsert_search.test.ts).

- **C# `namespace` declarations are indexed with kind `namespace`, not `const`.** `extractCsharp` pushed every namespace symbol with kind `const`, mislabeling a namespace as a constant in `symbol`, `outline`, and `skeleton` output and in any kind-based grouping. The single namespace emit now uses kind `namespace` (matching the php adapter); real C# `const` fields are unchanged. See [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **Makefile `::=` and `:::=` assignments are no longer mis-indexed as targets.** `TARGET_RE` excluded `:=` assignments but not the immediate-expansion operators `::=`/`:::=` (POSIX and GNU make 4.4+): on `VAR ::= value` the one-or-two-colon match consumed one colon and the trailing lookahead absorbed the second colon, hiding the `=`, so `VAR` was emitted as a phantom `makefile_target`. A `(?![:=])` guard after the colon run now rejects `:=`, `::=`, and `:::=` while still matching real `:` and `::` (double-colon) rules. See [src/languages/makefile_idx.ts](src/languages/makefile_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **PHP code and braces that share a line with a block comment are now parsed.** `extractPhp` skipped the whole line whenever it contained `*/` (`inComment = false; continue`), so a closing `}` on a `} /* closes Foo */` line was never counted - leaving the class context un-popped and mis-parenting the next top-level `function`/`class` as a method of that class - and a declaration sharing a line with a comment (`class Bar { /* note */ }`) was dropped entirely. The line-granular skip is replaced with a stateful span stripper that removes only the `/* ... */` spans (carried across lines) and parses the residual code, so braces and declarations sharing a line with a comment are seen and a brace inside a comment is not counted. Parsing such lines for the first time also surfaced a scope-push bug: a one-line class (`class Bar { }`, open and close on the same line) was pushed with an entry depth one below the surrounding scope and never popped, mis-parenting the next declaration as its method; the threshold is corrected to the brace depth before the line (a no-op for multiline classes). See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **Top-level Kotlin `const val`/`val` declarations are now indexed.** The Kotlin adapter advertises that it extracts SCREAMING_SNAKE const vals, but `CONST_RE` was anchored `^\s+` (leading whitespace required) and the top-level branch only ran the function regex, so a file-scope `const val MAX_SIZE = 100` or `val GREETING = "hi"` was never emitted - only in-class consts were. The anchor is relaxed to `^\s*` and the top-level branch now also runs `CONST_RE`, so column-0 SCREAMING_SNAKE consts are indexed; in-class consts and the exclusion of non-SCREAMING_SNAKE vals are unchanged. See [src/languages/kotlin.ts](src/languages/kotlin.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **C# methods declared with no access modifier are now indexed.** `METHOD_RE` in the C# adapter required one or more modifiers, so an implicitly-private helper (`int Add(int a, int b)`) or a method with only a return type (`void Run()`) matched nothing and was silently dropped from `symbol` search, `outline`, and `skeleton`. The modifier group is now zero-or-more, fronted by a negative-lookahead that rejects statement-starting keywords (`return`, `throw`, `await`, control-flow) in the return-type slot so the relaxed pattern cannot mistake a statement for a method; `new`-modified methods are unaffected and method detection still runs only at one brace level inside a class body. See [src/languages/csharp.ts](src/languages/csharp.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **Rust function-local `const` declarations are no longer indexed as top-level symbols.** `extractRustSymbols` walked the AST with no scope tracking, so a `const` declared inside a function body or a closure was emitted as a package-level symbol, polluting global `symbol` search, `outline`, and `skeleton`. The walk now threads an `insideFunction` flag and skips `const_item` inside any function or closure scope, mirroring the TS/JS extractor, which excludes local value bindings while still indexing nested items. Nested structs, enums, functions, traits, impls, types, and associated `const`s inside `impl` blocks remain indexed. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts).

- **`.env` keys written with a leading `export ` are now indexed.** The dotenv/envrc key pattern was anchored so that `export FOO=bar` captured the literal `export` and then failed to find the `=`, dropping the key entirely - a common shape in shell-sourced `.env` and direnv `.envrc` files. The pattern now consumes an optional leading `export ` so the captured symbol is the variable name; a variable literally named `export` is unaffected. See [src/languages/ini_idx.ts](src/languages/ini_idx.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **Go function-local declarations are no longer indexed as top-level symbols.** `extractGoSymbols` walked the AST with no scope tracking, so a `var`/`const`/`type` declared inside a function body (or a closure) was emitted as a package-level symbol, polluting global `symbol` search, `outline`, and `skeleton` - the opposite of the TS/JS and Python extractors, which deliberately exclude locals. The walk now threads an `insideFunction` flag and skips those declaration kinds inside any function/method/closure scope, while package-level declarations, functions, and methods are unchanged. See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts); regression-tested in [tests/parser.test.ts](tests/parser.test.ts).

- **PHP parser no longer mis-parents top-level declarations that follow a class.** In `extractPhp` the class-scope stack was popped using a brace depth that had this line’s opening braces added but its closing braces not yet subtracted, so a class’s closing `}` never popped its context. Every top-level `function` or `class` after the first class in a file was then attributed to that class (a function came back as a `method` of it, a second class got it as a parent). The net brace delta is now applied before the pop check, matching the [Kotlin](src/languages/kotlin.ts) and [C#](src/languages/csharp.ts) adapters. See [src/languages/php.ts](src/languages/php.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **Pruning and reindexing no longer break on platforms without the sqlite-vec binary.** `chunk_vectors` (the vec0 table) is created only when sqlite-vec loads, but `deleteFileEmbeddings` referenced it unconditionally, so on any install lacking the prebuilt binary every prune and reindex threw `no such table: chunk_vectors` - and because that delete ran first, the chunk-row delete never ran and the rows leaked. The vector delete is now guarded by a `sqlite_master` existence check; the chunks delete always runs. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested in [tests/embeddings_novec_delete.test.ts](tests/embeddings_novec_delete.test.ts).

- **`deleteFileEmbeddings` no longer overflows SQLites bound-parameter limit on very large files.** It expanded `DELETE FROM chunk_vectors WHERE rowid IN (?, ?, ...)` to one bound parameter per chunk, so deleting or reindexing a file with more than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (32766) chunks - a large generated or minified file - threw `SqliteError: too many SQL variables`. It now deletes via a correlated subquery (`WHERE rowid IN (SELECT id FROM chunks WHERE ...)`) that binds zero id parameters, preserving the case-folding path match and the vectors-before-chunks delete order. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts); regression-tested with a 32767-chunk delete in [tests/embeddings_var_limit.test.ts](tests/embeddings_var_limit.test.ts).

- **Semantic search now actually functions: declared the missing `sqlite-vec` dependency and fixed the `vec0` rowid bind.** `sqlite-vec` (the native extension providing the `vec0` virtual table that stores 384-dim embedding vectors) is loaded at runtime in [src/db.ts](src/db.ts) and marked `external` in the bundle, but was never declared in any `package.json` section, so a clean install never had it, `vec0` never loaded, and `token-goat semantic` silently returned nothing. It is now in `optionalDependencies` alongside `@xenova/transformers`. This surfaced a second bug the missing dependency had masked: [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts) bound the chunk rowid into `chunk_vectors` as a plain JS number, but `vec0` declares `rowid` as a strict `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` and rejects a number-bound value ("Only integers are allowed for primary key values"), so the first vector insert threw and the whole `upsertChunks` transaction rolled back. The insert is now centralized in an exported `insertChunkVector` helper that coerces the rowid to `BigInt`, regression-tested against a real `vec0` table in [tests/embeddings_vec_insert.test.ts](tests/embeddings_vec_insert.test.ts).

- **Regression guards so the dead-semantic-search class cannot silently return.** Added [tests/guards/semantic_deps.test.ts](tests/guards/semantic_deps.test.ts), which derives every optional native package the runtime loads via `_require('<pkg>')` (outside the tree-sitter grammars already covered by `grammar_deps`) from the `src` sources and asserts each is declared in `package.json`, so it fails the instant `sqlite-vec` or any future optional native dependency is required but undeclared. Strengthened [tests/embeddings_vec_insert.test.ts](tests/embeddings_vec_insert.test.ts) to classify `sqlite-vec` as working/broken/absent so an installed-but-non-loading `vec0` fails loudly instead of skipping to green, and to run the production `MATCH`/`k` KNN query after inserting, proving the stored vector is actually retrievable rather than just stored.

- **TS/JS destructuring declarations now index each bound identifier individually.** Previously, `const { alpha, beta } = obj` and `const [first, second] = arr` emitted a single unresolvable symbol named after the whole pattern (`"{ alpha, beta }"` or `"[first, second]"`), making it impossible for `token-goat symbol alpha` to find the binding and polluting the symbols table. The fix adds a `collectPatternBindings()` helper that walks destructuring pattern nodes recursively, extracting the actual bound identifiers (`alpha`, `beta`, `first`, `second`), and emits one variable symbol per binding instead. Renamed bindings (`const { a: b } = obj`) now correctly bind `b` (the value), not `a` (the key). See [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts).

- **chunkFile endLine off-by-one on newline-terminated files.** The `split(/\r?\n/)` method yields a phantom trailing empty string when splitting newline-terminated content (e.g., `"a\nb\n".split(/\r?\n/)` → `["a","b",""]`). This inflated the final chunk's `endLine` by one and appended a stray newline. The fix mirrors Python's `splitlines()` behavior by popping a single trailing empty element if present, ensuring `endLine` reflects the file's actual line count. See [src/embeddings.ts](src/embeddings.ts).

- **drainOnce lost-update race in the dirty queue.** The drain loop in [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts) was vulnerable to a lost-update race: a file appended to the queue by `appendDirtyPath` (from a concurrent hook) between the queue snapshot and the whole-file delete would be dropped without being indexed. The fix ports the Python original's atomic rename-to-claim pattern: the drain atomically renames the live `dirty.txt` to `dirty.txt.draining` so concurrent appends either land before the rename (and travel with it) or recreate a fresh queue after it (next poll). Also adds crash recovery: if a drain process crashes, the next drain absorbs the abandoned `.draining` file and indexes its contents. Windows rename contention (EPERM/EBUSY when the file is open for append) is handled via a retry loop with 50ms sleeps. Two regression tests verify the fix: "does not drop paths appended during a drain" and "recovers from abandoned .draining file".

- **Surgical-read path lookups now match case-insensitively on Windows/macOS.** On case-insensitive filesystems, `token-goat symbol`/`read`/`refs` silently missed when the queried path's casing differed from the stored on-disk casing. Root cause: `normalizePath` lowercases only the drive letter — the rest keeps the user-typed casing — while indexed `file_path` keeps the on-disk casing; SQL queries used case-sensitive `file_path = ?` comparisons, so `read "src/Worker.ts"` missed a row stored as `src/worker.ts` and fell back to a full Read (the exact waste token-goat exists to prevent). The fix adds a shared `isCaseInsensitiveFs()` / `foldPath()` helper pair to [src/util.ts](src/util.ts), consolidates two existing case-folding duplicates in [src/walk_index.ts](src/walk_index.ts) and [src/worker.ts](src/worker.ts), and applies case-insensitive SQL matching to the three affected query paths in [src/index_reader.ts](src/index_reader.ts) via a `pathEq()` predicate builder (`COLLATE NOCASE` on case-insensitive filesystems, plain `= ?` on case-sensitive). Regression tests verify case-folding queries match across casing and case-sensitive queries still distinguish (set via `TOKEN_GOAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_FS` for deterministic cross-platform testing).

### Added

- **PowerShell symbol indexing (`.ps1`/`.psm1`).** A new regex adapter extracts top-level `function`/`filter`, `class`/`enum`, and class methods so `symbol`, `read`, `skeleton`, and `outline` work on PowerShell scripts. Methods are scoped to one brace level inside the class body and guarded against control-flow keywords (`if`/`foreach`/…) so statement lines in a method body are never mis-extracted as methods; `<# #>` block comments and `#` line comments are skipped. See [src/languages/powershell_idx.ts](src/languages/powershell_idx.ts), wired through [src/parser.ts](src/parser.ts) and [src/parser_types.ts](src/parser_types.ts); regression-tested in [tests/languages.test.ts](tests/languages.test.ts).

- **PowerShell `Get-Content -Tail N` and `… | Select-Object -First N` read-slice hints.** `Get-Content <path> -Tail N` (either flag order) now suggests a surgical read the way `tail -n N` does, and `Get-Content <path> | Select-Object -First N` suggests `skeleton`/`read`/`config-get` the way `head -N` does. Already-surgical slices (`-Tail` ≤ 10, `-First` < 10) pass through untouched. See [src/hooks_bash.ts](src/hooks_bash.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_bash.test.ts](tests/hooks_bash.test.ts).

- **WebFetch responses are recalled instead of re-fetched.** `postFetchHandler` already cached WebFetch bodies cross-process, but `preFetchHandler` never surfaced them, so the cache was write-only and a second fetch of the same URL silently hit the network again. `preFetchHandler` now emits a non-blocking hint pointing at `token-goat web-output <id>` (mirroring the curl-GET recall hint) when the URL was fetched earlier this session and the cached body is still present. See [src/hooks_fetch.ts](src/hooks_fetch.ts); regression-tested in [tests/hooks_fetch_persistence.test.ts](tests/hooks_fetch_persistence.test.ts) and [tests/session_persistence_e2e.test.ts](tests/session_persistence_e2e.test.ts).

- **Bash-output compression: 17 language-runtime and compiler filters (batch K1).** The K1 language filter family is ported from Python to TypeScript and registered in `TOOL_FILTERS` as `LANGUAGE_FILTERS` ([src/tool_filters/languages.ts](src/tool_filters/languages.ts)). All 17 filters share `errorPassthrough = true` so stderr is preserved when a command fails. Filters: `NodeFilter` (`node -e`/`--eval`/`-p`/`--print`; collapses node_modules and node:internal stack frames; token-capped at 1 000 on failure); `PythonFilter` (`python`/`python3`; traceback compression with first-2+last-3 frame trimming for deep traces; consecutive repeated-line dedup; warning-class dedup capped at 3 per category); `RubyFilter` (`ruby -e`/`-r`; backtrace compression, gem-install progress drop); `BunFilter` (`bun test`/`build`/`run`; registered _before_ `NodePackageFilter` which also claims `bun`; download-line collapse, test-result keep, error-section preserve); `DenoFilter` (`deno run`/`test`/`compile`; bundle/compile progress drop; error-chunk preserve); `FlutterFilter` (`flutter build`/`run`/`test`; verbose framework frames collapse); `DartFilter` (`dart run`/`test`/`compile`; stack-trace head+tail with omission marker); `SwiftFilter` (`swift build`/`run`/`test`/`package`; linker/linking-progress collapse; compiler warning dedup); `XcodeFilter` (`xcodebuild`; per-phase collapsing of compile/link/copy lines); `MixFilter` (`mix`/`elixir`; compilation-warning dedup; test-suite summary keep); `ZigFilter` (`zig build`/`run`/`test`; note-line accumulation, error-chunk extraction); `RCmdFilter` (`R`/`Rscript`; message/warning line dedup; loading-package progress drop); factory-built via `makeLanguageFilter`: `erlangFilter` (`erl`/`escript`/`rebar3`; crash-dump drop, error-chunk keep), `crystalFilter` (`crystal`; compile-error keep, progress drop), `haskellFilter` (`ghc`/`stack`/`cabal`; warning/note dedup, linking-progress collapse), `elmFilter` (`elm`; compile-error keep, dependency-fetch drop), `juliaFilter` (`julia`; precompile-progress drop, deprecation dedup), `powerShellFilter` (`pwsh`/`powershell`; error/warning dedup, progress-bar drop).

- **Bash-output compression: 18 db/runner/utility filters (batch K2) — completes the 158-filter port.** The final filter family is ported from Python to TypeScript in `misc.ts` and registered in `TOOL_FILTERS` after `LANGUAGE_FILTERS` ([src/tool_filters/misc.ts](src/tool_filters/misc.ts)). Two filters (`PlaywrightFilter`, `CypressFilter`) are registered individually before `bunFilter` in dispatch to avoid being shadowed by `BunFilter`'s `bunx` claim. The remaining 16 form `MISC_FILTERS`. Four filters have `errorPassthrough = true` (`ToxFilter`, `NoxFilter`, `NgFilter`, `WasmPackFilter`). `SeverityLogFilter.matches()` and `TailTruncFilter.matches()` both return `false` (content-based and explicit-opt-in respectively). DB clients: `PsqlFilter` (`psql`; migration vs SELECT routing; >20-row collapse); `MySQLFilter` (`mysql`/`mysqldump`; binary-name routing; query table state machine; dump first-3-CREATE-TABLE keep); `Sqlite3Filter` (`sqlite3`; DDL passthrough when ≥50% of lines are schema; else row collapse); `RedisCLIFilter` (`redis-cli`; SCAN cursor detection, bulk-OK collapse, long-list collapse). Build/runner: `SysPackageFilter` (`apt-get`/`apt`/`apk`/`brew`; per-manager progress collapse); `ProtocFilter` (`protoc`/`buf`; `[libprotobuf INFO]` drop, WARNING keep, identical-line dedup); `SassFilter` (`sass`/`node-sass`/`lessc`; first-5 write lines sample, deprecation dedup by 60-char prefix); `ToxFilter` (`tox`; env-create/pip noise collapse); `NoxFilter` (`nox`; venv-create/reuse/pip noise collapse); `WasmPackFilter` (`wasm-pack`; `[INFO]` and Cargo compile drop); `NgFilter` (`ng`; test → Karma noise drop, build → webpack chunk table head+tail); `PlaywrightFilter` (`playwright`/`npx playwright`/`bunx playwright`; pass-line and download-progress drop); `CypressFilter` (`cypress`/`npx cypress`/`bunx cypress`; 5-state section suppressor). Generic/catch-all: `DotenvFilter` (`dotenv`; ≥2 banner lines → count note); `EnvFilter` (`env`/`printenv`; ≤20 vars passthrough, else low-priority var suppression); `JsonArrayFilter` (content-based; key-set dedup of objects preserving high-entropy values; 50-item cap); `SeverityLogFilter` (content-based; WARN+ kept + 2-line context, stack-trace continuations); `TailTruncFilter` (opt-in only; first 50 + marker + last 50 when >500 lines). 108 golden tests in [tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts](tests/tool_filters_misc.test.ts); e2e smoke (psql + playwright) in [tests/bash_compress_rewrite.test.ts](tests/bash_compress_rewrite.test.ts).

- **Bash-output compression: 20 shell/file-utility filters (batch J).** The complete Python shell/file filter family is now ported to TypeScript and registered in `TOOL_FILTERS` as `SHELL_FILE_FILTERS` ([src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts](src/tool_filters/shell_file.ts)). Dispatch ordering within `SHELL_FILE_FILTERS`: `RgFilter` precedes `GrepFilter` (RgFilter claims both `rg` and `grep`; GrepFilter is the simpler fallback); `LsFilter` precedes `EzaFilter` (LsFilter claims `ls`/`eza`/`exa`; EzaFilter is reached via `exa` only).
